catalog.name: 389ds-access
catalog.product: 389 Directory Server / Red Hat Directory Server access log
catalog.sample_line: [27/Apr/2015:13:16:35 -0400] conn=324375 op=606903 SRCH base="cn=users,cn=accounts,dc=example,dc=com" scope=2 filter="(uid=root)" attrs=ALL
catalog.detect_signature: [DD/Mon/YYYY:HH:MM:SS(.ns) zone] conn=<n|Internal(n)> op=<n> then verb; RESULT err=<n> tag=<n> nentries=<n> etime=<f>
catalog.fields: timestamp(+ns on 1.4+), conn, op, fd, slot, verb, base/dn, scope, filter, err, tag, nentries, etime, notes=A/P/U
catalog.notes: Distinct from OpenLDAP: bracketed Apache-style timestamp, no syslog wrapper. Internal ops use conn=Internal(0) op=0(0)(0). Docs: port389.org + insights-core dirsrv_logs

catalog.name: ARM Trusted Firmware-A (TF-A) log
catalog.sample_line:
NOTICE:  BL1: Booting BL2
INFO:    Loading image id=1 at address 0x4001000
NOTICE:  BL31: v2.11(release):v2.11
ERROR:   Error initializing runtime service
catalog.detect_signature: Fixed-width level prefix + colon + spaces: 'NOTICE: ','INFO:    ','WARNING: ','ERROR:   ','VERBOSE: '; boot-stage tokens 'BL1:'/'BL2:'/'BL31:'/'BL32:'.
catalog.fields: level, stage(BLx), message, image_id, address
catalog.notes: LOG_LEVEL compile-time gated. Version banner 'BL31: v<x>(release/debug):<commit>'.

catalog.name: Bazel Build Event Protocol (JSON)
catalog.sample_line: {"id":{"targetCompleted":{"label":"//src:app","configuration":{"id":"abc"}}},"completed":{"success":true,"outputGroup":[{"name":"default","fileSets":[{"id":"1"}]}]}}
catalog.detect_signature: NDJSON where each object has "id" (a BuildEventId oneof: started/progress/targetConfigured/targetCompleted/testResult/namedSetOfFiles/buildFinished) and a payload key matching. Files via NamedSetOfFiles reference.
catalog.fields: id(oneof), children[], payload(started/progress/completed/testResult/finished)
catalog.notes: Also emitted as protobuf (--build_event_binary_file) and text. NamedSetOfFiles indirection for file paths.

catalog.name: Cargo human build output
catalog.sample_line:
Compiling serde v1.0.195
   Compiling my_app v0.1.0 (/home/u/my_app)
warning: unused variable: `x`
  --> src/main.rs:4:9
    Finished dev [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3.42s
catalog.detect_signature: Right-aligned status verbs 'Compiling'/'Finished'/'Building'/'Downloaded'/'Updating'/'Running'; 'warning:'/'error[E####]:' with ' --> file:line:col' pointer lines and '|' code frames.
catalog.fields: status_verb, crate, version, path, diagnostic_level, error_code, file:line:col
catalog.notes: rustc diagnostics embedded. Profile 'dev [unoptimized + debuginfo]' vs 'release [optimized]'.

catalog.name: Chrome Trace Event Format (JSON array/object)
catalog.sample_line: {"pid":1,"tid":2,"ts":0,"ph":"X","name":"Foo","dur":50,"cat":"work","args":{}}
catalog.detect_signature: Either a bare JSON array of event objects, or `{"traceEvents":[...]}`; each event has `ph` (single-char phase) + `ts` + `pid` + `tid`
catalog.fields: ph (B/E/X/i/C/b/e/n/M/s/t/f/...), ts(us), dur(us for X), pid, tid, name, cat, args, id (async), s(scope)
catalog.notes: Phases: X=complete, B/E=begin/end, i=instant, C=counter, b/e/n=async, M=metadata, s/t/f=flow. Also supports systemTraceEvents, metadata keys. Widely used JIT/engine profile export (V8, Perfetto ingests it).

catalog.name: Datadog APM trace payload
catalog.sample_line: [[{"trace_id":1234567890,"span_id":987,"parent_id":0,"name":"web.request","resource":"GET /","service":"cart","start":1716124800000000000,"duration":1200000,"meta":{"http.method":"GET"},"metrics":{}}]]
catalog.detect_signature: Array-of-arrays of spans; span has numeric `trace_id`/`span_id`/`parent_id`, `resource`, `service`, `start`(ns), `duration`(ns), `meta`/`metrics` maps
catalog.fields: trace_id(uint64), span_id, parent_id, name, resource, service, type, start(ns epoch), duration(ns), error, meta{str}, metrics{num}
catalog.notes: PUT /v0.4/traces as msgpack on the wire (JSON-equivalent shape). Grouped by trace into outer array. dd-trace-agent logs are separate plaintext.

catalog.name: Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP)
catalog.sample_line: Content-Length: 82\r\n\r\n{"seq":153,"type":"request","command":"next","arguments":{"threadId":3}}
catalog.detect_signature: 'Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n' framing then JSON with "seq"+"type" (request/response/event); requests have "command"+"arguments", responses "request_seq"+"success"+"body", events "event"+"body". Events: stopped/output/terminated/initialized.
catalog.fields: seq, type, command, request_seq, success, event, body, arguments
catalog.notes: Same HTTP-like framing as LSP but keyed on seq/type rather than jsonrpc/id. 'output' event carries debuggee stdout.

catalog.name: Deterministic replay seed dump (game)
catalog.sample_line: [Replay] Recording started seed=0xDEADBEEF tick=0 build=1.4.2
catalog.detect_signature: Tokens 'seed=' (hex or dec) with 'tick'/'frame'/'replay'/'checksum'/'desync'; often per-frame checksum lines
catalog.fields: seed(hex/dec); tick/frame; build/version; checksum; desync markers
catalog.notes: User named seed dumps explicitly. Lockstep sims log seed at start then per-frame hashes; desync detection logs 'DESYNC at frame N: local=... remote=...'. Format is engine-specific free text keyed on seed/tick/checksum.

catalog.name: EDK2 / UEFI DEBUG serial log
catalog.sample_line:
Loading driver at 0x0007E4C4000 EntryPoint=0x0007E4C8260 PcdDxeIplBuildShareCodeHobs
DEBUG [DXE] InstallProtocolInterface: 5B1B31A1-9562-11D2-8E3F-00A0C969723B 7E4A98
catalog.detect_signature: Lines with EFI phase tags like 'DEBUG [DXE]', 'PROGRESS CODE:', 'InstallProtocolInterface:', 'Loading driver at 0x'; GUIDs in 8-4-4-4-12 form; often over serial (115200 8N1). EFI_D_*/DEBUG_* level prefixes.
catalog.fields: phase(SEC/PEI/DXE/BDS/SMM), level(EFI_D_ERROR/INFO/etc), message, addresses(0x...), GUIDs
catalog.notes: No timestamps by default; free-form printf via DEBUG((level,fmt,...)). Variants: BaseDebugLibSerialPort, UefiDebugLibConOut, StdErr. ASSERT lines: 'ASSERT /path/File.c(123): expr'.

catalog.name: Elastic APM intake NDJSON
catalog.sample_line: {"metadata":{"service":{"name":"cart","agent":{"name":"python"}}}}\n{"transaction":{"id":"abc","trace_id":"...","type":"request","duration":12.3}}\n{"span":{"id":"..","transaction_id":"abc","type":"db","duration":3.1}}
catalog.detect_signature: NDJSON where each line is a single-key object keyed `metadata`|`transaction`|`span`|`error`|`metricset`; first line is always `metadata`
catalog.fields: metadata.service, transaction{id,trace_id,parent_id,type,duration(ms),span_count}, span{id,transaction_id,type,subtype,duration,stacktrace}, error{}
catalog.notes: POST /intake/v2/events (application/x-ndjson). Line-per-event; metadata dictates the rest.

catalog.name: FlameGraph folded (generic)
catalog.sample_line: main;compute;inner_loop 89
catalog.detect_signature: Each line: `frame;frame;...;leaf<space>integer`; no header, no JSON; last space-delimited token is a positive integer count
catalog.fields: semicolon-delimited frame names, single space, numeric sample/weight count
catalog.notes: Lingua franca of profilers — output of stackcollapse-perf/-jstack/-dtrace/-stap/-gdb etc. Optional module suffix `[module]` and `_[k]` kernel annotations.

catalog.name: GDB/MI machine interface
catalog.sample_line:
^done,bkpt={number="1",type="breakpoint",disp="keep",enabled="y",addr="0x08048564"}
*stopped,reason="breakpoint-hit",disp="keep",bkptno="1",thread-id="1"
~"Reading symbols from a.out...\n"
(gdb)
catalog.detect_signature: Records by leading char: '^' result (^done/^running/^error/^exit), '*' exec-async (*stopped/*running), '=' notify-async, '~' console-stream, '@' target-stream, '&' log-stream; optional numeric token prefix; terminator '(gdb)'. Values are name="val" / {tuples} / [lists].
catalog.fields: token, class(^*=~@&), result_class, reason, key=value tuples
catalog.notes: GDB-MI tuple/list grammar (not JSON). '(gdb)\n' terminates each command's output batch.

catalog.name: GIT_TRACE2 event target (JSON)
catalog.detect_signature: One JSON object per line, always has "event" + "sid" + "thread" + "time" + "file" + "line". event enum: version/start/exit/atexit/cmd_name/cmd_mode/child_start/child_exit/region_enter/region_leave/data/error. sid has TZ-timestamp-Hhash-Ppid shape.
catalog.fields: event, sid, thread, time, file, line, plus event-specific (exe, argv, code, t_abs, category, key, value, nesting, repo)
catalog.notes: Enable via GIT_TRACE2_EVENT=<path|fd|1>. sid nests child sessions with '/'. Best structured Git source.

catalog.name: GROMACS md.log
catalog.sample_line:
Step           Time
         100000      200.00000

   Energies (kJ/mol)
          Bond          Angle    ...
catalog.detect_signature: 'Step Time' two-column header followed by energies block header 'Energies (kJ/mol)'; startup 'GROMACS:' banner and 'Log file opened on'; 'Started mdrun'
catalog.fields: Step;Time; then named energy terms (Bond,Angle,LJ-14,Coulomb-14,Potential,Kinetic En.,Total Energy,Temperature,Pressure)
catalog.notes: md.log begins with 'Log file opened on <date>' and a big banner. Energy terms printed in fixed-width fp blocks every nstlog steps. Ends with performance table 'Core t (s)  Wall t (s)  (%)'.

catalog.name: Generic RNG seed init line
catalog.sample_line: INFO: Using random seed 1337 (source: /dev/urandom)
catalog.detect_signature: case-insensitive 'seed' near 'random'/'rng'/'prng' with int/hex value: /random seed\s*[=:]\s*\w+/
catalog.fields: seed_value(int/hex), source(clock|urandom|fixed|arg), optional generator name
catalog.notes: User explicitly named seed logs. Very varied phrasing ('seed=', 'Random seed set to', 'Seeding RNG with'); best matched by keyword heuristic + numeric capture.

catalog.name: Jaeger JSON trace (API/UI)
catalog.sample_line: {"data":[{"traceID":"1be...","spans":[{"traceID":"1be...","spanID":"abc","operationName":"HTTP GET","references":[{"refType":"CHILD_OF","traceID":"..","spanID":".."}],"startTime":1716124800000000,"duration":1200,"tags":[{"key":"http.method","value":"GET"}]}],"processes":{"p1":{"serviceName":"cart"}}}]}
catalog.detect_signature: `traceID`+`spanID`+`operationName`+`references[].refType` (CHILD_OF/FOLLOWS_FROM) + top-level `processes` map keyed p1/p2
catalog.fields: traceID, spanID, operationName, references[refType,traceID,spanID], startTime(us epoch), duration(us), tags[{key,type,value}], logs, processID, processes{serviceName,tags}
catalog.notes: jaeger-query /api/traces response shape. Distinct from Zipkin by camelCase traceID and processes map. Also a Thrift/protobuf wire form.

catalog.name: LAMMPS log.lammps thermo output
catalog.detect_signature: Header line of whitespace-aligned column names beginning with 'Step' followed by numeric rows; run bracketed by 'Per MPI rank memory allocation' and 'Loop time of'
catalog.fields: columns are dynamic (thermo_style): Step,Temp,E_pair,E_mol,TotEng,Press,...; each subsequent line is a data row
catalog.notes: Column set is user-defined via thermo_style; parser must read the header row to know fields. YAML thermo mode also exists (thermo_modify) emitting 'keywords:' + 'data:' blocks. Also startup 'LAMMPS (2 Aug 2023)' banner + 'Loop time of X on N procs'.

catalog.name: LAMMPS log.lammps thermo table
catalog.detect_signature: Header row of thermo keywords ('Step Temp E_pair ... Press') followed by whitespace-aligned numeric rows; bounded by 'Per MPI rank memory allocation' and 'Loop time of'
catalog.fields: columns defined by preceding header (Step, Temp, E_pair, E_mol, TotEng, Press, PotEng, KinEng, Volume, ...); units per 'units' command
catalog.notes: Newer LAMMPS can emit YAML thermo (thermo_modify format yaml) with 'keywords:'/'data:' — separate adapter. Header order is run-defined, must be read dynamically.

catalog.name: LSF job resource-usage summary
catalog.sample_line: CPU time :                                   209542.33 sec.
catalog.detect_signature: Block headed 'Resource usage summary:' with indented 'CPU time :', 'Max Memory :', 'Max Swap :'; often preceded by 'Successfully completed.'
catalog.fields: CPU time(sec), Max Memory(MB), Average Memory(MB), Total Requested Memory(MB), Delta Memory, Max Swap, Max Processes, Max Threads, Run time(sec)
catalog.notes: Job .out also has 'Sender: LSF System', 'Subject: Job <id>', 'Successfully completed.'/'Exited with exit code N' markers.

catalog.name: LSF job resource-usage summary (bsub -o)
catalog.sample_line: CPU time :                                   209542.33 sec.
catalog.detect_signature: Block headed by 'Resource usage summary:' with indented 'CPU time :', 'Max Memory :', 'Max Swap :' lines; often preceded by 'Successfully completed.'
catalog.fields: CPU time(sec), Max Memory(MB), Average Memory(MB), Total Requested Memory(MB), Delta Memory, Max Swap, Max Processes, Max Threads, Run time(sec)
catalog.notes: Whole job .out has 'Sender: LSF System', 'Subject: Job <id>', 'Successfully completed.'/'Exited with exit code N' markers useful for detect.

catalog.name: LSP JSON-RPC wire stream
catalog.sample_line: Content-Length: 126\r\n\r\n{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"textDocument/completion","params":{"textDocument":{"uri":"file:///a.ts"},"position":{"line":3,"character":5}}}
catalog.detect_signature: 'Content-Length: <N>\r\n\r\n' header then a JSON-RPC 2.0 body ({"jsonrpc":"2.0",...} with method/id/result/error/params). Methods 'textDocument/*', 'initialize', '$/progress'.
catalog.fields: content_length, jsonrpc, id, method, params, result, error
catalog.notes: Header/body framing like HTTP. Body-only JSON is what most trace tools capture.

catalog.name: MPICH / Hydra rank-prefixed output
catalog.sample_line: [2] rank 2 reporting: setup complete
catalog.detect_signature: '[<rank>] ' bracket-integer prefix (-prepend-rank); or '-l' style '<rank>: '
catalog.fields: rank(bracket int), raw app line
catalog.notes: -prepend-pattern allows %r/%g/%p custom prefixes; Intel MPI uses same Hydra base.

catalog.name: NAMD ENERGY output
catalog.detect_signature: Lines prefixed 'ENERGY:' (data) / 'ETITLE:' (header every 10 lines); also 'Info:'/'TCL:'/'WALL:'
catalog.fields: ETITLE cols: TS BOND ANGLE DIHED IMPRP ELECT VDW BOUNDARY MISC KINETIC TOTAL TEMP TOTAL2 TOTAL3 TEMPAVG PRESSURE GPRESSURE VOLUME PRESSAVG GPRESSAVG
catalog.notes: Prefix-tagged for grep/awk; energies kcal/mol, pressure bar, temp K. 'Info:' lines carry config/startup.

catalog.name: NAMD standard output / log
catalog.detect_signature: Lines with fixed prefixes 'ENERGY:', 'ETITLE:', 'Info:', 'TIMING:', 'WRITING', 'OPENING'
catalog.fields: ENERGY: TS BOND ANGLE DIHED IMPRP ... (order defined by preceding ETITLE line); TIMING: step CPU/step Wall/step
catalog.notes: Grep-friendly unique prefixes by design. ETITLE printed once per 10 ENERGY lines defining columns. 'Info:' carries startup config (NAMD version, processor count, patch grid). 'TIMING:' and 'Benchmark time:' for perf.

catalog.name: OTLP/JSON trace
catalog.sample_line: {"resourceSpans":[{"resource":{"attributes":[{"key":"service.name","value":{"stringValue":"cart"}}]},"scopeSpans":[{"scope":{"name":"lib"},"spans":[{"traceId":"71699b6f...","spanId":"3c191d03fa8be065","name":"GET /","kind":2,"startTimeUnixNano":"1716124800000000000"}]}]}]}
catalog.detect_signature: Top-level `resourceSpans` (or resourceMetrics/resourceLogs) → `scopeSpans` → `spans`; ids are hex strings, timestamps are nanosecond decimal STRINGS
catalog.fields: traceId(32hex), spanId(16hex), parentSpanId, name, kind(int), startTimeUnixNano/endTimeUnixNano(string), attributes[{key,value:{stringValue/intValue/...}}], events, links, status{code,message}
catalog.notes: File-exporter writes one OTLP JSON per line (NDJSON). Nanos are strings to avoid JS int overflow. kind: 1=INTERNAL 2=SERVER 3=CLIENT 4=PRODUCER 5=CONSUMER.

catalog.name: Open MPI --tag-output
catalog.sample_line: [1,3]<stdout>:iteration 100 residual=1.2e-06
catalog.detect_signature: Line prefix '[<jobid>,<rank>]<stdout|stderr|stddiag>:' then app text
catalog.fields: jobid, MCW_rank, channel(stdout|stderr|stddiag), then raw app line
catalog.notes: --timestamp-output prepends an ISO ts before the tag. Core Open MPI multi-rank fingerprint.

catalog.name: OpenMPI --tag-output
catalog.sample_line: [1,0]<stdout>: Rank 0 starting on node compute-01
catalog.detect_signature: Line prefix /^\[\d+,\d+\]<(stdout|stderr|stddiag)>:? /
catalog.fields: jobid; MCW_rank; channel(stdout/stderr/stddiag); message
catalog.notes: Per-rank multiplexed output. --timestamp-output adds an ISO/'Wed Jul' timestamp prefix. TAG-DETAILED variant: '[namespace,rank][hostname:pid]<stream>:'. Very common HPC pattern.

catalog.name: PBS Pro / TORQUE server log
catalog.sample_line: 05/12/2024 14:23:01;0008;PBS_Server;Job;12345.hpc;Job Queued at request of user@host, owner = user@host, job name = run1, queue = batch
catalog.detect_signature: Semicolon 6-field: 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS;<4-hex eventcode>;<daemon>;<objtype>;<objid>;msg'
catalog.fields: ts(US MM/DD/YYYY), event_code(hex bitmask), daemon(PBS_Server), object_type(Job|Svr|Que|Node), object_id(<jobid>.<host>), message
catalog.notes: Event code is 4-digit hex log-level bitmask (0001=error..0100=job). Daily files YYYYMMDD.

catalog.name: PBS Pro / TORQUE server log (pbs_server)
catalog.sample_line: 05/12/2024 14:23:01;0008;PBS_Server;Job;12345.hpc;Job Queued at request of user@host, owner = user@host, job name = run1, queue = batch
catalog.detect_signature: Semicolon-delimited: 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS;<4-hex-eventcode>;<daemon>;<objtype>;<objid>;msg'
catalog.fields: ts(US MM/DD/YYYY), event_code(hex bitmask), daemon(PBS_Server), object_type(Job|Svr|Que|Node), object_id(<jobid>.<host>), message
catalog.notes: Event code is a 4-digit hex log-level bitmask (0001=error … 0100=job). Daily files named YYYYMMDD.

catalog.name: PBS/Torque server_log & mom_log
catalog.sample_line: 07/09/2011 14:02:33;0008;PBS_Server;Job;1234.headnode;Job Modified at request of root@headnode
catalog.fields: date(MM/DD/YYYY); time; event_hex_mask(4 hex); server/component; object_class(Job/Svr/Req); object_id; message
catalog.notes: Distinctive semicolon-delimited 6-field record with a 4-hex event-class bitmask. Log files named by date YYYYMMDD in server_logs/ and mom_logs/.

catalog.name: PyTorch Lightning seed_everything
catalog.sample_line: Global seed set to 42
catalog.detect_signature: Line matches /^(Global )?[Ss]eed set to \d+$/ or /Seed set to \d+/ emitted by logger name 'lightning' / 'pytorch_lightning.utilities.seed'
catalog.fields: seed(int); optional logger prefix [rank]
catalog.notes: User named seed explicitly. Newer Lightning emits 'Seed set to {n}'; older emits 'Global seed set to {n}'. Emitted once per process; in DDP appears once per rank. Often preceded by nothing (bare stdout) or wrapped in a Python logging line.

catalog.name: Python logging seed / reproducibility init
catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-20 11:03:22,145 INFO [train] Using seed 1337 (np, random, torch, cuda)
catalog.detect_signature: Message body contains /\b(seed|random[_ ]seed|PYTHONHASHSEED)\b/ with an integer; often via std logging '%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s'
catalog.fields: ts; level; logger; seed(int); libs seeded
catalog.notes: Free-form; the load-bearing token is 'seed <int>'. Also 'torch.manual_seed(1337)', 'np.random.seed(1337)', 'PYTHONHASHSEED=0' echoed at startup.

catalog.name: ROS 2 console log (rcutils)
catalog.sample_line: [INFO] [1698723864.357328121] [my_node]: Robot initialized
catalog.detect_signature: /^\[(DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR|FATAL)\] \[\d+\.\d+\] \[[\w./]+\]: /
catalog.fields: severity; time(sec.nanosec float); logger/node name; message; optional '(func() at file:line)'
catalog.notes: Default format from RCUTILS_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_FORMAT. Fully customizable via that env var (tokens {severity}{time}{name}{message}{function_name}{file_name}{line_number}). Levels: DEBUG10/INFO20/WARN30/ERROR40/FATAL50.

catalog.name: ROS1 rosout / rosconsole
catalog.detect_signature: '[<5-char level>] [<sec.nsec epoch>]:' — level padded ' INFO'/' WARN'/'ERROR'/'FATAL'/'DEBUG'; optional ' [/node]' before colon
catalog.fields: level(padded), ros_time(sec.nsec epoch or sim time), optional node/logger, message
catalog.notes: ROSCONSOLE_FORMAT env customizes. Default has no node name; many sites add [${node}].

catalog.name: ROS2 rcutils console output
catalog.sample_line: [INFO] [1620000000.123456789] [my_node]: My message
catalog.detect_signature: '[<LEVEL>] [<sec.nsec>] [<logger>]:' — LEVEL unpadded (INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL/DEBUG), three bracket groups
catalog.fields: severity, time(sec.nsec), logger/node name, message; RCUTILS_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_FORMAT can add {function_name}/{file_name}:{line_number}
catalog.notes: /rosout topic carries rcl_interfaces/msg/Log (stamp, level enum 10..50, name, msg, file, function, line) — structured variant if bagged.

catalog.name: SLURM job stdout (sbatch %j.out)
catalog.sample_line: slurmstepd: error: *** JOB 1234 ON compute-05 CANCELLED AT 2026-07-20T14:00:00 DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
catalog.detect_signature: 'slurmstepd: error: ***' banners; or filename pattern 'slurm-<jobid>.out'; mixed with the job's own stdout
catalog.fields: jobid; node; reason; ts
catalog.notes: The .out file is mostly the user program's own stdout/stderr, but slurmstepd injects distinctive '*** JOB ... CANCELLED/OOM ***' and 'srun: error:' lines. Detector should key on slurmstepd/srun prefixes, treat rest as passthrough.

catalog.name: SLURM slurmctld log
catalog.sample_line: [2024-05-12T14:23:01.123] sched: Allocate JobId=12345 NodeList=node[001-004] #CPUs=128 Partition=batch
catalog.detect_signature: Line starts with ISO-8601 bracket ts '[YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.mmm]' followed by optional 'error:'/'debug:'/'sched:'/'agent' token; co-occurs with JobId=, NodeList=
catalog.fields: bracket_ts(local, .%3N), optional_level(error|debug|verbose|sched|info implicit), subsystem_tag, free message with Key=Value pairs (JobId, NodeList, Partition, UID)
catalog.notes: Level is not a fixed column; often embedded as 'error:'/'debug2:' prefix. Same bracket-ts shape shared by slurmd/slurmdbd/sched.log — disambiguate by daemon-specific tokens.

catalog.name: SLURM slurmd log
catalog.sample_line: [2022-12-08T13:12:20.101] launch task 1234.0 request from UID:1000 GID:1000
catalog.detect_signature: Same bracketed-ISO-ms format as slurmctld but subsystem tokens 'launch task','task/cgroup','Invalid job credential','job_container'
catalog.fields: ts; level; job.step id (e.g. 1234.0); UID/GID; message
catalog.notes: Distinguish from slurmctld by node-side tokens. 'Invalid job credential from <ip>: Job credential expired' is a classic slurmd line.

catalog.name: TPM2 measured-boot event log
catalog.sample_line:
- EventNum: 1
  PCRIndex: 0
  EventType: EV_S_CRTM_VERSION
  DigestCount: 1
  Digests:
  - AlgorithmId: sha256
    Digest: "3d458cfe..."
  EventSize: 2
  Event: "0000"
catalog.detect_signature: YAML emitted by tpm2_eventlog: keys PCRIndex/EventType/Digests/AlgorithmId/Digest/EventSize; EventType enums 'EV_*' (EV_SEPARATOR, EV_EFI_VARIABLE_DRIVER_CONFIG, EV_EFI_PLATFORM_FIRMWARE_BLOB). Underlying binary is TCG PFP crypto-agile.
catalog.fields: PCRIndex, EventType, AlgorithmId, Digest, EventSize, Event
catalog.notes: Raw form at /sys/kernel/security/tpm0/binary_bios_measurements is packed binary (TCG_PCR_EVENT2). Two dialects: TPM1.2 SHA1-only vs TPM2 agile.

catalog.name: U-Boot boot console log
catalog.sample_line:
U-Boot 2026.01 (Jan 15 2026 - 10:22:33 +0000)
DRAM:  2 GiB
MMC:   sdhci@fe330000: 1
Net:   eth0: ethernet@fe300000
Hit any key to stop autoboot:  0
catalog.detect_signature: Banner 'U-Boot <year>.<month> (<builddate>)'; section labels 'DRAM:','MMC:','Net:','Loading Environment','Hit any key to stop autoboot'.
catalog.fields: version, builddate, dram, mmc, net, autoboot
catalog.notes: Free-form. SPL stage prefixes 'U-Boot SPL ...'.

catalog.name: Valgrind Memcheck report
catalog.sample_line:
==29== Invalid write of size 4
==29==    at 0x804838F: main (example.c:6)
==29== HEAP SUMMARY:
==29==     definitely lost: 16 bytes in 2 blocks
==29== ERROR SUMMARY: 1 errors from 1 contexts (suppressed: 0 from 0)
catalog.detect_signature: Every line prefixed '==<pid>== ' (or '--<pid>-- ' for debug); blocks 'HEAP SUMMARY:'/'LEAK SUMMARY:'/'ERROR SUMMARY:'; error kinds 'Invalid read/write', 'definitely/indirectly/possibly lost', 'Conditional jump ... uninitialised'; frames '   at 0x...: func (file:line)'.
catalog.fields: pid, error_kind, stack_frame(addr,func,file:line), leak_category, bytes, blocks, error_count
catalog.notes: '==pid==' prefix is the universal Valgrind signature across tools. --log-file redirects.

catalog.name: Vite build output
catalog.sample_line:
vite v7.1.7 building for production...
✓ 963 modules transformed.

catalog.name: aix-errpt-detail

catalog.detect_signature: Multi-line block with labeled fields in fixed order: 'LABEL:', 'IDENTIFIER:', 'Date/Time:', 'Sequence Number:', 'Machine Id:', 'Node Id:', 'Class:', 'Type:', 'Resource Name:', then sections 'Description', 'Probable Causes', 'Failure Causes', 'Recommended Actions', 'Detail Data'; records separated by dashed lines
catalog.fields: label, identifier, date/time (Ddd Mmm DD HH:MM:SS TZ YYYY), sequence number, machine/node id, class, type (PERM/TEMP/INFO), resource name/class/type, free-text sections, detail data (often hex dumps)
catalog.notes: Sequence Number is a good trace_id. Type: PERM => level=error. Source: IBM errpt docs + check_aix_errpt ('^Type: *PERM' matching).

catalog.name: aix-errpt-summary
catalog.sample_line: A63BEB70   0626155306 P S SYSPROC        SOFTWARE PROGRAM ABNORMALLY TERMINATED

catalog.fields: identifier (8 hex), timestamp mmddhhmmyy, type (Permanent/Temporary/Informational/Unknown/Pending), class (Hardware/Software/Operator/Undetermined), resource_name, description
catalog.notes: The mmddhhmmyy timestamp needs century/era handling. Source: check_aix_errpt Nagios plugin (sample quoted verbatim) + IBM errpt docs.

catalog.name: android-anr-traces
catalog.product: Android ANR thread dumps (/data/anr/traces.txt, /data/anr/anr_*, bugreport 'VM TRACES AT LAST ANR' section)
catalog.sample_line: ----- pid 6996 at 2015-01-01 01:01:01 -----\nCmd line: com.example.app\n\"main\" prio=5 tid=1 MONITOR
catalog.detect_signature: ^----- pid \d+ at \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} -----$ followed by 'Cmd line: '; thread headers ^\"[^\"]+\" (daemon )?prio=\d+ tid=\d+ (Runnable|RUNNABLE|MONITOR|WAIT|NATIVE|TimedWaiting|Blocked|Waiting|Native|Sleeping)
catalog.fields: per-process: pid, wall time, cmdline, build; per-thread: name, daemon, prio, tid, state, sysTid/nice/utm/stm line, held mutexes, Java frames ('at com.example.Foo.bar(Foo.java:42)'), native frames ('native: #00 pc 0004793e /system/lib/libc.so (...)'), lock edges ('- waiting to lock <0x0abc1234> ... held by thread 5')
catalog.notes: ART (>=5.0) and Dalvik variants differ slightly (Dalvik: 'DALVIK THREADS: (mutexes: tll=0 tsl=0 tscl=0 ghl=0)'). Ends with '----- end <pid> -----'. Lock-graph edges are the payload an AI wants.

catalog.name: android-bugreport
catalog.product: Android bugreport / dumpstate output (adb bugreport zip: bugreport-*.txt)
catalog.detect_signature: '== dumpstate: ' header near top, and repeated '------ SECTION NAME (cmd) ------' ... '------ 0.318s was the duration of ...' dividers
catalog.fields: container: header block (build fingerprint, kernel, uptime) + named sections each holding another format (logcat threadtime, dmesg, dumpsys per-service, ANR traces, tombstones)
catalog.notes: Implement as a container/demultiplexer: split on section dividers and route each section to the matching sub-adapter (logcat, dmesg, dumpsys, anr, tombstone). Zip also contains FS/, anr/, tombstones/ copies.

catalog.name: android-logcat-threadtime
catalog.product: Android logcat (default -v threadtime; also what `adb logcat` emits since ~4.x, and the crash/radio/system buffers)
catalog.sample_line: 04-01 16:05:35.099   158   163 D dalvikvm: GC_CONCURRENT freed 384K, 19% free 18438K/22727K, paused 6ms+6ms
catalog.fields: date(MM-DD, no year), time(HH:MM:SS.mmm), pid, tid, priority(V/D/I/W/E/F/S), tag, message
catalog.notes: THE most common mobile log line on Earth. Map priority V->trace D->debug I->info W->warn E->error F->fatal S->silent. Also handle interleaved buffer-divider lines '--------- beginning of main' / 'beginning of crash' / 'beginning of system' / 'beginning of events' emitted by adb logcat. No year in timestamp: infer from file mtime/context. Multi-line messages repeat the full prefix per line.

catalog.name: android-tombstone
catalog.product: Android native crash tombstones (/data/tombstones/tombstone_NN, debuggerd/crash_dump output, also mirrored into logcat E/DEBUG)

*** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** *** ***
Build fingerprint: 'Android/aosp_angler/angler:7.1.1/NYC/enh12211018:eng/test-keys'
pid: 17946, tid: 17949, name: crasher  >>> crasher <<<
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR), fault addr 0xc
catalog.detect_signature: leading row of '*** *** ***' stars; 'Build fingerprint:' + 'pid: \d+, tid: \d+, name: .+ >>> .+ <<<' + 'signal \d+ \(SIG','backtrace:' with frames '#\d\d pc [0-9a-f]+ <path> (\(symbol\+off\))?'
catalog.fields: build fingerprint, revision, ABI, pid/tid/thread-name/process, signal/code/fault-addr, abort message, registers (r0../x0..), backtrace frames (num, pc, mapped file, symbol+offset, BuildId), stack memory dump, memory map ('memory near', maps), open FDs, log tail

catalog.name: android_anr_trace
catalog.sample_line:
----- pid 12345 at 2026-07-21 15:40:39 -----
Cmd line: com.myapp
"main" prio=5 tid=1 Native
  | group="main" sCount=1 ...
  at android.os.MessageQueue.nativePollOnce(Native Method)
catalog.detect_signature: '----- pid <n> at <ts> -----' header, 'Cmd line:', then per-thread blocks: '"threadname" prio=N tid=N <state>' followed by '  | ...' and '  at ...' frames; also logcat 'ANR in com.pkg' line
catalog.fields: ts (header), pid, data.threads[] (name, tid, state, stack), source=ANR
catalog.notes: Large MULTILINE dump; one file = one event with many thread sub-blocks. Thread states: Runnable/Native/Waiting/Suspended/Sleeping. The separate logcat 'ANR in <pkg> (reason ...)' + 'Reason:'/'CPU usage' summary lines pair with this.

catalog.name: android_crash_fatal
catalog.product: Android app crash — FATAL EXCEPTION block (Logcat / uncaught handler)
catalog.sample_line:
E/AndroidRuntime(  915): FATAL EXCEPTION: main
E/AndroidRuntime(  915): java.lang.NullPointerException: Attempt to invoke virtual method ...
E/AndroidRuntime(  915): 	at com.myapp.MainActivity.onCreate(MainActivity.java:34)
catalog.detect_signature: 'FATAL EXCEPTION:' line under AndroidRuntime tag, followed by an exception class line and '\tat ' stack frames, plus 'Caused by:' chains
catalog.fields: level=E(rror), source=AndroidRuntime, pid (in parens), message=exception class+msg, data.stack=frames; thread name after FATAL EXCEPTION:
catalog.notes: MULTILINE Java/Kotlin stack trace; must coalesce all '\tat', 'Caused by:', '... N more' continuation lines into one event. May appear with logcat threadtime prefix ('07-21 15:40:39.123  915  915 E AndroidRuntime:'). The logcat framing itself is already covered; the crash BLOCK grouping is the gap.

catalog.name: astm-e1394-lis2
catalog.product: ASTM E1394 / CLSI LIS2-A2 analyzer-to-LIS messages (Horiba Yumizen, Sysmex, Roche, Abbott lab instruments; SENAITE/other LIS session logs)
catalog.detect_signature: Frame lines: leading frame number digit 0-7, then record type H/P/O/R/C/Q/M/L + '|'; header record contains '|\^&' delimiter definition; message ends with L|1 terminator; raw sessions framed STX(0x02)...ETX/ETB + 2-hex checksum + CRLF, with ENQ/ACK/EOT handshake bytes
catalog.fields: H record: sender name^version, processing ID, version (LIS2-A2), timestamp YYYYMMDDHHMMSS -> ts; P patient record, O order (specimen ID, test ^^^DIF, priority, order datetime), R results (value/units/flags), C comments (e.g. CONTROL_FAILED^^PLT_ABOVE_TOLERANCE), Q query, L terminator; frame digit + trailing checksum chars to strip/verify
catalog.notes: Sample lines verified verbatim from senaite.astm test data (Yumizen H500 capture on GitHub): '1H|\^&|||H500^910YOXH02826^2.2.2.2b|||||||Q|LIS2-A2|20230329110749BC', '2P|1|...|33', '3O|1|PX440N||^^^DIF|R|20230329110631|...|F|||||26', '4C|1|I|CONTROL_FAILED^^PLT_ABOVE_TOLERANCE|ID3', '2L|1|N05'. Trailing 2 chars per line are the frame checksum. Ubiquitous in clinical labs; often captured in LIS debug logs.

catalog.detect_signature: Semicolon-separated frames, trailing space + integer count; Java frames dotted (Class.method), native frames with `_[k]`/`_[j]` suffixes possible

catalog.notes: `-o collapsed`. Frame annotations: `_[j]` JIT-compiled, `_[i]` inlined, `_[k]` kernel, `_[0]` C1. Canonical folded-stacks producer alongside FlameGraph.

catalog.name: bpftrace histogram (hist/lhist)

catalog.name: brocade-fos-raslog-audit

catalog.fields: syslog ts/host, audit ts+tz, event_id ([SEC-3022]), severity, event_class (SECURITY/CLI/ZONE), user/role/src_ip/interface/app 5-tuple, admin_domain/switch/FID, fos_version, then 'Event:', 'Status:', 'Info:' or 'CLI:' kv tail

catalog.name: carbonblack-edr-event-forwarder-json

catalog.detect_signature: JSON with "type" key whose value is a dotted event name in the ingress.event.* / watchlist.hit.* / feed.* / alert.* namespace, plus "sensor_id" and "cb_server"
catalog.fields: type (ingress.event.procstart/procend/netconn/filemod/regmod/moduleload, watchlist.hit.process, alert.watchlist.hit.ingress.process), process_guid, pid, path, command_line, parent_path, md5/sha256, sensor_id, hostname, timestamp (epoch), cb_server
catalog.notes: cb-event-forwarder subscribes to the Cb Response event bus and emits per-type JSON. Dotted event-type namespace is the strong fingerprint. Verified from Carbon Black Developer Network event-schema docs.

catalog.name: cef
catalog.product: ArcSight Common Event Format (many vendors: MikroTik, Imperva, Zscaler, etc.)
catalog.sample_line: Jan 24 12:32:10 host CEF:0|Security|threatmanager|1.0|100|worm successfully stopped|10|src=10.0.0.1 dst=2.1.2.2 spt=1232 act=blocked dpt=443
catalog.detect_signature: literal 'CEF:0|' then 7 pipe-delimited header fields (Version|Vendor|Product|Version|SignatureID|Name|Severity) followed by a space + key=value extension
catalog.fields: header pipes->vendor/product/signature/name; final Severity->level; extension key=value (src/dst/spt/dpt/act)->data
catalog.notes: Cross-vendor normalization format — one adalter covers dozens of security products. Header is exactly 7 pipe fields; escaped \| and \= allowed; extension is space-separated k=v (values may contain spaces). LEEF is the sibling: 'LEEF:2.0|Vendor|Product|Version|EventID|' with tab or custom-delimited k=v — worth a paired adapter.

catalog.name: celery-worker-log

catalog.fields: [asctime: LEVEL/processName], message; task lines embed 'Task app.tasks.name[uuid] succeeded in 1.23s' — task id is trace_id
catalog.notes: Real lines verified from NeuroVault CELERY_README (default '[%(asctime)s: %(levelname)s/%(processName)s]' format). Extremely common in Python deployments alongside the already-covered brokers.

catalog.name: chef-client-log

catalog.fields: ts, level, message (includes 'Starting Chef Infra Client, version X', run_list, resource updates)

catalog.name: cics-dfh-message-log
catalog.product: IBM CICS TS message logs (console, CSMT/CDBC/MSGUSR transient-data queues)
catalog.sample_line: 07/20/2026 09:15:32 CICSPROD DFHSI1517 Control is being given to CICS.
catalog.detect_signature: Message ID '^DFH[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4,5}I?' (DFHSI=init, DFHAC=abnormal task, DFHTM=termination, DFHDU=dump); in MSGUSR lines are prefixed date time applid; in SYSLOG they carry the standard hardcopy prefix
catalog.fields: date, time, applid, message_id, transaction, task, terminal, abend code (e.g. DFHAC2206 ... ABEND ASRA)
catalog.notes: DFHAC2206/ASRA-style transaction-abend messages are the mainframe equivalent of an app crash log; severity letter at end of msgid.

catalog.name: cics-msgusr-transient-data
catalog.product: IBM CICS TS transient-data destination logs (MSGUSR/CSMT/CDBC)
catalog.sample_line: DFHAC2206 13:03:15 CICSPROD Transaction ABCD has failed with abend ASRA. Resource backout was successful.
catalog.detect_signature: Lines begin with CICS message id ^DFH[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4}[IWES]? then time hh:mm:ss and APPLID, then text; abend messages DFHAC22xx, sign-on DFHSN12xx/13xx, file DFHFC messages
catalog.fields: message_id (module code AC/SN/FC/SI...), time, applid, transaction, userid, terminal, abend code, text
catalog.notes: Where CICS application-level errors/abends/security events land. Date is not on each line (file/day context). Console-side DFH messages also flow into SYSLOG with '+DFH' prefix.

catalog.name: cisco-asa-syslog
catalog.detect_signature: token matching %ASA-[0-7]-\d{6}: (also %PIX-/%FWSM-); message id selects one of ~2000 fixed English templates
catalog.fields: severity,message_id,then per-id: direction,proto,conn_id,interface:ip/port pairs,duration,bytes,acl_name,reason
catalog.notes: Key ids: 302013/302014 built/teardown TCP, 302015/302016 UDP, 106023 ACL deny, 106100 ACL log, 113019 VPN. Template-table parse per message id.

catalog.name: cisco-cucm-sdl-trace
catalog.product: Cisco Unified Communications Manager SDL/SDI trace files
catalog.sample_line: 00123456.001 |10:26:12.123 |AppInfo  |//SIP/SIPTcp/wait_SdlReadRsp: Incoming SIP TCP message from 203.0.113.10 on port 51234 index 8 with 1330 bytes:
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{8}\.\d{3} \|\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3} \|(AppInfo|SdlSig|Created|Destroyed|PktCap|SdlStat)\s*\| pipe-delimited: seq.line | time | trace-type | body
catalog.fields: sequence.line, time-of-day (date from file header), trace type, body (SDL signal names, //SIP/ SIPTcp dumps with embedded raw SIP)
catalog.notes: CCM SDL traces (SDL00x_xxx.txt from RTMT). Embedded SIP messages delegate to sip-raw-message.

catalog.name: cisco-ftd-syslog
catalog.product: Cisco Firepower FTD/FMC syslog (%FTD-1-430001..430005 'Key: Value' CSV)
catalog.sample_line: Dec 12 2023 16:53:19 %FTD-1-430003: EventPriority: Low, DeviceUUID: 43e77ca4-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, InstanceID: 4, FirstPacketSecond: 2023-12-12T16:53:19Z, ConnectionID: 57192, AccessControlRuleAction: Allow, SrcIP: 172.26.214.182, DstIP: 8.8.8.8, Protocol: icmp, IngressInterface: inside, EgressInterface: outside, ACPolicy: MY_POLICY, AccessControlRuleName: ICMP_IPS_TEST, InitiatorPackets: 1, ResponderPackets: 1, InitiatorBytes: 74, ResponderBytes: 74
catalog.detect_signature: %FTD-\d-43000[1-5]: followed by comma-separated 'Key: Value' pairs (CamelCase keys); 430001=intrusion, 430002/3=connection start/end, 430004/5=file events
catalog.fields: EventPriority,DeviceUUID,InstanceID,ConnectionID,AccessControlRuleAction,SrcIP,DstIP,SrcPort,DstPort,Protocol,IngressZone,EgressZone,ACPolicy,AccessControlRuleName,ApplicationProtocol,Client,ConnectionDuration,InitiatorBytes,ResponderBytes,URL,SigID
catalog.notes: FTD also re-emits ASA-style %FTD-6-302013 platform messages — route those to the cisco-asa template parser.

catalog.name: cisco-ios-syslog
catalog.sample_line: 000123: *Mar  1 18:46:11.011 UTC: %SYS-5-CONFIG_I: Configured from console by vty2 (10.34.195.36)
catalog.detect_signature: regex %[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+-[0-7]-[A-Z0-9_]+: preceded by optional 'seqno: ' and optional '*'/'.' service-timestamp (uptime 'HH:MM:SS' or 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS.mmm TZ'); NOT preceded by 'RP/x/y' node prefix (IOS-XR) and timestamp does NOT start with a 4-digit year (NX-OS)
catalog.fields: seq_no?, ts (uptime or datetime; '*'=unsynced clock, '.'=NTP-sync-lost), facility, severity(0-7), mnemonic, message; via remote syslog also PRI + hostname
catalog.notes: Single adapter covers IOS classic and IOS-XE; map severity 0-7 directly to level; category=facility, source=hostname if syslog-wrapped. Mnemonic examples: LINK-3-UPDOWN, LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN, OSPF-5-ADJCHG, BGP-5-ADJCHANGE, DUAL-5-NBRCHANGE.

catalog.name: cisco-iosxr-syslog
catalog.sample_line: RP/0/RSP0/CPU0:Mar 26 22:04:26.104 : ifmgr[240]: %PKT_INFRA-LINK-3-UPDOWN : Interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, changed state to Up
catalog.detect_signature: line starts with node prefix regex ^(RP|LC|SP)/\d+/[A-Z0-9]+/CPU\d+: then timestamp, then process[pid]:, then %CATEGORY-GROUP-SEV-MNEMONIC (4-part mnemonic vs IOS 3-part)
catalog.fields: node (rack/slot/module), ts.ms, process, pid, category, group, severity, mnemonic, message
catalog.notes: 4-part %CAT-GROUP-SEV-MNEMONIC and RP/x/y/CPU0 prefix are unique. trace_id candidate: node+process+pid.

catalog.name: cisco-mds-nxos-syslog
catalog.product: Cisco MDS 9000 / NX-OS SAN switch syslog (%FACILITY-SEV-MNEMONIC)
catalog.sample_line: 2024 Mar 15 14:31:45 +00:00 mds9148-01 %FLOGI-3-FLOGI_FAILED: FLOGI failed for port fc2/3, WWN 50:00:14:40:5d:a2:b1:c8
catalog.detect_signature: 'YYYY Mon DD HH:MM:SS <tz>' NX-OS date then '%FAC-SEV-MNEMONIC:'; SAN facilities PORT/ETHPORT/ZONE/FLOGI/VSAN/FCNS; sev digit 0-7
catalog.fields: ts, switch_hostname, facility, severity_num, mnemonic, message (interface fcX/Y, WWNs, zoneset names)
catalog.notes: Sample lines from canast01/chris-kb docs/san/cisco/mds/troubleshooting/diagnostics.md; framing corroborated by AlienVault OSSIM cisco-nexus-nx-os.cfg regexes (alienfault/ossim). Covers NX-OS Nexus too (cisco-nexus absent from known list). Also matches %PORT-5-IF_UP / %ZONE-5-ZONESET_ACTIVATED / %ETHPORT-5-IF_DOWN.

catalog.name: cisco-nxos-syslog
catalog.sample_line: 2013 Nov  1 14:07:58 switch %ETHPORT-5-IF_DOWN_LINK_FAILURE: Interface Ethernet1/5 is down (Link failure)
catalog.detect_signature: timestamp begins with 4-digit YEAR then 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS' followed by hostname and %FACILITY[-SUBFACILITY]-SEV-MNEMONIC:; optional VDC marker '%$ VDC-N %$' between ts and facility
catalog.fields: ts (year-first), hostname, vdc_id?, facility (may be compound e.g. ETH_PORT_CHANNEL), severity, mnemonic, message
catalog.notes: Year-first timestamp is the reliable NX-OS discriminator vs IOS. 'show logging' local format identical to syslog export minus PRI.

catalog.name: cisco_asa
catalog.product: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA / PIX / FTD syslog
catalog.sample_line: <166>Jun 27 2018 12:17:46 asa-fw : %ASA-6-302016: Teardown UDP connection 806353 for outside:172.18.123.243/24057 to identity:172.18.124.136/161 duration 0:02:01 bytes 313
catalog.detect_signature: '%ASA-<sev>-<msgid>:' (also %PIX- / %FTD- / %ASASM-)
catalog.fields: pri<>, ts, host, msg_class=ASA, severity(0-7), message_id(e.g.302016), free-text -> data; message_id maps to semantics (302013/16 build/teardown, 106023 deny)
catalog.notes: Timestamp format varies (RFC3164, RFC5424, EMBLEM). message_id is the key correlator — a lookup table gives category. Deny messages: %ASA-4-106023 'Deny tcp src ... dst ... by access-group'.

catalog.name: cisco_ios
catalog.product: Cisco IOS / IOS-XE / NX-OS device syslog
catalog.sample_line: Jun 27 12:17:46.123: %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down
catalog.detect_signature: '%FACILITY-[subfac-]SEVERITY-MNEMONIC:' e.g. %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN, %SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP
catalog.fields: ts (optional seq '000123:' + uptime/datetime), FACILITY, severity(0-7), MNEMONIC, message -> data
catalog.notes: Optional leading sequence number and 'service timestamps' format. %SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP carries ACL hits. NX-OS uses same %FAC-SEV-MNEMONIC shape.

catalog.name: cisco_ios_syslog
catalog.sample_line: Jan 24 12:20:11 sw1 123456: *Jan 24 12:20:10.512: %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down
catalog.detect_signature: token matching '%FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC:' e.g. '%LINK-3-UPDOWN:' / '%SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP:' (facility upper, single-digit severity 0-7, mnemonic upper)
catalog.fields: %FAC-SEV-MNEM->category+level(severity 0-7); optional seq# and timestamp; free-text tail->data.message
catalog.notes: The %FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC: tag is the universal Cisco IOS detector; severity digit maps to syslog severity. Optional leading sequence number and a millisecond '*Mon DD HH:MM:SS.mmm:' device timestamp precede the tag. ACL hits use %SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP.

catalog.name: citrix-netscaler-appfw-native
catalog.product: Citrix NetScaler AppFirewall (WAF) violation lines in native syslog
catalog.sample_line: Jun 22 19:14:37 <local0.info> 81.2.69.144 06/22/2015:19:14:37 GMT ns 0-PPE-1 : default APPFW APPFW_cross-site scripting 60 0 : 175.16.199.1 616-PPE1 y/3upt2K8ySWWId3Kavbxyni7Rw0000 pr_ffc http://aaron.stratum8.net/FFC/login.php?login_name=abc&passwd=12345 Cross-site script check failed for field text_area="Bad tag: script" <blocked>
catalog.detect_signature: native NetScaler skeleton with feature APPFW and event starting APPFW_ (APPFW_STARTURL, APPFW_FIELDCONSISTENCY, APPFW_XSS...); violation payload = src-ip, msgid-PPE, base64 session cookie, profile name, URL, reason, trailing <blocked>/<not blocked>
catalog.fields: everything in citrix-netscaler-syslog-native + client ip, session token, appfw profile, attacked URL, violation reason, block verdict

catalog.notes: Elastic Endpoint emits Elastic Common Schema (ECS) events via Elastic Agent. ECS is a broad schema; the endpoint discriminator is agent.type=endpoint + event.module/dataset=endpoint.*. Note many other Elastic sources also use ECS — dedup carefully at the dataset level.

catalog.name: emqx-text-log
catalog.sample_line: 2024-03-20T11:08:39.568980+01:00 [warning] tag: AUTHZ, clientid: client1, msg: cannot_publish_to_topic_due_to_not_authorized, peername: 127.0.0.1:47860, username: user1, topic: republish-event/1, reason: not_authorized
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T[\d:.]+[+-]\d{2}:\d{2} \[(debug|info|notice|warning|error|critical|alert|emergency)\] (tag: [A-Z]+, )?(clientid: |msg: )
catalog.fields: RFC3339 ts with microseconds+offset, [level], comma-separated k:v pairs — tag (MQTT/AUTHN/AUTHZ...), clientid, msg (snake_case), peername ip:port, username, extra context
catalog.notes: Sample quoted verbatim from docs.emqx.com observability/log page. msg value is machine-readable snake_case — good candidate for data.message plus structured extras.

catalog.name: eset-protect-cef-syslog
catalog.product: ESET PROTECT (endpoint threat events, syslog CEF)
catalog.sample_line: CEF:0|ESET|Threat Event|1.0|Threat|Threat detected|8|rt=2022-07-11T20:33:24Z dhost=win-desktop01 suser=jdoe filePath=C:\Users\jdoe\evil.exe cs1=Eicar test file cs1Label=Threat cs2=Real-time file system protection cs2Label=Scanner act=cleaned by deleting
catalog.detect_signature: CEF header with device vendor "ESET"; event class from ESET set (Threat, HIPS, Firewall aggregated, FilteredWebsites, Audit); cs*Label values "Threat"/"Scanner"
catalog.fields: CEF header (vendor=ESET, product=event category), rt (ISO8601), dhost, suser, filePath, cs1=Threat name, cs2=Scanner/module, act (action), plus hash/hits fields
catalog.notes: ESET PROTECT can emit JSON, LEEF, or CEF via its syslog server. Vendor=ESET header is the fingerprint. Event categories: Antivirus, HIPS, Firewall, Web protection, Audit, ESET Inspect (EDR) alerts, Blocked files.

catalog.name: esp32_panic
catalog.product: ESP32 Guru Meditation panic + register dump + backtrace (Xtensa/RISC-V)
catalog.sample_line:
Guru Meditation Error: Core  1 panic'ed (LoadProhibited). Exception was unhandled.
PC      : 0x400d1234  PS      : 0x00060730  A0      : 0x800d5678  A1      : 0x3ffb1f60
Backtrace:0x400d1231:0x3ffb1f60 0x400d5675:0x3ffb1f80
catalog.detect_signature: "Guru Meditation Error: Core <n> panic'ed (<cause>)"; register dump lines with PC/PS/A0..A15/EXCCAUSE/EXCVADDR (Xtensa) or MEPC/MTVAL (RISC-V); 'Backtrace:' line of PC:SP pairs
catalog.fields: level=error/fatal; trace_id=core id; data.message=panic cause (LoadProhibited/StoreProhibited/IllegalInstruction/InstrFetchProhibited); register kv; backtrace=PC:SP pairs (decode with addr2line)
catalog.notes: Multiline. RISC-V (C3/C6) omits Backtrace by default and uses MEPC/MTVAL. Followed by 'Rebooting...' and optionally a base64 core dump. Source: docs.espressif.com fatal-errors, esp-techpedia guru-meditation.

catalog.name: esp32_rom_boot
catalog.product: ESP32 first-stage ROM bootloader + 2nd-stage bootloader banner
catalog.sample_line:
rst:0x1 (POWERON_RESET),boot:0x13 (SPI_FAST_FLASH_BOOT)
configsip: 0, SPIWP:0xee
I (31) boot: ESP-IDF v5.1 2nd stage bootloader
catalog.detect_signature: 'rst:0x.. (..._RESET),boot:0x.. (..._BOOT)' ROM line; then 'I (n) boot:' / 'boot.esp32:' 2nd-stage lines; sometimes garbage at wrong baud
catalog.fields: reset_reason, boot_mode from rst/boot hex+enum; subsequent lines follow esp_idf_log format with tag 'boot'/'boot.esp32'
catalog.notes: The rst:/boot: line is emitted by ROM at fixed 115200 (or crystal-derived) baud before app logging config applies. Reset-reason decode is diagnostic gold. Source: docs.espressif.com bootloader guide.

catalog.name: esp_idf_log
catalog.sample_line: I (1523) wifi:connected with MyAP, aid = 1, channel 6
catalog.detect_signature: '<L> (<ms>) <tag>: msg' — single level letter I/W/E/D/V, space, '(millis)' or '(HH:MM:SS.sss)', tag, colon
catalog.fields: level: E=error W=warn I=info D=debug V=verbose; ts_ms from (number) or (HH:MM:SS.sss) per CONFIG_LOG_TIMESTAMP_SOURCE; source=tag; data.message=text
catalog.notes: Very common in AI-debugged embedded work. Timestamp modes: millis since boot (default), HH:MM:SS.sss, YY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss, or unix-ms. ANSI color per level by default. Source: docs.espressif.com esp-idf log.html.

catalog.name: esxi-syslog-rfc5424-wrapper
catalog.product: VMware ESXi/vCenter remote syslog transport (all agents, RFC5424 with '-' fields)
catalog.sample_line: <14>1 2022-02-11T09:07:33.823Z myhosttest.mylab.com Hostd: info hostd[2100216] [Originator@6876 sub=Vimsvc.TaskManager] Task Created : haTask-...
catalog.detect_signature: '<PRI>1 ' RFC5424 header whose MSG part itself begins with a Vmacore/vmkernel/vobd payload; vCenter appliance variant '<14>1 ts host vpxd 54128 - - Event [...]' with '- -' SD fields
catalog.fields: pri, ts, host, appname, then delegate MSG to inner adapter (vmacore/vmkernel/vobd)
catalog.notes: Composite: detect the 5424 envelope, then re-dispatch the message to the inner ESXi adapters. All samples in SplunkScriplets file are in this envelope

catalog.name: esxi-vmkernel
catalog.sample_line: 2022-02-11T09:08:05.317Z cpu40:2100116)MemSchedAdmit: 489: uw.2100116 (6935) extraMin/extraFromParent: 158/158, lbt (804) childEmin/eMinLimit: 3198/3328
catalog.detect_signature: ISO8601 ts then 'cpu<N>:<worldID>)' prefix; warnings add 'WARNING: <Subsys>: <line>:' (e.g. 'cpu52:2097791)WARNING: VFAT: 3739: ...'); often syslog-wrapped with program 'vmkernel'/'vmkwarning'
catalog.fields: ts, cpu, world_id, subsystem, source_line, severity(WARNING/ALERT via prefix), message
catalog.notes: Grounded verbatim from getkub/SplunkScriplets sampleData/raw/vmware/sample_logs.txt. Kernel-side ESXi log; also appears wrapped as RFC5424 '<14>1 ts host vmkernel: cpu...'

catalog.name: esxi-vobd
catalog.sample_line: vobd: [netCorrelator] 25665383us: [esx.audit.net.firewall.config.changed] Firewall configuration has changed. Operation 'add' for rule set vpxHeartbeats succeeded.
catalog.detect_signature: 'vobd:' program + '[<correlator>] <N>us: [vob.* or esx.audit.*/esx.problem.*]' — dotted VOB event id in second bracket
catalog.fields: ts(syslog wrapper), correlator, uptime_us, vob_event_id(category), message
catalog.notes: Grounded verbatim (SplunkScriplets). VOB ids (esx.audit.*, esx.problem.*, vob.*) are a stable event taxonomy — map to category and level (audit→info, problem→warning/error)

catalog.name: etcd-zap-json
catalog.product: etcd v3.4+ (also Milvus and other go.uber.org/zap JSON-encoder services)
catalog.sample_line: {"level":"info","ts":"2023-05-20T10:22:33.987Z","caller":"embed/etcd.go:308","msg":"starting an etcd server","etcd-version":"3.5.9","member-id":"8e9e05c52164694d"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with exact key trio level+ts+caller(+msg) where caller matches \S+\.go:\d+ — zap production encoder; ts may be float epoch or RFC3339 depending on config
catalog.fields: level (lowercase), ts, caller, msg, plus arbitrary typed fields (member-id, remote-peer-id, took, error)
catalog.notes: Confirmed etcd builds console/JSON encoders from DefaultZapLoggerConfig in server/embed/config_logging.go. Generic zap-json adapter also catches Milvus, Dgraph alpha (zap mode), TiDB Lightning, cilium etc. — keep product attribution by filename/fields.

catalog.name: exchange-message-tracking-csv
catalog.product: Microsoft Exchange Server message tracking log (MSGTRK*.LOG)
catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-20T09:00:12.345Z,10.0.0.5,MBX01.contoso.com,10.0.0.9,EDGE01,"MDB:...;Mailbox:...",MBX01\Default MBX01,SMTP,RECEIVE,73014444033,<abc@contoso.com>,d7c8...,jane@contoso.com,250 2.1.5,4096,1,,,Weekly report,bob@contoso.com,bob@contoso.com,,Incoming,,,
catalog.detect_signature: file header lines '#Software: Microsoft Exchange Server' + '#Log-Type: Message Tracking Log' + '#Fields: date-time,client-ip,client-hostname,server-ip,server-hostname,source-context,connector-id,source,event-id,internal-message-id,message-id,network-message-id,recipient-address,...'; data rows are CSV with ISO8601 first field and event-id in {RECEIVE,SEND,DELIVER,FAIL,DSN,EXPAND,DEFER,...}
catalog.fields: date-time, client/server ip+hostname, connector-id, source (SMTP/STOREDRIVER/ROUTING/AGENT), event-id, internal-message-id, message-id, network-message-id (trace_id), recipient-address(;-separated), recipient-status, total-bytes, recipient-count, message-subject, sender-address, return-path, directionality, original-client-ip, custom-data
catalog.notes: W3C-style #Fields header makes columns self-describing — parse header, map dynamically.

catalog.name: exim-mainlog
catalog.sample_line: 2002-10-31 08:57:53 16ZCW1-0005MB-00 <= kryten@dwarf.fict.example H=mailer.fict.example [192.168.123.123] U=exim P=smtp S=5678 id=<incoming-msg-id>
catalog.detect_signature: line starts 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (+opt ms/tz/pid) then Exim message-ID XXXXXX-YYYYYY-ZZ then a 2-char flag from <= => -> >> *> ** == (or flagless event text like 'Completed')
catalog.fields: ts, exim msgid (trace_id), direction flag, address, H=host [ip], U=user, P=protocol, S=size, R=router, T=transport, C=confirmation, DT=delivery time, id=message-id
catalog.notes: Flag semantics: <= arrival, => delivery, -> extra rcpt, ** failed, == deferred. cPanel servers make this format enormously widespread.

catalog.name: express_morgan_combined
catalog.sample_line: ::1 - - [21/Jul/2026:15:40:39 +0000] "GET /api/users HTTP/1.1" 200 1234 "http://localhost/" "Mozilla/5.0"
catalog.detect_signature: Apache combined/common: '<ip> - <user> [<clf-date>] "<req>" <status> <bytes> "<referer>" "<ua>"'; 'common' drops referer+ua
catalog.fields: data.ip, data.user, ts (CLF date), data.method/path/proto, data.status, data.bytes, data.referer, data.ua
catalog.notes: Identical shape to apache/gunicorn/nginx access — a shared 'CLF/combined' parser should serve all. Node origin only inferable from surrounding context.

catalog.name: express_morgan_dev
catalog.sample_line: GET /api/users 200 12.345 ms - 1234
catalog.detect_signature: '<METHOD> <path> <status> <resp-time> ms - <length>' — no timestamp, no IP; status is ANSI-colored by class in a TTY
catalog.fields: data.method, data.path, data.status, data.duration_ms, data.bytes; no ts → use ingest time
catalog.notes: Very common in Node dev consoles. No timestamp field at all (generic_ts must supply one). '- -' shows when length unknown.

catalog.name: f5-bigip-asm-kv-request
catalog.product: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF + Bot Defense remote logging (comma-separated key="value" over syslog)
catalog.sample_line: hostname="asm.example.com",bigip_mgmt_ip="10.10.100.100",client_ip="192.168.10.10",client_port="54389",client_request_uri="/test/picture.jpg",dest_ip="10.10.10.10",dest_port="80",device_product="Application Security Module",device_vendor="F5",errdefs_msgno="23003147",http_method="GET",support_id="3161892955527053449",request_status="illegal",action="undetermined",bot_name="Presenting as CHROME",session_id="8549049561352296353",http_request="GET /test/picture.jpg HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 10.10.10.10\r\n..."
catalog.detect_signature: comma-separated k="v" pairs with the trio device_vendor="F5" + support_id= + errdefs_msgno= (or unit_hostname=/management_ip_address= in older ASM profiles). Values are double-quoted; embedded raw HTTP request with \r\n.
catalog.fields: support_id (F5's official correlation id), errdefs_msgno, client/dest ip+port, method, uri, request_status/action, violations, attack_type, sig_ids, bot fields, full raw http_request
catalog.notes: Sample from Elastic f5_bigip pipeline test corpus (bot-defense event). Classic ASM security-event profile uses the same k="v" comma format with violations=/attack_type= fields. Parse into data.* and set trace_id=support_id.

catalog.name: f5-bigip-ltm-syslog
catalog.sample_line: err tmm[11661]: 01010028:3: No members available for pool /Common/my_pool
catalog.detect_signature: syslog line whose process is tmm/tmm1/mcpd/bigd etc. and whose message starts with an 8-hex-digit F5 errdefs code + severity digit: regex \b[0-9a-f]{8}:\d: (e.g. 01010028:3:). Full on-box line is 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS hostname err tmm[pid]: 01010028:3: msg' — BSD-syslog prefix with the F5 level word (err/notice/info) before the process.
catalog.fields: timestamp, hostname, f5 severity word, process[pid], errdefs msg code (maps to KB article), numeric severity, free-text message (pool/member/monitor names in /Partition/name form)
catalog.notes: The errdefs code is the trace_id-grade key (e.g. 01010028=no pool members, 01010221=members available). Same skeleton carries GTM (gtmd), audit and APM lines. Grounded via F5 community/K-article snippets.

catalog.name: f5-telemetry-streaming-json
catalog.product: F5 Telemetry Streaming (TS) event listener JSON — LTM request log, ASM, APM, AFM, AVR, system poller
catalog.sample_line: {"event_source":"request_logging","event_timestamp":"2022-09-27T06:02:48.000Z","hostname":"hostname","client_ip":"216.160.83.56","server_ip":"89.160.20.128","http_method":"GET","http_uri":"/","virtual_name":"/Common/app.app/app_vs","tenant":"Common","application":"app.app","telemetryEventCategory":"LTM"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON object containing key telemetryEventCategory (values LTM/ASM/APM/AFM/AVR/systemInfo) — unique to F5 TS. ASM variant carries support_id/violations, APM carries errdefs_msgno like "01490102:5:" + Access_Profile, AFM carries acl_policy_name/acl_rule_name.
catalog.fields: telemetryEventCategory routes sub-schema; common: hostname, tenant, application, event_timestamp/f5telemetry_timestamp; per-category HTTP/violation/session/ACL fields
catalog.notes: One adapter can fan out on telemetryEventCategory. Samples verbatim from Elastic f5_bigip pipeline tests (ltm/asm/apm/afm files).

catalog.name: fail2ban
catalog.sample_line: 2023-02-17 23:44:17,037 fail2ban.actions        [992]: NOTICE  [apache-auth] Ban 45.91.244.228
catalog.detect_signature: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm' + a 'fail2ban.<module>' token + '[pid]:' + level + '[jail] Ban/Unban/Found <ip>'
catalog.fields: ts(comma-ms)->ts_ms; fail2ban.<module>->source; NOTICE/INFO/WARNING->level; [jail]->category; Ban/Unban/Found + ip->data
catalog.notes: Python-logging-derived but with the distinctive fail2ban.<module> + [jail] structure. Actions of interest: Found (detect), Ban, Unban, Restore Ban, already banned. CrowdSec (its successor) emits its own JSON+text format — separate adapter.

catalog.name: fhir-auditevent-json
catalog.product: FHIR AuditEvent resources (R4/R5) — HAPI FHIR, Medplum, IHE BALP RESTful ATNA feed (ITI-20 FHIR option), SMART-on-FHIR servers
catalog.sample_line: {"resourceType":"AuditEvent","id":"example","code":{"coding":[{"system":"http://dicom.nema.org/resources/ontology/DCM","code":"110120","display":"Application Start"}]},"recorded":"2012-10-25T22:04:27+11:00","agent":[{"role":[{"text":"Service User (Logon)"}],"who":{"identifier":{"value":"Grahame"}},"requestor":false}]}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with "resourceType":"AuditEvent"; also appears wrapped in FHIR Bundle entries (resourceType Bundle containing entry[].resource.resourceType==AuditEvent) and in NDJSON bulk exports
catalog.fields: recorded -> ts (ISO8601); type/subtype (R4) or code/category (R5) DCM codes -> category; outcome (0=success,4/8/12 failure) -> level; agent[].who -> user; source.observer -> source; entity[]/object[] -> affected resources (patient, query); id -> trace_id fallback
catalog.notes: Verified against hl7.org/fhir/auditevent-example.json.html. R4 uses type+subtype+outcome code; R5 restructured to category+code+outcome.code — adapter must handle both. This is the modern replacement for ATNA XML in IHE BALP.

catalog.name: firebird-server-log
catalog.sample_line:
X8000 (Client)	Thu Jan 21 13:06:51 2010
	INET/inet_error: connect errno = 10061
catalog.detect_signature: Header line ^hostname[ (Client|Server)]?\t?ctime-date$ followed by tab-indented message line(s), blank line between records; message subsystems INET/inet_error, XNET, REMOTE INTERFACE, 'Database: <path>'
catalog.fields: hostname, role (Client/Server, optional), timestamp (ctime, no tz), message (indented, may be multiple lines; errno codes)
catalog.notes: Verbatim real firebird.log from GitHub (reportman-delphi repo). Record = host+date header then indented body — same family as OpenEdge date-header style

catalog.name: flink-log4j2

catalog.fields: ts(comma millis), level, logger FQCN, message; job id (32-hex), attempt/execution ids, lifecycle 'Starting/Registering' events; multi-line stack traces on failures
catalog.notes: Default log4j2 pattern %d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSS} %-5p %-60c %x - %m. Verified from Flink docs + GCP Ops Agent flink parser. Also emitted per-container under YARN/K8s.

catalog.name: fluentbit-internal

catalog.notes: Grounded via docs.fluentbit.io. Google Cloud Ops Agent's logging subagent emits identical lines.

catalog.name: fluentd-internal
catalog.sample_line: 2023-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 [info]: #0 fluentd worker is now running worker=0

catalog.name: flux-controller-zap-json

catalog.name: fortigate-traffic-kv

catalog.name: fortinet_fortigate
catalog.sample_line: date=2026-01-24 time=12:30:01 devname="FGT60F" devid="FGT60F0000000000" logid="0000000013" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="notice" vd="root" srcip=203.0.113.5 srcport=51882 dstip=198.51.100.9 dstport=443 action="accept" policyid=7 service="HTTPS" sentbyte=840 rcvdbyte=1320

catalog.name: freebsd_messages
catalog.sample_line: Jul 20 14:03:11 fbsdhost kernel: ada0: <Samsung SSD 870 SVQ01B6Q> ACS-4 ATA SATA 3.x device
catalog.detect_signature: rfc3164 shape; kernel tag 'kernel:'; BSD device names (ada0, em0, cam)
catalog.fields: ts=BSD local; host; tag (kernel/daemon)[pid]; message
catalog.notes: BSD device-driver messages (ada/da/em/re/cam). newsyslog rotates. Boot dmesg lines may lack timestamp (raw kernel probe output) when read via dmesg(8).

catalog.name: freertos_logging
catalog.sample_line: 12.045.678 [Tmr Svc      ] MQTT connection established
catalog.detect_signature: Format '%4u.%03u.%03u [%-10s] msg' when configLOGGING_INCLUDE_TIME_AND_TASK_NAME=1: sec.ms.us then bracketed 10-char task name
catalog.fields: ts_ms=sec.ms.us since boot; source=task name (padded, inside []); data.message=remainder
catalog.notes: Time-and-task prefix is optional (config flag). Without it, output is raw printf. Amazon FreeRTOS uses LogInfo/LogError/LogWarn/LogDebug macros that prepend [INFO]/[ERROR]/[WARN]/[DEBUG]. Source: freertos.org/logging.html, aws/amazon-freertos logging task.

catalog.name: freeswitch-logfile
