catalog.fields: P<pid>, T<tid> (or T<0xhex>), frames file:function:line, trailing metric (time in us, or memory with -m)
catalog.notes: Austin's own collapsed variant. `-p` per-process, memory mode appends +/- byte deltas. Feeds austin-python/flamegraph.

catalog.name: auth0-logs
catalog.product: Auth0 tenant log events (Management API / log streams)
catalog.sample_line: {"_id":"5ef3bb0a72487a0047c32959","date":"2020-06-24T20:43:54.159Z","type":"s","description":"Successful login","connection":"Username-Password-Authentication","connection_id":"con_16Tpc6YqlWZ4HCut","client_id":"9ZteveEZ8CqSLtCNXgvhoCJQ0jt2"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with short mnemonic "type" code (s, f, fp, fu, seccft, slo, sapi...) + date + connection_id/client_id
catalog.fields: _id/log_id, date, type (code table), description, connection, client_id/client_name, ip, user_agent, user_id, user_name, details{}
catalog.notes: Type codes documented at auth0.com/docs/logs/log-event-type-codes; adapter needs the code->name table

catalog.name: auth_secure_log
catalog.sample_line: Jul 20 14:03:11 myhost sshd[1234]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 10.0.0.5 port 55221 ssh2
catalog.detect_signature: rfc3164 shape with security tags sshd/sudo/su/PAM/polkitd
catalog.fields: ts=BSD; host; program[pid]; message (semantic: 'Failed password', 'Accepted', 'session opened')
catalog.notes: Structurally rfc3164 but semantically security-relevant; worth its own category tag for auth event extraction. Related to auditd (already covered).

catalog.name: aws-apigateway-access-json
catalog.product: Amazon API Gateway access logs (JSON $context template)
catalog.sample_line: {"requestId":"a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-EXAMPLE11111","ip":"192.0.2.1","requestTime":"20/Jul/2026:10:00:00 +0000","httpMethod":"GET","routeKey":"GET /items","status":"200","protocol":"HTTP/1.1","responseLength":"1024","extendedRequestId":"AbCdEfGhIAMEp="}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with requestTime in CLF-date form (dd/MMM/yyyy:HH:mm:ss Z) plus routeKey/extendedRequestId or the common requestId+ip+httpMethod+status quartet; user-defined so detect on AWS's documented default template keys
catalog.fields: requestId, ip, requestTime, httpMethod, routeKey/resourcePath, status, protocol, responseLength, extendedRequestId, optional responseLatency/integrationLatency/userAgent/errorMessage
catalog.notes: Format is customer-defined from $context variables; AWS docs give this canonical JSON template and a CLF-style alternative ('$context.identity.sourceIp $context.identity.caller ... [$context.requestTime] "$context.httpMethod $context.resourcePath $context.protocol" $context.status $context.responseLength $context.requestId'). Parse defensively: keys vary, values are strings.

catalog.name: aws-aurora-mysql-audit-csv
catalog.product: Amazon Aurora MySQL Advanced Auditing audit logs
catalog.sample_line: 1646766494550603,ip-10-21-0-160,admin,10.0.2.44,102,922,QUERY,mydb,'SELECT * FROM account_totals',0
catalog.detect_signature: CSV row: 16-digit unix-microsecond timestamp, hostname, user, host/ip, connectionid, queryid, event token CONNECT|QUERY|TABLE_ACCESS_DATA|DISCONNECT, db, quoted SQL, retcode
catalog.fields: timestamp(us)->ts, serverhost, username, host, connection_id, query_id, operation, database, query->data.message, retcode->level(nonzero=warn)
catalog.notes: audit.log files via download or CloudWatch Logs export. Aurora advanced auditing variant; RDS MariaDB audit plugin is the sibling below.

catalog.name: aws-backup-job-event
catalog.product: AWS Backup — EventBridge 'Backup Job State Change' / CloudWatch events (JSON)
catalog.sample_line: {"version":"0","source":"aws.backup","detail-type":"Backup Job State Change","time":"2026-07-21T02:00:01Z","detail":{"backupJobId":"1b2f23c5-ex-ample","state":"COMPLETED","resourceArn":"arn:aws:ec2:us-east-1:123456789012:volume/vol-0ab","backupVaultName":"Default"}}
catalog.detect_signature: EventBridge envelope with source == "aws.backup" and detail-type containing 'Backup Job'|'Restore Job'|'Copy Job' State Change
catalog.fields: time, detail-type → category, detail.backupJobId → trace_id, detail.state → level mapping (FAILED/ABORTED=error, EXPIRED=warn, COMPLETED=info), resourceArn, vault
catalog.notes: Envelope shape is standard EventBridge (already partially covered by gcp/aws envelopes? aws EventBridge generic is NOT in known list); state vocabulary documented in AWS Backup monitoring docs.

catalog.name: aws-cdk-deploy-events
catalog.product: AWS CDK cdk deploy progress output
catalog.sample_line: MyStack | 3/5 | 12:26:36 PM | CREATE_COMPLETE      | AWS::S3::Bucket    | MyBucket (MyBucket1234)
catalog.detect_signature: pipe-separated columns: stack | n/total | locale time | CFN status (CREATE_IN_PROGRESS/CREATE_COMPLETE/UPDATE_ROLLBACK_...) | AWS::Service::Type | logical id; plus banner lines '✅  MyStack' and 'MyStack: deploying... [1/1]'
catalog.fields: stack, progress n/total, time, cloudformation status, resource type, logical/physical id

catalog.name: aws-clientvpn-connection-log
catalog.product: AWS Client VPN connection logs (CloudWatch Logs)
catalog.sample_line: {"connection-log-type":"connection-attempt","connection-attempt-status":"successful","client-vpn-endpoint-id":"cvpn-endpoint-0123456789abcdef0","connection-id":"cvpn-connection-0123456789abcdef0","username":"alice","connection-start-time":"2023-01-15 12:00:00","client-ip":"10.0.0.34"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with 'connection-log-type' + 'client-vpn-endpoint-id' hyphenated keys
catalog.fields: connection-log-type (connection-attempt/connection-reset), connection-attempt-status, endpoint/connection ids, username, client-ip, ingress/egress-bytes, connection-duration-seconds
catalog.notes: Hyphenated (not camelCase) keys are the AWS quirk here; arrives via CloudWatch envelope.

catalog.name: aws-config-configuration-item-json
catalog.sample_line: {"configurationItemVersion":"1.3","configurationItemCaptureTime":"2016-02-17T01:36:34.043Z","configurationStateId":1455672994043,"configurationItemStatus":"OK","resourceType":"AWS::EC2::Instance","resourceId":"i-1a2b3c4d","arn":"arn:aws:ec2:us-west-2:123456789012:instance/i-1a2b3c4d","awsRegion":"us-west-2","availabilityZone":"us-west-2a","awsAccountId":"123456789012","configurationStateMd5Hash":"8f1ee69b287895a0f8bc5753eEXAMPLE","resourceCreationTime":"2016-01-16T03:05:34.000Z","tags":{},"relationships":[],"configuration":{"instanceType":"t2.micro"}}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with configurationItemVersion + configurationItemCaptureTime + resourceType starting "AWS::"; snapshot files wrap in {"fileVersion":"1.0","configurationItems":[...]}
catalog.fields: configurationItemCaptureTime->ts, resourceType+resourceId+configurationItemStatus->data.message, awsAccountId, awsRegion, configuration diff payload
catalog.notes: Status ResourceDeleted/ResourceNotRecorded worth level=warn. category=cloud-config.

catalog.name: aws-eventbridge-event-json
catalog.product: Amazon EventBridge / CloudWatch Events event envelope
catalog.sample_line: {"version":"0","id":"6a7e8feb-b491-4cf7-a9f1-bf3703467718","detail-type":"EC2 Instance State-change Notification","source":"aws.ec2","account":"111122223333","time":"2017-12-22T18:43:48Z","region":"us-west-1","resources":["arn:aws:ec2:us-west-1:123456789012:instance/i-1234567890abcdef0"],"detail":{"instance-id":"i-1234567890abcdef0","state":"terminated"}}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with version=="0" + "detail-type" + source starting "aws." (or custom) + account + detail object
catalog.fields: time->ts, detail-type->data.message, source->source, account, region, resources[], id->trace_id, detail payload passthrough
catalog.notes: Envelope for GuardDuty/Config/Health/etc when routed via EventBridge - detect inner detail and chain adapters.

catalog.name: aws-network-firewall-alert-json
catalog.product: AWS Network Firewall alert/flow logs (Suricata EVE wrapped in AWS envelope)
catalog.sample_line: {"firewall_name":"test-firewall","availability_zone":"us-east-1b","event_timestamp":"1602627001","event":{"timestamp":"2020-10-13T22:10:01.006481+0000","flow_id":1582438383425873,"event_type":"alert","src_ip":"203.0.113.4","src_port":55555,"dest_ip":"192.0.2.16","dest_port":111,"proto":"TCP","alert":{"action":"allowed","signature_id":5,"signature":"test_tcp","category":"","severity":1}}}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with firewall_name + availability_zone + event_timestamp + nested event.event_type (alert|netflow)
catalog.fields: event_timestamp->ts, firewall_name->source, event.* delegated to suricata-eve semantics (src/dest ip+port, alert.signature->data.message, severity->level)
catalog.notes: Envelope around Suricata EVE (already covered) - unwrap .event and reuse the suricata-eve mapper.

catalog.name: aws-nlb-access-log
catalog.product: AWS Network Load Balancer access logs (TLS listeners)
catalog.sample_line: tls 2.0 2018-12-20T02:59:40 net/my-network-loadbalancer/c6e77e28c25b2234 g3d4b5e8bb8464cd 72.21.218.154:51341 172.100.100.185:443 5 2 98 246 - arn:aws:acm:us-east-2:671290407336:certificate/2a108f19-aded-46b0-8493-c63eb1ef4a99 - ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA tlsv12 - my-network-loadbalancer-c6e77e28c25b2234.elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com - - - 2018-12-20T02:59:30
catalog.detect_signature: First tokens literally "tls 2.0" then ISO8601 and net/<name>/<id> resource id
catalog.fields: type, version, time->ts, elb, listener, client:port, destination:port, connection_time_ms, tls_handshake_time_ms, received/sent_bytes, incoming_tls_alert, chosen_cert_arn, tls_cipher, tls_protocol_version, tls_keyexchange, domain_name(SNI), alpn fe/be/preference, tls_connection_creation_time
catalog.notes: Sample verbatim from AWS docs (joined to one line). Connection-level, not request-level; TLS-only.

catalog.name: aws-redshift-connection-log
catalog.product: Amazon Redshift audit logging - connection log (pipe-delimited)
catalog.detect_signature: Pipe-delimited line whose first field is a connection event word (initiating session|authenticated|disconnecting session|authentication failure) and second is "Day, DD Mon YYYY HH:MM:SS:mmm"
catalog.fields: event, recordtime->ts, remotehost, remoteport, pid, dbname, username, authmethod, duration, sslversion, sslcipher, mtu, application_name
catalog.notes: Delivered to S3 as connectionlog_*.gz. authentication failure -> level=warn.

catalog.name: aws-redshift-useractivity-log
catalog.product: Amazon Redshift audit logging - user activity log
catalog.sample_line: '2023-06-26T18:02:47Z UTC [ db=dev user=awsuser pid=26189 userid=100 xid=712798 ]' LOG: SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10;
catalog.detect_signature: Line starting 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ UTC [ db= user= pid= userid= xid= ]' followed by "LOG:" and SQL; statements may span multiple lines
catalog.fields: timestamp->ts, db, user, pid, userid, xid->trace_id, SQL text->data.message
catalog.notes: Multiline SQL: continuation lines lack the bracket header - join until next header. useractivitylog_*.gz files.

catalog.name: aws-securityhub-asff-json
catalog.product: AWS Security Hub findings (ASFF - AWS Security Finding Format)
catalog.sample_line: {"SchemaVersion":"2018-10-08","Id":"arn:aws:securityhub:us-west-2:123456789012:subscription/pci-dss/v/3.2.1/PCI.Lambda.2/finding/01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef","ProductArn":"arn:aws:securityhub:us-west-2::product/aws/securityhub","GeneratorId":"pci-dss/v/3.2.1/PCI.Lambda.2","AwsAccountId":"123456789012","Types":["Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/PCI-DSS"],"CreatedAt":"2020-06-02T02:15:29.442Z","UpdatedAt":"2020-06-09T22:26:44.483Z","Severity":{"Product":40,"Label":"MEDIUM","Normalized":40},"Title":"PCI.Lambda.2 Lambda functions should be in a VPC","Description":"...","Resources":[{"Type":"AwsLambdaFunction","Id":"arn:aws:lambda:..."}],"Compliance":{"Status":"FAILED"},"RecordState":"ACTIVE"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with SchemaVersion=="2018-10-08" + ProductArn containing :securityhub: + Severity.Label + AwsAccountId (PascalCase keys)
catalog.fields: UpdatedAt->ts, Severity.Label->level, Title->data.message, Types, Resources[].Id, Compliance.Status, Workflow.Status, Id->trace_id
catalog.notes: Normalized findings hub - PascalCase distinguishes it from GuardDuty native. Also the OCSF successor exists (Security Lake) but ASFF still dominates.

catalog.name: aws_vpc_flow
catalog.product: AWS VPC Flow Logs (default v2 space-delimited)
catalog.detect_signature: space-delimited with leading version '2' then account-id + 'eni-' interface id; positional: version account interface srcaddr dstaddr srcport dstport protocol packets bytes start end action log-status
catalog.fields: start/end epoch->ts; srcaddr/dstaddr/srcport/dstport/protocol->data; action(ACCEPT/REJECT)->data.action+level; account/eni->source
catalog.notes: Default v2 has 14 positional fields; custom formats reorder/add fields (region, az, tcp-flags, pkt-srcaddr) so a header/format hint helps. REJECT lines are the security signal. Delivered via CloudWatch Logs or S3.

catalog.name: azure-appgateway-access-log
catalog.sample_line: {"timeStamp":"2017-04-26T19:27:38+00:00","resourceId":"/SUBSCRIPTIONS/<sub>/RESOURCEGROUPS/PEERINGTEST/PROVIDERS/MICROSOFT.NETWORK/APPLICATIONGATEWAYS/{applicationGatewayName}","operationName":"ApplicationGatewayAccess","category":"ApplicationGatewayAccessLog","properties":{"instanceId":"appgw_1","clientIP":"191.96.249.97","clientPort":46886,"httpMethod":"GET","requestUri":"/phpmyadmin/scripts/setup.php","userAgent":"-","httpStatus":404,"httpVersion":"HTTP/1.0","receivedBytes":65,"sentBytes":553,"timeTaken":205,"sslEnabled":"off","host":"www.contoso.com","originalHost":"www.contoso.com"}}
catalog.detect_signature: Diagnostic record with category=="ApplicationGatewayAccessLog" (siblings: ApplicationGatewayPerformanceLog, ApplicationGatewayFirewallLog)
catalog.fields: timeStamp->ts, properties.clientIP/httpMethod/requestUri/httpStatus->level/timeTaken/host/serverRouted/transactionId->trace_id
catalog.notes: WAF sibling category ApplicationGatewayFirewallLog has ruleId/message/action - worth handling in same adapter family.

catalog.name: azure-firewall-rule-log
catalog.product: Azure Firewall network/application rule logs (diagnostic records, message-in-properties)
catalog.sample_line: {"time":"2018-06-14T01:44:11.0000000Z","category":"AzureFirewallNetworkRule","resourceId":"/SUBSCRIPTIONS/<sub>/RESOURCEGROUPS/MYRG/PROVIDERS/MICROSOFT.NETWORK/AZUREFIREWALLS/MYFW","operationName":"AzureFirewallNetworkRuleLog","properties":{"msg":"TCP request from 10.1.0.4:52623 to 13.69.65.17:443. Action: Allow."}}
catalog.detect_signature: Diagnostic record with category AzureFirewallNetworkRule|AzureFirewallApplicationRule|AzureFirewallDnsProxy and properties.msg free-text "<proto> request from <ip:port> to <ip:port>. Action: <Allow|Deny>"
catalog.fields: time->ts, parse properties.msg regex -> proto/src/dst/action(Deny=warn); newer "structured logs" variant puts fields directly in properties (sourceIp, destPort, action, policy/ruleCollection/rule)
catalog.notes: Two generations: legacy msg-string and resource-specific structured tables (AZFWNetworkRule etc). Handle both.

catalog.name: azure-frontdoor-access
catalog.product: Azure Front Door access log (Azure Monitor diagnostic-setting JSON)
catalog.sample_line: {"time":"2026-07-20T10:00:00.0000000Z","category":"FrontDoorAccessLog","operationName":"Microsoft.Cdn/Profiles/AccessLog/Write","properties":{"trackingReference":"0mMxsXwAAAABEalekYeI4S55qpi5R7R0/V1NURURHRTA4MTIAZGI4NGQzZDgtNWQ5Ny00","httpMethod":"GET","httpVersion":"2.0","requestUri":"https://www.example.com/","requestBytes":"1234","responseBytes":"5678","userAgent":"Mozilla/5.0","clientIp":"192.0.2.1","pop":"WSTEDGE0812","httpStatusCode":"200","timeTaken":"0.02","routingRuleName":"myroute","cacheStatus":"HIT"}}
catalog.detect_signature: Azure diagnostic envelope: JSON with category=='FrontDoorAccessLog' (or FrontDoorWebApplicationFirewallLog/FrontDoorHealthProbeLog) and properties.trackingReference + properties.pop
catalog.fields: time, category, resourceId, operationName, properties.{trackingReference,httpMethod,httpVersion,requestUri,clientIp,clientPort,userAgent,pop,httpStatusCode,requestBytes,responseBytes,timeTaken,securityProtocol,routingRuleName,cacheStatus,originUrl,originIp}
catalog.notes: Delivered via Azure Monitor diagnostic settings (Event Hub / Storage / Log Analytics), records batched under a top-level {"records":[...]} array. trackingReference == X-Azure-Ref header → trace_id. Same envelope pattern covers Azure CDN (Microsoft) access logs.

catalog.name: azure-functions-appinsights
catalog.product: Azure Functions → Application Insights traces (Kusto export JSON)
catalog.sample_line: {"timestamp":"2023-06-08T06:08:14.123Z","message":"Executed 'Functions.approval' (Succeeded, Id=9a3eeb87-8f4a-4a17-84c6-9e8e5f51312b, Duration=21110ms)","severityLevel":1,"operation_Id":"5eca8f170d9ded26b7c1e5f78e5aa2ec","operation_Name":"approval","cloud_RoleName":"my-func-app","customDimensions":{"Category":"Function.approval","InvocationId":"9a3eeb87-8f4a-4a17-84c6-9e8e5f51312b","LogLevel":"Information"}}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with severityLevel (0-4 int) + operation_Id + cloud_RoleName + customDimensions.Category (Function.* / Host.* / Worker.*) — the App Insights traces-table shape
catalog.fields: timestamp, message, severityLevel (0=Verbose..4=Critical), operation_Id (trace), operation_Name, cloud_RoleName, customDimensions.{Category,InvocationId,HostInstanceId,LogLevel}
catalog.notes: This is how Azure Functions logs land when exported/queried from Application Insights (continuous export, Log Analytics, REST). severityLevel int must be mapped to level names; operation_Id maps to trace_id.

catalog.name: azure-servicebus-operational-json
catalog.product: Azure Service Bus resource logs — OperationalLogs (AzureDiagnostics / AZMSOperationalLogs)
catalog.sample_line: {"ActivityId":"0000000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000000000","EventName":"Create Queue","resourceId":"/SUBSCRIPTIONS/.../PROVIDERS/MICROSOFT.SERVICEBUS/NAMESPACES/NS","SubscriptionId":"...","EventTimeString":"9/28/2016 8:40:06 PM +00:00","EventProperties":"{\"Namespace\":\"mynamespace\",...}","Status":"Succeeded","Caller":"ServiceBus Client","category":"OperationalLogs"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with category/type OperationalLogs|AZMSOperationalLogs and resourceId containing MICROSOFT.SERVICEBUS
catalog.fields: ActivityId (trace_id), EventName (mgmt op), resourceId, SubscriptionId, EventTimeString or TimeGenerated(UTC), EventProperties (nested JSON string!), Status, Caller, Provider
catalog.notes: Samples quoted verbatim from learn.microsoft.com monitor-service-bus-reference. EventProperties is a JSON-escaped string needing second-level parse. US-style datetime '9/28/2016 8:40:06 PM +00:00'. Event Hubs/Relay emit the sibling AZMS* tables with the same envelope.

catalog.name: azure-storage-analytics-log
catalog.product: Azure Storage Analytics classic logs ($logs container, semicolon-delimited)
catalog.sample_line: 1.0;2014-06-19T22:59:23.1967767Z;GetBlob;AnonymousSuccess;200;17;16;anonymous;;storagesample;blob;"https://storagesample.blob.core.windows.net/sample-container1/00001.txt";"/storagesample/sample-container1/00001.txt";61d2e3f6-bcb7-4cd1-a81e-4f8f497f0da2;0;192.100.0.102:4362;2014-02-14;283;0;354;23;0;;;"0x8D15A2913C934DE";Thursday, 19-Jun-14 22:58:10 GMT;;"WA-Storage/4.0.1 (.NET CLR 4.0.30319.34014; Win32NT 6.3.9600.0)";;"44dfd78e-7288-4898-8f70-c3478983d3b6"
catalog.detect_signature: Semicolon-delimited line starting "1.0;" or "2.0;" then ISO8601 then storage operation name (GetBlob/PutBlob/ListBlobs...) then auth-status word
catalog.fields: version, request-start-time->ts, operation-type, request-status->level, http-status, e2e/server-latency-ms, authentication, account, service, request-url, request-id->trace_id, client-ip:port, user-agent
catalog.notes: Legacy but widely retained for blob/table/queue access auditing; v2 appends AAD auth fields at end.

catalog.name: azure-vpngateway-diagnostics
catalog.product: Azure VPN Gateway diagnostic logs (Azure Monitor)
catalog.sample_line: {"time":"2023-01-15T12:00:00.0000000Z","resourceId":"/SUBSCRIPTIONS/…/VIRTUALNETWORKGATEWAYS/MYGW","category":"TunnelDiagnosticLog","operationName":"TunnelConnected","instance":"GatewayTenantWorker_IN_0","remoteIP":"203.0.113.5"}
catalog.detect_signature: AzureDiagnostics JSON with category in {GatewayDiagnosticLog, TunnelDiagnosticLog, RouteDiagnosticLog, IKEDiagnosticLog, P2SDiagnosticLog}
catalog.fields: time, resourceId, category, operationName (TunnelConnected/TunnelDisconnected), instance, remoteIP, message (IKE payload dumps in IKEDiagnosticLog)
catalog.notes: Five sub-categories share the Azure Monitor envelope; IKEDiagnosticLog messages embed raw IKE trace text worth secondary parsing.

catalog.name: bacula-bareos-job-report
catalog.product: Bacula/Bareos end-of-job summary report (emailed or appended to log: 'JobId:', 'Elapsed time:', 'Termination: Backup OK')
catalog.sample_line: Termination:            Backup OK
catalog.detect_signature: Multi-line block: aligned 'Key:   value' pairs including 'JobId:', 'Backup Level:', 'FD Bytes Written:', ending 'Termination:' — detect block start '(Build OS|JobId):' after a 'bacula-dir JobId' line
catalog.fields: job_id, client, fileset, level (Full/Incremental/Differential), start/end time, SD/FD bytes, rate, compression, volume names, termination status → level (OK=info, 'Backup Error'/'*** Backup Error ***'=error)
catalog.notes: Parse as a single multi-line event whose Termination field sets level; the richest single record in the Bacula family.

catalog.name: barman-log
catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-21 02:00:01,123 [12345] barman.server INFO: Starting backup using postgres method for server pg (backup_id: 20260721T020001)
catalog.detect_signature: Python-logging line whose logger name starts 'barman.': ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3} \[\d+\] barman\.\w+ (DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR):
catalog.fields: ts (comma-ms), pid, logger (barman.server/barman.backup → category), level, message; backup_id token = trace_id
catalog.notes: Standard python logging with barman.* logger namespace as the discriminator.

catalog.name: bigquery-audit-metadata
catalog.product: Google BigQuery audit logs (Cloud Logging export, BigQueryAuditMetadata)
catalog.sample_line: {"protoPayload":{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.audit.AuditLog","serviceName":"bigquery.googleapis.com","methodName":"google.cloud.bigquery.v2.JobService.InsertJob","metadata":{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.bigquery.logging.v1.BigQueryAuditMetadata","jobChange":{"job":{"jobName":"projects/p/jobs/j1","jobStats":{"queryStats":{"totalBilledBytes":"1048576"}}}}}},"resource":{"type":"bigquery_project"},"timestamp":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
catalog.detect_signature: LogEntry with protoPayload.serviceName="bigquery.googleapis.com" and metadata @type ending BigQueryAuditMetadata (legacy variant: protoPayload.metadata @type AuditData with jobCompletedEvent)
catalog.fields: timestamp, severity, resource.type/labels, protoPayload.methodName, authenticationInfo.principalEmail, jobChange.job.jobName/jobConfig/jobStats(query text, billed bytes, slot ms), tableDataRead/tableDataChange events
catalog.notes: Rides inside the already-covered gcp-logentry-envelope; needs a payload-level sub-adapter keyed on the @type. jobName is the natural trace_id.

catalog.name: bind-named-general-log
catalog.sample_line: 20-Jul-2026 10:15:32.101 general: info: zone example.com/IN: loaded serial 2026072001
catalog.detect_signature: line = 'dd-Mon-YYYY HH:MM:SS.mmm <category>: <severity>: <message>' with category in {general,xfer-in,xfer-out,notify,security,lame-servers,resolver,dnssec,database,client}; distinguish from querylog by absence of ': query:'
catalog.fields: timestamp, category, severity(critical/error/warning/notice/info/debug N), free-text message (zone events, transfers 'transfer of ...', denied queries)
catalog.notes: One adapter can cover all non-query named categories; also appears syslog-wrapped as 'named[pid]:'.

catalog.name: bind-rpz-log
catalog.product: ISC BIND 9 named (rpz category / response policy zones)
catalog.sample_line: 17-Mar-2020 09:34:49.887 rpz: info: client 192.168.123.10#53112 (casasur.cl): rpz QNAME NODATA rewrite casasur.cl via casasur.cl.phishy.di000001.rpz.threatstop.local
catalog.detect_signature: substring ': rpz QNAME ' or ': rpz IP/NSDNAME/NSIP ' + 'rewrite ... via ...'; category token 'rpz:'
catalog.fields: timestamp, category(rpz), severity, client ip#port, qname, rpz trigger type (QNAME/IP/NSDNAME/NSIP/CLIENT-IP), policy action (NXDOMAIN/NODATA/Local-Data/PASSTHRU/DROP), rewritten name, matching rpz zone
catalog.notes: Security-relevant (DNS firewall hits). Same channel framing as other named categories.

catalog.name: bird-log
catalog.product: BIRD Internet Routing Daemon (v1/v2/v3) log file
catalog.sample_line: 2019-06-19 17:47:03.822 <TRACE> bgp1: Connect delayed by 5 seconds
catalog.detect_signature: ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.mmm]' then log class in angle brackets <TRACE|INFO|WARN|ERR|FATAL|DBG|BUG|AUTH|RMT> then 'protocol_name:'
catalog.fields: ts (docs: default 'iso long ms'), class, protocol/instance name, message
catalog.notes: Classes verified from bird.network.cz docs (info/warning/error/fatal/debug/trace/remote/auth/bug); file destination renders class in <>. Widely used at IXP route servers.

catalog.name: bitdefender-gravityzone-cef
catalog.product: Bitdefender GravityZone (endpoint events, syslog CEF / push notifications)
catalog.sample_line: CEF:0|Bitdefender|GravityZone|6.0|av|Antimalware Event|8|dvchost=win-desktop01 duser=jdoe filePath=C:\Users\jdoe\evil.exe cs1=Trojan.GenericKD.12345 cs1Label=malwareName cs2=file cs2Label=malwareType act=blocked
catalog.detect_signature: CEF header vendor "Bitdefender" product "GravityZone"; event class short codes (av, aph=anti-phishing, fw, uc, dp=data-protection); cs*Label=malwareName/malwareType
catalog.fields: CEF header (vendor=Bitdefender, product=GravityZone), dvchost, duser, filePath, cs1=malwareName, cs2=malwareType, act, plus module-code event class

catalog.name: bpftrace JSON output

catalog.name: brocade-fos-raslog-errdump

catalog.fields: ts, msg_id, sequence_number, fabric_id, severity, switch_name, message
catalog.notes: Structure attested by pyfos (brocade/pyfos pyfos_brocade_logging.py) and BROCADE-MAPS-MIB in librenms; same raslogd CSV framing as verified AUDIT lines minus the AUDIT prefix. Sample reconstructed from that structure — capture a fixture from a real errdump before finalizing the parser.

catalog.name: busybox_syslogd
catalog.sample_line: Jul 20 14:03:11 hostname user.info kernel: eth0: link up

catalog.name: carbonblack-cloud-data-forwarder-json

catalog.name: carbonblack-edr-event-forwarder-leef

catalog.name: celery_worker
catalog.sample_line:
[2026-07-21 15:40:39,123: INFO/MainProcess] Task app.tasks.add[1a2b-...] received

catalog.name: checkpoint
catalog.sample_line: <134>1 2023-05-01T12:00:00Z gw CheckPoint 1234 - [action:"Accept"; flags:"..."; src:"10.0.0.5"; dst:"8.8.8.8"; proto:"17"; service:"53"; rule:"5"; product:"VPN-1 & FireWall-1"]

catalog.fields: action, src, dst, proto, service, rule, product, origin -> data; Drop/Reject->WARN
catalog.notes: Log Exporter emits multiple targets; native form is semicolon key:"value". CEF and JSON exports also common — prefer detecting the CheckPoint field set (product:, rule:) over envelope.

catalog.name: checkpoint_fw
catalog.sample_line: <134>1 2026-01-24T12:31:00Z cpmgmt CheckPoint 12345 - [action:"Accept"; flags:"..."; src:"203.0.113.5"; dst:"198.51.100.9"; proto:"6"; service:"443"; rule_name:"web-allow"; product:"VPN-1 & FireWall-1"]

catalog.fields: 5424 ts->ts; action/src/dst/proto/service/rule_name->data; product->source
catalog.notes: Log Exporter emits Splunk (key:value; semicolon), CEF, or LEEF. The 'key:"value";' semicolon grammar is Check Point specific and differs from CEF/LEEF pipe grammar — may need a mode branch.

catalog.name: chef-run-doc-output

catalog.name: chroma-server-log

catalog.notes: Verbatim from chroma-core/chroma issues. Newer Chroma (Rust core) also emits tracing-style lines — recheck when bumping versions.

catalog.name: cisco-anyconnect-client-log

catalog.sample_line: Function: ConnectMgr::processIfcData File: .\ConnectMgr.cpp Line: 2168 Invoked Function: ConnectMgr::initiateConnect Return Code: 0 (0x00000000) Description: unknown
catalog.detect_signature: 'Function:' + 'File:' + 'Line:' + 'Return Code:' key sequence in one event body; Event provider 'Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client' / 'Cisco Secure Client'
catalog.fields: function, source file, line, invoked function, return code (dec+hex), description
catalog.notes: Client-side counterpart to the already-covered ASA syslog; on Windows it rides EVTX transport, DART zips contain the same bodies as plain text.

catalog.name: cisco-cucm-cdr-csv
catalog.sample_line: 1,1,1234567,25631,"203.0.113.10",1767608772,1001,"1001",... (after 2 header rows: field-name row starting "cdrRecordType","globalCallID_callManagerId","globalCallID_callId",... and a type row INTEGER,INTEGER,...)
catalog.detect_signature: first line starts "cdrRecordType","globalCallID_callManagerId" (CDR) or "cmrRecordType" (CMR); second line is a comma list of INTEGER/VARCHAR type tokens
catalog.fields: ~130 columns: globalCallID_*, dateTimeOrigination/Connect/Disconnect (epoch), callingPartyNumber, originalCalledPartyNumber, orig/destCause_value (Q.850), duration, origDeviceName/destDeviceName
catalog.notes: cdr_/cmr_ prefixed files. globalCallID_callId -> trace_id; Q.850 cause values map to level.

catalog.name: cisco-dhcp-snooping-syslog
catalog.sample_line: %DHCP_SNOOPING-5-DHCP_SNOOPING_MATCH_MAC_FAIL: DHCP_SNOOPING drop message because the chaddr doesn't match source mac, message type: DHCPRELEASE, chaddr: 4e4d.ab54.bdf1, MAC sa: 0015.587f.effe
catalog.detect_signature: '%DHCP_SNOOPING-<sev>-<MNEMONIC>:' token (MATCH_MAC_FAIL, UNTRUSTED_PORT, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ERRDISABLE_WARNING, AGENT_OPERATION_FAILED...)
catalog.fields: facility, severity digit, mnemonic, dhcp message type, chaddr (cisco dotted mac), source mac, interface, vlan
catalog.notes: Rides the generic Cisco IOS syslog frame but the DHCP_SNOOPING payload grammar (chaddr vs MAC sa, message type) deserves dedicated field extraction — it's a rogue-DHCP/spoofing security signal.

catalog.name: cisco-ios-ccsip-debug
catalog.product: Cisco IOS/IOS-XE voice gateway 'debug ccsip messages' (CUBE)

catalog.detect_signature: IOS syslog/debug timestamp + body matching ^//-?\d+/[0-9A-Fx]+/SIP/(Msg|Call|State|Transport)/\w+: (callID/GUID/SIP/subsystem/function header), Msg lines followed by Received:/Sent: + raw SIP
catalog.fields: IOS ts, callID, GUID, subsystem path, function; direction (Received/Sent); raw SIP payload
catalog.notes: GUID -> trace_id. Also covers 'debug voip ccapi inout' //callid/GUID/CCAPI/... lines with same framing.

catalog.name: cisco-ios-dhcp-server-syslog
catalog.product: Cisco IOS/IOS-XE built-in DHCP server (%DHCPD facility)
catalog.sample_line: Aug 9 11:21:34.527: %DHCPD-4-PING_CONFLICT: DHCP address conflict: server pinged 172.25.199.172.
catalog.detect_signature: '%DHCPD-<sev>-<MNEMONIC>:' token (PING_CONFLICT, DECLINE_CONFLICT, HIGH_UTILIZATION, POOL_EXHAUSTED...)
catalog.fields: ios timestamp, severity, mnemonic, conflict ip / pool name / utilization
catalog.notes: Pool-exhaustion and address-conflict events — the on-router counterpart to server-grade DHCP logs.

catalog.name: cisco-meraki-syslog
catalog.product: Cisco Meraki MX/MR syslog (flows / urls / ids-alerts / security_event / events)

catalog.name: cisco-wlc-aireos-syslog

catalog.fields: task_name, ts.ms, facility, severity, mnemonic, src_file, src_line, message
catalog.notes: Legacy but still deployed; task name and embedded source file:line distinguish it from IOS.

catalog.name: citrix-netscaler-rfc5424

catalog.fields: pri, version, iso timestamp, hostname, feature-as-appname, PPE procid, then same fields as the native/CEF adapters
catalog.notes: Verbatim from Elastic citrix_waf rfc5424 corpus. Newer firmware default when 'syslog over TCP/RFC5424' is enabled.

catalog.name: clamav-clamscan-stdout-summary

catalog.name: cloudfront-realtime-tsv

catalog.name: cockroachdb-crdb-v1

catalog.name: couchbase-ns-server-log
catalog.product: Couchbase Server cluster-manager logs (debug.log, info.log, ns_couchdb.log — Erlang ns_server format)

catalog.notes: Body is frequently multi-line Erlang terms — join until next '[subsystem:' header. memcached.log and the SDK logs use different formats (follow-up). Grounded from couchbase/docs-server manage-logging.adoc.

catalog.name: couchdb-log
catalog.detect_signature: ^\[(debug|info|notice|warning|error|critical|alert|emergency)\] \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T\S+Z couchdb@\S+ <\d+\.\d+\.\d+> — level-first bracket + erlang node + pid triple
catalog.fields: [level], ISO ts (us, Z), node name couchdb@host, <erlang pid>, request-id (or -------- for non-HTTP), then message; HTTP lines add host, peer, user, method, path, status, reason, duration
catalog.notes: Distinct product from Couchbase's bundled couchdb logs (those use the ns_server bracket header). request-id → trace_id.

catalog.notes: The ::ffff: mapped-IPv4 bracket form is a strong fingerprint vs Dovecot/Cyrus.

catalog.name: crowdsec

catalog.detect_signature: logfmt-style time=/level=/msg= with CrowdSec phrases (scenario names 'crowdsecurity/...', 'ban', 'decision')
catalog.fields: time(ISO), level, msg (ip, scenario, event count), bucket_id -> data; also decisions API JSON with {source.ip, scenario, duration, type:ban}
catalog.notes: Agent log is logfmt (covered by logfmt adapter) but scenario/decision semantics are domain-specific; decisions are also exposed as JSON. Modern fail2ban alternative.

catalog.name: crowdstrike-falcon-siem-connector-cef
catalog.product: CrowdStrike Falcon (SIEM Connector / detection stream, CEF output)
catalog.sample_line: CEF:0|CrowdStrike|FalconHost|1.0|DetectionSummaryEvent|Detection Summary|8|externalId=ldt:abc123 rt=Jul 11 2022 20:33:24 src=10.0.0.5 shost=WIN-DESKTOP01 suser=jdoe filePath=\\Device\\HarddiskVolume2\\Users\\jdoe\\evil.exe fname=evil.exe cs1=malware cs1Label=Tactic cs2=Execution cs2Label=Technique act=Prevented
catalog.detect_signature: CEF header where device vendor field == "CrowdStrike" and product == "FalconHost"; event class often DetectionSummaryEvent/AuthActivityAuditEvent
catalog.fields: CEF header (vendor=CrowdStrike, product=FalconHost, signatureId=event type, severity), externalId, rt, src, shost, suser, filePath, fname, cs1/cs1Label (Tactic), cs2/cs2Label (Technique), act
catalog.notes: The Falcon SIEM Connector normalizes streaming API events to CEF or LEEF. Distinct from the raw FDR JSON. Vendor/product header is the fingerprint.

catalog.name: cumulus-linux-syslog
catalog.sample_line: 2016-09-14T21:56:07.996136+00:00 cumulus switchd[4106]: switchd version 1.0-cl3u7
catalog.detect_signature: rsyslog RFC3339 timestamp with 6-digit microseconds and offset, hostname, then a Cumulus daemon name (switchd, clagd, mstpd, portwd, ledmgrd, neighmgrd, nvued)[pid]:
catalog.fields: ts RFC3339.us+tz, hostname, daemon, pid, message (often 'file.c:line' prefix inside message)
catalog.notes: Routing on Cumulus is FRR (see frr-log). The high-precision RFC3339 default template + Cumulus-specific daemon set is the discriminator vs plain Linux syslog.

catalog.name: cylance-protect-cef-syslog
catalog.sample_line: CEF:0|Cylance|CylancePROTECT|2.0|Threat|Threat|5|rt=Jul 11 2022 20:33:24 dvchost=win-desktop01 fname=evil.exe filePath=C:\Users\jdoe\evil.exe fileHash=ABC... cs1=Unsafe cs1Label=Classification cs2=100 cs2Label=CylanceScore act=Quarantined
catalog.detect_signature: CEF header vendor "Cylance" product "CylancePROTECT" (or "CylanceOPTICS"); cs*Label=Classification/CylanceScore
catalog.fields: CEF header (vendor=Cylance, product=CylancePROTECT), rt, dvchost, fname, filePath, fileHash, cs1=Classification(Unsafe/Abnormal), cs2=CylanceScore, act, plus Device/Zone/Detected-by
catalog.notes: Cylance's ML-verdict fields (Classification + CylanceScore 0-100) are the distinctive extension. Sample reflects documented Cylance CEF fields; verify header product string for OPTICS EDR vs PROTECT AV.

catalog.name: cyrus-imapd-syslog
catalog.sample_line: Jul 20 09:15:33 mailhost cyrus/imap[12345]: login: client.example.com [192.0.2.10] jane PLAIN+TLS User logged in SESSIONID=<cyrus-12345-1721466933-1>
catalog.detect_signature: syslog tag cyrus/<service>[pid] (imap, pop3, lmtpunix, master, imaps) — or legacy 'imap[pid]:' with Cyrus verbs login:, badlogin:, USAGE, Delivered:, duplicate_check:, mystore:
catalog.fields: service, event verb, client host, ip, user, auth mech, SESSIONID, for lmtp: message-id + mailbox
catalog.notes: badlogin: lines are the fail2ban-style security signal; SESSIONID is trace_id.

catalog.name: db2-zos-console-dsn
catalog.product: IBM Db2 for z/OS address-space console messages (DSNxxxx)
catalog.sample_line: DSNL004I  -DB2P DDF START COMPLETE
catalog.detect_signature: Message id ^DSN[A-Z][0-9]{3}[IAE] followed by '-ssid' (Db2 subsystem recognition character + id); families: DSNL (DDF), DSNT (timeout/deadlock DSNT376I), DSNR (restart), DSNJ (logging)
catalog.fields: message_id, db2_ssid, text; DSNT376I carries plan/correlation/luwid of deadlock participants
catalog.notes: Rides on SYSLOG; message-family classifier. DSNT376I/DSNT375I deadlock-timeout pairs are prime alert material.

catalog.name: dcmtk-oflog
catalog.product: DCMTK DICOM toolkit (storescu/storescp/echoscu/dcmqrscp, and embedded DCMTK in PACS products) — oflog/log4cplus output
catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-21 12:00:00.123 INFO - dcmnet   - Association Accepted (Max Send PDV: 16372)
catalog.detect_signature: Two documented patterns: console '%D{%H:%M:%S} %5p: %m' -> 'HH:MM:SS LEVEL: msg', and file '%D{%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%q} %5p - %-8c{1} - %m' -> timestamp, padded level, ' - logger - ' with 8-char-padded short logger name; default CLI short form is single-letter prefix 'I: ', 'E: ', 'W: ', 'D: ' at line start
catalog.fields: ts from %D; %5p level; %c logger (dcmnet, dcmdata...) -> category; message; association negotiation / DIMSE messages often span multiple lines (presentation contexts) -> multiline join
catalog.notes: Patterns verified verbatim from support.dcmtk.org docs (file_filelog.html sample logger.cfg). Sample line constructed strictly from the verified file pattern with a real DCMTK message string. The bare 'I:/E:/W:/D:' console prefix overlaps with pynetdicom (below) — keep detect signatures cooperative.

catalog.name: dfsmshsm-arc-activity-log
catalog.sample_line: ARC0521I PRIMARY SPACE MANAGEMENT STARTING AT 02:00:00 ON 2026/07/20
catalog.detect_signature: Message ID '^ARC[0-9]{4}[IEWA]' in HSM command/migration/backup/dump activity logs and job log (ARC0734I per-dataset action lines with ACTION=MIGRATE/BACKUP, RC=)
catalog.fields: message_id, function (migration/backup/recall), dataset, volume, action, return/reason codes, timestamps
catalog.notes: ARC0734I lines are the per-dataset audit trail of automatic storage management; failures (nonzero RC) are actionable.

catalog.name: dgraph-glog-classic
catalog.product: Dgraph (graph DB) alpha/zero logs — classic glog (2-digit month/day, no year)
catalog.sample_line: I1103 11:57:31.739339 24395 google.cc:2341] Command line: ./some_prog
catalog.fields: Lmmdd HH:MM:SS.uuuuuu threadid file:line] msg (canonical glog spec)
catalog.notes: Format spec + example line verbatim from google/glog official docs; Dgraph (and badger, CockroachDB-adjacent tools, osquery already covered) emit this classic no-year variant. NOTE: no year — normalizer must infer year from file mtime/context.

catalog.name: dnf.rpm.log
catalog.detect_signature: '<ISO8601±tz> <LEVEL> <verb>: <NEVRA>' with verbs Installed/Upgraded/Erased/Obsoleted/Reinstalled; NEVRA 'name-[epoch:]version-release.arch'.
catalog.fields: timestamp, level, action, nevra(name,epoch,version,release,arch)
catalog.notes: NEVRA parsing is the payoff. SUBDEBUG is the dominant level here.

catalog.name: dnscrypt-proxy-query-tsv
catalog.sample_line: [2020-12-15 14:36:30]	127.0.0.1	www.ripe.net	A	PASS	1ms	faelix-ch-ipv4
catalog.detect_signature: tab-separated: bracketed local ts, client ip, qname, qtype, return code in {PASS,FORWARD,DROP,REJECT,SYNTH,NOT_READY,PARSE_ERROR,NXDOMAIN,RESPONSE_ERROR,SERVER_ERROR,CLOAK}, duration 'Nms', server name
catalog.fields: timestamp, client_ip, query_name, query_type, return_code, duration, server, relay
catalog.notes: Also nx_log (same shape) for NXDOMAIN-only stream.

catalog.name: dnsmasq-leases-file
catalog.detect_signature: whitespace-separated 5-field lines: ^\d{9,10} ([0-9a-f]{2}:){5}[0-9a-f]{2} <ipv4> (<hostname>|\*) (<clientid>|\*)$ ; IPv6 rows use 'duid ...' header line and IAID field
catalog.fields: expiry epoch (0=infinite), mac (optionally ARP-type-prefixed XX-...), ip, hostname or *, client-id or *
catalog.notes: Snapshot file rewritten by dnsmasq; each line = one current lease. ts = expiry epoch.

catalog.name: dnstap-framestream
catalog.product: dnstap binary capture (BIND, Unbound, Knot, PowerDNS, CoreDNS, NSD all emit it)
catalog.sample_line: <frame-streams control frame: content-type "protobuf:dnstap.Dnstap"> + protobuf Dnstap{identity, version, message{type=CLIENT_QUERY, socket_family=INET, socket_protocol=UDP, query_address, query_port, query_time_sec/nsec, query_message=<dns wire>}}
catalog.detect_signature: Frame Streams container: 4-byte length 0x00000000 escape + control frame with content-type string 'protobuf:dnstap.Dnstap'
catalog.fields: identity, version, message.type (CLIENT_QUERY/CLIENT_RESPONSE/RESOLVER_QUERY/RESOLVER_RESPONSE/AUTH_QUERY/AUTH_RESPONSE/FORWARDER_*/STUB_*/TOOL_*/UPDATE_*), socket family/protocol, query/response address+port, sec/nsec timestamps, raw DNS wire message, policy (RPZ) sub-message
catalog.notes: THE cross-vendor DNS telemetry format. Adapter should decode frame-streams + protobuf and then the embedded DNS message header for qname/qtype/rcode.

catalog.name: dnstap-quiet-text
catalog.product: dnstap CLI / dnstap-read -q quiet text output
catalog.detect_signature: '<HH:MM:SS.us> <2-letter mnemonic in {CQ,CR,RQ,RR,AQ,AR,FQ,FR,SQ,SR,TQ,TR,UQ,UR}> <ip> UDP|TCP <N>b "name." CLASS TYPE'
catalog.fields: time, message-type mnemonic, peer ip, protocol, size with 'b' suffix, quoted qname, qclass, qtype
catalog.notes: Emitted by golang-dnstap CLI and bind9 dnstap-read; the 2-letter type code set is the fingerprint.

catalog.name: druid-log4j2
catalog.sample_line: 2021-05-14T18:10:03,418 INFO [org.apache.druid.metadata.SQLMetadataSegmentManager-Exec--0] org.apache.druid.metadata.SQLMetadataSegmentManager - Polled and found 1,079 segments in the database
catalog.detect_signature: ISO8601 'T' + comma-millis ts, [thread], full org.apache.druid.* logger, ' - ' msg; optional [markerSimpleName] between logger and msg
catalog.fields: ts, level, thread, logger, optional marker, message; segment ids + task ids (index_kafka_…) = trace_id; task logs for ingestion jobs are separate per-task files
catalog.notes: Real line + documented pattern '%d{ISO8601} %p [%t] %c -%notEmpty{ [%markerSimpleName]} %m%n' from druid.apache.org logging docs.

catalog.name: duo-authlogs
catalog.product: Duo Security Admin API v2 authentication logs

catalog.fields: timestamp/isotimestamp, result, reason, factor, user{}, application{}, access_device{location,ip}, auth_device, txid, trusted_endpoint_status

catalog.name: duplicati-log-file
catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-21 02:00:01 +02 - [Information-Duplicati.Library.Main.Controller-StartingOperation]: The operation Backup has started
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} [+-]\d{2} - \[(Information|Warning|Error|Profiling|Verbose)-[A-Za-z.]+-\w+\]: — bracketed Level-Namespace-EventId tag
catalog.fields: ts (+TZ offset hours), level, dotted source class, event_id (last dash segment), message; result summaries serialized as multi-line object dumps

catalog.name: emqx-json-log

catalog.detect_signature: JSON lines with keys time+level+msg where msg is snake_case and optional clientid/peername/tag
catalog.fields: time (rfc3339 or epoch per config), level, msg, tag, clientid, peername, username, arbitrary context
catalog.notes: JSON formatter existence + field set verified from EMQX log docs (same fields as text formatter); sample assembled from the verified text-format example — capture one live JSON line to lock exact key order/names before finalizing detect().

catalog.name: erep-logrec
catalog.product: IBM z/OS LOGREC / EREP (hardware & software error records)

catalog.detect_signature: Raw: LOGREC dataset/log stream binary records with class/source byte (MCH machine check, SVCDUMP software, DDR, MIH). Text: EREP report banners 'SYSTEM SUMMARY', 'DETAIL EDIT REPORT', TYPE:/REPORT: header pairs
catalog.fields: record class (machine check/software/channel), timestamp, jobname, abend code, PSW, failing CSECT/module, device CUA for I/O errors
catalog.notes: Mainframe hardware-error trail (SMART/mcelog equivalent). Support EREP text reports first; raw LOGREC as opaque envelope. Sample header reconstructed.

catalog.name: esbuild output / metafile
catalog.sample_line:
dist/out.js  1.2mb

✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "./missing"

    src/index.ts:3:20:
      3 │ import x from "./missing"
        ╵                     ~~~~~~~~~~
catalog.detect_signature: Human: '✘ [ERROR]' / '▲ [WARNING]' with '<file>:line:col:' and '│'/'╵' code frames; output-size lines 'path  <size>'. --analyze gives text tree; --metafile=meta.json gives JSON {inputs,outputs}.
catalog.fields: level, message, file:line:col, output_path, size, metafile(inputs,outputs)
catalog.notes: '✘ [ERROR]'/'▲ [WARNING]' glyph+bracket tag is the tell. metafile is separate JSON.

catalog.name: eset-protect-json-syslog
catalog.product: ESET PROTECT (event export, JSON over syslog)
catalog.sample_line: {"event_type":"Threat_Event","ipv4":"10.0.0.5","hostname":"win-desktop01","source_uuid":"abc-123","occured":"11-Jul-2022 20:33:24","severity":"Warning","threat_name":"Eicar test file","threat_type":"test file","scanner_id":"Real-time file system protection","object_uri":"file:///C:/Users/jdoe/evil.exe","action_taken":"cleaned by deleting","threat_handled":true}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with ESET keys "event_type" (values like Threat_Event, FirewallAggregated_Event, HipsAggregated_Event, Audit_Event) + "source_uuid" + "occured" (note the ESET misspelling) + "scanner_id"
catalog.fields: event_type, ipv4, hostname, source_uuid, occured (dd-Mon-yyyy HH:MM:SS), severity, threat_name, threat_type, scanner_id, object_uri (file:/// URI), action_taken, threat_handled (bool)
catalog.notes: Verified key names from ESET Online Help 'Events exported to JSON'. The misspelled "occured" timestamp key is a reliable ESET fingerprint.

catalog.name: etcd-capnslog-legacy
catalog.product: etcd <= v3.4 legacy capnslog text format
catalog.fields: ts (space sep, µs), single-char level (C/E/W/N/I/D), ' | ', subsystem (etcdmain, flags, embed, raft, grpc), ': ', message
catalog.notes: Verbatim from real issues (often wrapped in journald prefix). Still extremely common in older k8s control planes.

catalog.name: exabgp-log
catalog.sample_line: 14:30:41 | 21730  | welcome       | Thank you for using ExaBGP
catalog.detect_signature: pipe-delimited fixed columns 'HH:MM:SS | pid | source | message' where source is a padded token like welcome, version, network, api, reactor, peer-1
catalog.fields: time, pid, subsystem/source, message; peer events embed neighbor ip + state in message
catalog.notes: Column layout configurable but pipe default is distinctive. Newer versions can add date + severity column — accept optional leading date.

catalog.name: exchange-smtp-protocol-log
catalog.product: Microsoft Exchange SMTP send/receive protocol logs (RECV*.LOG / SEND*.LOG)
catalog.detect_signature: header '#Log-type: SMTP Receive Protocol Log' (or SMTP Send) + '#Fields: date-time,connector-id,session-id,sequence-number,local-endpoint,remote-endpoint,event,data,context'; event column is one of + - > < *
catalog.fields: date-time, connector-id, session-id (trace_id), sequence-number, local/remote ip:port, event (+connect,-disconnect,>sent,<received,*info), data (SMTP verb/reply), context
catalog.notes: Wire-level SMTP dialogue; pair with message-tracking adapter.

catalog.name: exim-rejectlog
catalog.sample_line: 2020-02-09 10:31:12 H=spammer.example [203.0.113.9] F=<junk@spammer.example> rejected RCPT <nobody@example.net>: relay not permitted
catalog.detect_signature: exim-style 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' line containing 'rejected' / 'temporarily rejected' with H= F= and RCPT/MAIL/DATA stage tokens; file usually named rejectlog
catalog.fields: ts, H=host[ip], F=sender, rejection stage, recipient, reason; may be followed by copied message headers
catalog.notes: Same lexer as mainlog; multi-line (header snapshot appended) — parser must attach continuation lines.

catalog.name: extreme-exos-log
catalog.sample_line: 05/20/2015 14:02:33.85 <Info:AAA.authPass> Login passed for user admin through telnet (192.168.1.10)
catalog.detect_signature: 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS.ss' then '<Severity:Component.Subcomponent.eventName>' angle-bracket tag (Info|Noti|Warn|Erro|Crit|Debu-*)
catalog.fields: ts, severity, component, subcomponent, event condition name, message; 'show log' may prepend slot id
catalog.notes: The <Sev:Comp.Event> tag is a stable machine-parseable key into Extreme's event catalog.

catalog.name: f5-bigip-apm-syslog
catalog.product: F5 BIG-IP APM (Access Policy Manager) session logs via apmd/apd syslog
catalog.sample_line: 01490102:5: /Common/test:Common:acb12bdc: Access policy result: Logon_Deny
catalog.detect_signature: F5 syslog skeleton (see f5-bigip-ltm-syslog) where the errdefs code starts 0149 (APM range) and the message begins with /Partition/profile:Partition:8-hex-session-id: — regex ^0149\d{4}:\d: \S+:\w+:[0-9a-f]{8}:
catalog.fields: errdefs code, access profile path, partition, APM session id (trace_id), event text (session start/policy result/ACL, Max_concurrent_Users etc.)
catalog.notes: Message-code (01490102:5:), session-id and Access_Profile structure grounded from the Elastic APM test corpus; outer transport is the standard BIG-IP syslog wrapper. APM session id is the cross-line trace key.

catalog.name: f5-bigip-dos-kv-semicolon
catalog.product: F5 BIG-IP ASM/AFM Application DoS event remote logging (semicolon-delimited key=value)

catalog.detect_signature: semicolon-delimited unquoted key=value pairs containing dos_attack_id= and errdefs_msgno= (device_vendor=F5). Trailing semicolon.
catalog.fields: dos_attack_id (trace), dos_attack_name/event, mitigation action+reason, tps/latency baselines, source_ip, context (virtual server), errdefs_msgno, severity
catalog.notes: Grounded from Elastic f5_bigip test corpus. Distinct delimiter (;) from the comma ASM format — needs its own detect.

catalog.name: factorytalk-diagnostics-export

catalog.fields: Time, Severity (Error/Warning/Information/Audit), Message text, Provider (e.g. FactoryTalk Linx, FactoryTalk Directory), User, Computer; underlying store is FTD .dat/ODBC

catalog.name: fail2ban-log

catalog.notes: Comma-millisecond Python-logging timestamp; jail name maps to category.

catalog.fields: priority->level; rule->category; output->data.message; output_fields{}/inline k=v->data; time->ts_ms(nanoseconds)
catalog.notes: Two outputs: plain text (nanosecond time + priority + rule output) and JSON (json_output=true). Container/k8s security — increasingly common for devs on Kubernetes. Priority is syslog-style word.

catalog.name: fastly-realtime-apache

catalog.notes: Reuse the existing CLF/Apache parser; add prefix-stripping for the four Fastly syslog wrappers and recognize Fastly-specific VCL tokens (fastly_info.state, server.datacenter) when present. Many users emit JSON via VCL instead — falls through to json-lines adapter.

catalog.name: fortigate-event-kv
catalog.product: Fortinet FortiGate event/system logs (admin login, VPN, HA)
catalog.sample_line: date=2019-05-13 time=14:29:12 logid="0100032002" type="event" subtype="system" level="alert" vd="vdom1" eventtime=1557782952291849602 logdesc="Admin login failed" sn="0" user="admin1" ui="https(172.16.200.254)" method="https" srcip=172.16.200.254 dstip=172.16.200.1 action="login" status="failed" reason="name_invalid" msg="Administrator admin1 login failed from https(172.16.200.254) because of invalid user name"
catalog.detect_signature: FortiGate KV with type="event"; logdesc= and msg= present
catalog.fields: date,time,logid,type,subtype,level,vd,logdesc,user,ui,action,status,reason,msg

catalog.name: foundationdb-trace-xml
catalog.sample_line: <Event Severity="10" Time="1578010020.882538" DateTime="2020-01-02T23:27:00Z" Type="Role" ID="0000000000000000" Machine="10.0.0.1:4500" LogGroup="default" Roles="SS" />
catalog.detect_signature: ^<Event Severity="\d+" (Time|DateTime)= self-closing elements, one per line — Severity is numeric (5/10/20/30/40)
catalog.fields: Severity (numeric: 10=info,20=warn,30=warnAlways,40=error), Time (epoch float), DateTime, Type (event name), ID, Machine ip:port, LogGroup, Roles, plus event-specific attributes
catalog.notes: Attribute-per-field emission verified from flow/XmlTraceLogFormatter.cpp (Severity/Time always first). Type→category, ID→trace_id, numeric Severity needs mapping.

catalog.name: freebsd-periodic-daily
catalog.product: FreeBSD periodic(8) daily/weekly run output (mailed 'daily run output')
catalog.sample_line: Removing stale files from /var/preserve:
catalog.detect_signature: Mail subject '<host> daily run output'; body composed of blank-line-separated sections each starting with a known heading ('Cleaning out old system announcements:', 'Backup passwd and group files:', 'Disk status:' + df table, 'Network interface status:' + netstat table, 'Local system status:' + uptime, 'Checking status of mail queue:')
catalog.fields: section heading, embedded df/netstat/mailq tables
catalog.notes: Companion 'security run output' mail (periodic security) has its own sections: 'Checking setuid files and devices:', 'Checking for uids of 0:', kernel-message and login-failure extracts — treat as sibling adapter freebsd-security-run.

catalog.name: freebsd-security-run
catalog.product: FreeBSD periodic security output (mailed 'security run output')
catalog.sample_line: Checking for uids of 0:
catalog.detect_signature: Mail subject '<host> security run output'; sections 'Checking setuid files and devices:', 'Checking for uids of 0:', 'Checking for passwordless accounts:', '<host> login failures:', '<host> refused connections:', 'Checking for denied packets:' with pf/ipfw counter diffs (+/- prefixed lines)
catalog.fields: section heading; diff-style +/- lines for setuid & packet-counter changes; embedded syslog excerpts for login failures
catalog.notes: Overlaps OpenBSD insecurity report in spirit but sections/wording differ — keep as separate detect.

catalog.name: freebsd_dmesg_raw
catalog.sample_line: ugen0.2: <vendor product> at usbus0
catalog.detect_signature: no leading timestamp; device 'name0:' or 'name0.N:' prefix + descriptor; optional '[secs]' if kern.msgbuf_show_timestamp=1
catalog.fields: optional ts=[secs] when sysctl enabled; subsystem=device prefix; message=descriptor
catalog.notes: By default FreeBSD kernel messages carry NO timestamp; enable via kern.msgbuf_show_timestamp=1 to get '[secs]' bracket like Linux.

catalog.name: freeipa-api-log
catalog.product: FreeIPA server JSON-RPC API log (Apache error_log embed)
catalog.sample_line: [Wed Jul 16 09:31:03.145678 2025] [wsgi:error] [pid 1234] ipa: INFO: [jsonrpc] admin@EXAMPLE.COM: user_add/1(u'jdoe', version=u'2.251'): SUCCESS
catalog.detect_signature: 'ipa: <LEVEL>: [jsonrpc|xmlrpc] <principal>: <command>(args): SUCCESS|<error>' inside httpd error_log lines
catalog.fields: apache ts, wsgi level, pid, ipa level, protocol, authenticated principal, command, args, result
catalog.notes: FreeIPA otherwise reuses 389-DS access/audit + krb5kdc formats already listed

catalog.name: freepbx-monolog-log
catalog.sample_line: [2026-01-05 10:26:12] [freepbx.INFO]: Module core has been upgraded to 16.0.68 [] []
catalog.detect_signature: ^\[\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} [\d:]{8}\] \[?freepbx\.(DEBUG|INFO|NOTICE|WARNING|ERROR|CRITICAL)\]?:
catalog.fields: ts, channel 'freepbx', Monolog level, message, trailing context/extra JSON arrays
catalog.notes: Standard Monolog line format with channel fixed to freepbx.

catalog.name: freeradius-detail
catalog.sample_line:
Tue Jul 20 11:01:12 2026
	User-Name = "bob"
	NAS-IP-Address = 192.0.2.1
	Acct-Status-Type = Start
	Timestamp = 1626778872
catalog.detect_signature: multi-line records: bare ctime date line, then TAB-indented 'Attribute = Value' RADIUS AVP lines, blank-line separated
catalog.fields: all RADIUS attributes verbatim (User-Name, Acct-Session-Id, Packet-Type, NAS-*, Framed-IP-Address...), Timestamp
catalog.notes: Same record grammar used by radacct per-NAS files

catalog.name: freeradius-log
catalog.sample_line: Wed Oct 30 10:18:08 2019 : Auth: (0) Login OK: [bob] (from client host1 port 0)
catalog.detect_signature: ctime ts + ' : ' + category(Auth|Info|Error|Proxy) + ': ' + optional (reqnum) + 'Login OK:|Login incorrect' + '[user]' + '(from client X port N [cli MAC])'
catalog.fields: ts, category, request number, outcome, username, client shortname, NAS port, cli (calling-station)

catalog.name: freeswitch-cdr-csv
catalog.detect_signature: quoted CSV with 3 consecutive datetime fields at positions 5-7 and a Q.850-style hangup cause string (NORMAL_CLEARING, ORIGINATOR_CANCEL, NO_ANSWER, USER_BUSY...) followed by a 36-char UUID
catalog.fields: caller_id_name,caller_id_number,destination_number,context,start_stamp,answer_stamp,end_stamp,duration,billsec,hangup_cause,uuid,bleg_uuid,accountcode
catalog.notes: Template-configurable; ship the default. uuid -> trace_id.

catalog.name: freeswitch-cdr-xml
catalog.sample_line: <cdr core-uuid="4d6e56ae-..."><channel_data><state>CS_REPORTING</state><direction>inbound</direction></channel_data><variables><uuid>a1b2c3d4-...</uuid><sip_call_id>abc@203.0.113.10</sip_call_id><duration>108</duration><hangup_cause>NORMAL_CLEARING</hangup_cause></variables><callflow>...</callflow></cdr>
catalog.detect_signature: XML document with root <cdr> containing <channel_data> and <variables> children (FreeSWITCH variable names inside)
catalog.fields: channel_data (state/direction), variables/* (uuid, sip_call_id, start_epoch, answer_epoch, end_epoch, billsec, hangup_cause), callflow/caller_profile
catalog.notes: One file/POST per call leg. variables.uuid -> trace_id, end_epoch -> ts.

catalog.name: freeswitch-esl-event-plain
catalog.sample_line:
Event-Name: CHANNEL_ANSWER
Core-UUID: 4d6e56ae-9bcf-4b2a-9e3f-1234567890ab
FreeSWITCH-Hostname: fs01
Event-Date-Timestamp: 1767608772123456
Unique-ID: a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab
Caller-Caller-ID-Number: 1000
catalog.detect_signature: blank-line-separated 'Key: Value' blocks containing Event-Name: and Core-UUID:/Event-Date-Timestamp: headers (values URL-encoded)
catalog.fields: Event-Name, Event-Date-Timestamp (microsecond epoch), Unique-ID, Channel-*, Caller-*, variable_* keys; values are URL-encoded
catalog.notes: Also a 'json' subformat (same keys as one JSON object) — detect {"Event-Name": as a variant. Unique-ID -> trace_id.

catalog.name: freeswitch-sofia-siptrace
catalog.product: FreeSWITCH 'sofia global siptrace on' (nua/tport SIP dump)
catalog.detect_signature: ^(send|recv) \d+ bytes (to|from) (udp|tcp|tls|ws|wss)/\[[^\]]+\]:\d+ at [\d:.]+:$ followed by a dashed rule and 3-space-indented SIP message
catalog.fields: direction, byte count, transport, peer [ip]:port, time-of-day; indented raw SIP payload
catalog.notes: Interleaved in freeswitch.log/console. Strip 3-space indent, pull Call-ID -> trace_id.

catalog.name: ftp-xferlog
catalog.product: Classic Unix FTP transfer log (wu-ftpd/proftpd/vsftpd xferlog, /var/log/xferlog)
catalog.sample_line: Mon Jul 20 14:02:15 2026 1 192.168.1.5 4096 /pub/file.tgz b _ o r alice ftp 0 * c
catalog.detect_signature: 14 space-separated fields: asctime timestamp (5 tokens) + transfer-time secs + remote-host + byte-count + filename + transfer-type(a|b) + special-action(C|U|T|_) + direction(o|i|d) + access-mode(a|g|r) + username + service + auth-method(0|1) + auth-user-id(*|id) + completion(c|i)
catalog.fields: current-time, transfer-time, remote-host, file-size, filename, transfer type, special action flag, direction, access mode, username, service name, authentication method, authenticated user id, completion status
catalog.notes: Legacy but still emitted by vsftpd/proftpd on enterprise Unix; absent from the known-names list.

catalog.name: gcp-firewall-rules-log-json
catalog.sample_line: {"insertId":"1eq9kmtg2wqxatd","jsonPayload":{"connection":{"src_ip":"203.0.113.7","src_port":60094,"dest_ip":"10.128.0.2","dest_port":22,"protocol":6},"disposition":"DENIED","rule_details":{"reference":"network:default/firewall:deny-ssh","priority":900,"action":"DENY","direction":"INGRESS","ip_port_info":[{"ip_protocol":"TCP","port_range":["22"]}]},"instance":{"project_id":"my-project","vm_name":"my-vm","zone":"us-central1-a"},"vpc":{"project_id":"my-project","vpc_name":"default","subnetwork_name":"default"}},"resource":{"type":"gce_subnetwork"},"timestamp":"2019-11-06T00:20:32.564893297Z","logName":"projects/my-project/logs/compute.googleapis.com%2Ffirewall"}
catalog.detect_signature: LogEntry with logName ending compute.googleapis.com%2Ffirewall and jsonPayload.disposition ALLOWED|DENIED + rule_details
catalog.fields: timestamp->ts, disposition->level(DENIED=warn), connection 5-tuple, rule_details.reference->data.message, instance/vpc metadata->source
catalog.notes: Per-connection rule hits; sibling of vpc_flows.

catalog.name: gcp-healthcare-api-audit
catalog.product: Google Cloud Healthcare API (FHIR/DICOM/HL7v2 stores) — Cloud Audit Logs entries, serviceName healthcare.googleapis.com
catalog.sample_line: {"protoPayload":{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.audit.AuditLog","serviceName":"healthcare.googleapis.com","methodName":"google.cloud.healthcare.v1.fhir.rest.FhirService.SearchResources","authenticationInfo":{"principalEmail":"user@example.com"}},"logName":"projects/p/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access","timestamp":"2026-07-21T12:00:00Z"}
catalog.detect_signature: Within the (already-implemented) gcp-logentry-envelope: protoPayload.serviceName=='healthcare.googleapis.com'; methodName prefixes google.cloud.healthcare.v1.{fhir,dicom,dicomweb,hl7v2,dataset}
catalog.fields: timestamp -> ts; methodName -> category (SearchResources, RetrieveInstance, CreateMessage, CreateDataset, ExportResources LRO pairs); log type admin_activity vs data_access; principalEmail -> user; status.code -> level; resourceName (dataset/store path) -> source
catalog.notes: serviceName, log types (Admin Activity / Data Access / LRO start+end pairs) and method names (FhirService.SearchResources, DicomWebService.RetrieveInstance, Hl7V2Service.CreateMessage, DicomService.ImportDicomData) verified from docs.cloud.google.com/healthcare-api/docs/how-tos/audit-logging. Implement as a specialization on top of the existing gcp-logentry-envelope adapter.

catalog.name: gcp-lb-request-log-json
catalog.product: Google Cloud External HTTP(S) Load Balancer request logs (requests log, http_load_balancer resource)
catalog.sample_line: {"insertId":"2ax2hxfcv95jf","httpRequest":{"requestMethod":"GET","requestUrl":"http://www.example.com/","requestSize":"693","status":404,"responseSize":"884","userAgent":"curl/7.64.1","remoteIp":"203.0.113.9","serverIp":"10.128.0.3","latency":"0.003497s"},"jsonPayload":{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.loadbalancing.type.LoadBalancerLogEntry","statusDetails":"response_sent_by_backend","backendTargetProjectNumber":"projects/123456789"},"resource":{"type":"http_load_balancer","labels":{"project_id":"my-project","url_map_name":"web-map","zone":"global"}},"timestamp":"2020-04-01T21:21:26.194695Z","severity":"INFO","logName":"projects/my-project/logs/requests","trace":"projects/my-project/traces/ff1c9ed172a1cd2d439c4b1e19d5dfd7"}
catalog.detect_signature: LogEntry with resource.type=="http_load_balancer" and jsonPayload["@type"] LoadBalancerLogEntry + httpRequest block
catalog.fields: timestamp->ts, severity->level, httpRequest.* (method/url/status/latency/remoteIp), jsonPayload.statusDetails->data.message, trace->trace_id, url_map_name->source
catalog.notes: statusDetails encodes LB-side failure reasons (failed_to_pick_backend etc) - map non-response_sent_by_backend to warn.

catalog.name: gcp-scc-finding-json
catalog.product: Google Security Command Center findings (Pub/Sub NotificationMessage / export)
catalog.sample_line: {"notificationConfigName":"organizations/123456789/notificationConfigs/my-config","finding":{"name":"organizations/123456789/sources/9876543210/findings/0f26bf2af94e44e9b7f4d0a1c2e3d4f5","parent":"organizations/123456789/sources/9876543210","resourceName":"//compute.googleapis.com/projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances/my-vm","state":"ACTIVE","category":"OPEN_FIREWALL","sourceProperties":{"Recommendation":"Restrict the firewall rules"},"securityMarks":{},"eventTime":"2019-08-12T21:41:42.573Z","createTime":"2019-08-12T21:41:43.114Z","severity":"HIGH"}}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with finding.name matching organizations/*/sources/*/findings/* + state + category + eventTime
catalog.fields: finding.eventTime->ts, severity->level, category->data.message, resourceName->source, state, sourceProperties, finding.name->trace_id
catalog.notes: Also arrives bare (finding object without notification wrapper) from the API - detect both.

catalog.name: gcp-structured-stdout
catalog.product: GCP structured logging via stdout (Cloud Run/GCF special JSON fields)
catalog.sample_line: {"severity":"NOTICE","message":"This is the default display field.","component":"arbitrary-property","logging.googleapis.com/trace":"projects/my-proj/traces/1b02cd14bb8642fd092bc23f54c7ffcd","logging.googleapis.com/spanId":"f24e8631bd11faa7"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON line containing any 'logging.googleapis.com/*' key (trace, spanId, labels, sourceLocation, operation) or severity+message pair emitted to container stdout
catalog.fields: severity, message, time, logging.googleapis.com/trace, logging.googleapis.com/spanId, logging.googleapis.com/labels, logging.googleapis.com/sourceLocation, arbitrary extra keys
catalog.notes: What GCP apps print BEFORE the platform wraps it into a LogEntry; seen raw in container logs and local dev. The slash-namespaced keys are the strong fingerprint.

catalog.name: gem5 simout / console
catalog.sample_line: info: Entering event queue @ 0.  Starting simulation...
catalog.detect_signature: Level prefixes 'info:'/'warn:'/'panic:'/'fatal:'/'hack:' at line start; startup 'Global frequency set at N ticks per second'; DPRINTF lines 'tick: object: message'
catalog.fields: level(info/warn/panic/fatal); message; DPRINTF: tick, SimObject name, debug msg
catalog.notes: simout in m5out/. gem5 version banner, 'Global frequency set at', 'Beginning simulation!', 'Exiting @ tick N because <reason>'. Debug flags emit 'tick: system.cpu: ...'.

catalog.name: glassfish-access-log
catalog.product: GlassFish / Payara HTTP access log (server_access_log.<ts>.txt, virtual-server access logging) — fully double-quoted variant of CLF
catalog.detect_signature: ^"[^"]+" "[^"]*" "\d{2}/[A-Z][a-z]{2}/\d{4}:\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} [+-]\d{4}" "[A-Z]+ [^"]* HTTP/\d\.\d" \d{3} \d+ — every field double-quoted including the timestamp (no square brackets), literal NULL-AUTH-USER for anonymous
catalog.fields: client.name (quoted IP), auth-user-name (NULL-AUTH-USER when absent), datetime (quoted, CLF date grammar without []), request, status, response.length — default pattern %client.name% %auth-user-name% %datetime% %request% %status% %response.length%
catalog.notes: Distinct enough from CLF (quotes everywhere, no brackets) to need its own detect; unquoted trailing tokens appear if the format is customized.

catalog.name: gobgp-json-log
catalog.sample_line: {"Key":"10.0.255.1","State":"BGP_FSM_OPENCONFIRM","Topic":"Peer","level":"info","msg":"Peer Up","time":"2018-03-11T00:44:41+09:00"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON object with logrus keys level/msg/time PLUS gobgp keys Topic (Peer|Config|Server|Zebra) and Key/State BGP_FSM_*
catalog.fields: time RFC3339, level, msg, Topic->category, Key (peer ip)->trace_id, State, extra structured fields
catalog.notes: Also has a logrus text mode (time="..." level=info msg="...") which the existing logfmt/logrus adapters may already catch; JSON mode with Topic is the distinct one.

catalog.name: gpfs-mmfs-log
catalog.product: IBM Storage Scale / GPFS mmfs.log and mm-command output (6027-xxxx message codes)
catalog.sample_line: Fri Dec 29 18:26:11 CST 2023: 6027-1623 mmmount: Mounting file systems ...
catalog.detect_signature: IBM message code '6027-NNNN' after timestamp or 'GPFS:' prefix; commands mmmount/mmcrfs/mmcrnsd; log file /var/adm/ras/mmfs.log.latest
catalog.fields: ts (asctime + TZ), msg_code (6027-xxxx), component/command, message; severity letters [E]/[W]/[I]/[N] in newer releases
catalog.notes: Verbatim lines from bond-huang/ebook GPFS install doc: 'GPFS: 6027-540 Formatting file system ...', 'mmcrfs: 6027-1371 Propagating the cluster configuration data to all'. All Scale messages carry the 6027- prefix — a single msg-code lookup covers the product.

catalog.name: grafana-alloy-agent-logfmt
catalog.product: Grafana Alloy / Grafana Agent (flow) internal log
catalog.sample_line: ts=2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z level=info msg="now listening for http traffic" component_path=/ component_id=http addr=127.0.0.1:12345
catalog.detect_signature: logfmt with ts=/level=/msg= plus component_path= and component_id= keys (Alloy-specific)
catalog.fields: ts, level, msg, component_path (/ hierarchy), component_id (e.g. prometheus.scrape.default), node_id

catalog.name: graylog-server-log
catalog.sample_line: 2023-01-01T12:00:00.123+02:00 INFO  [ServerBootstrap] Graylog server up and running.
catalog.fields: ISO ts with colon offset, LEVEL padded, [SimpleClassName], message; java stack traces follow unindented

catalog.name: greenplum-csv-log
catalog.sample_line: 30-column CSV per gpdb docs: event_time,user_name,database_name,process_id(pNNN),thread_id(thNNN),remote_host,remote_port,session_start_time,transaction_id,gp_session_id(conNN),gp_command_count(cmdNN),gp_segment(segN/-1),slice_id,distr_tranx_id,local_tranx_id,sub_tranx_id,event_severity,sql_state_code,event_message,event_detail,event_hint,internal_query,internal_query_pos,event_context,debug_query_string,error_cursor_pos,func_name,file_name,file_line,stack_trace
catalog.detect_signature: CSV rows whose col4 matches ^p\d+$, col5 ^th\d+$, col10 ^con\d+ and col12 ^(seg\d+|mir\d+|-1)? — the p/th/con/cmd/seg prefixes are Greenplum-unique vs plain postgres csvlog
catalog.fields: see 30-column list; event_severity in {LOG,ERROR,FATAL,PANIC,DEBUG1,DEBUG2}; gp_session_id+gp_command_count correlate coordinator↔segment entries (trace_id candidate)
catalog.notes: Superset of postgres csvlog — must be detected BEFORE the generic postgres-csv adapter. Grounded from greenplum-db/gpdb-archive gpdb-doc admin_guide/managing/monitor.html.md.

catalog.name: gws-login-audit
catalog.product: Google Workspace Admin Reports API login/admin activity
catalog.sample_line: {"kind":"admin#reports#activity","id":{"time":"2024-01-01T10:00:00.000Z","applicationName":"login","customerId":"C03az79cb"},"actor":{"email":"jdoe@corp.com"},"ipAddress":"203.0.113.9","events":[{"type":"login","name":"login_success","parameters":[{"name":"login_type","value":"google_password"}]}]}
catalog.detect_signature: kind admin#reports#activity + id.applicationName + events[].name
catalog.fields: id.time, applicationName (login/admin/saml/token), actor.email, ipAddress, events[].name/type/parameters[]

catalog.name: h3c-comware-syslog
catalog.sample_line: %Jun 26 17:08:35:809 2013 H3C SHELL/5/SHELL_LOGIN: VTY logged in from 192.168.1.21
catalog.detect_signature: line (or syslog MSG part) starts with '%' + 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS:mmm YYYY' (milliseconds colon-separated, year AFTER time) + sysname + MODULE/SEV/MNEMONIC:
catalog.fields: ts (year-postfix), sysname, module, severity, mnemonic, message; newer Comware 7 adds -Slot=/-Chassis= location tokens
catalog.notes: The leading '%' and year-after-time ordering distinguish it from both Cisco and Huawei.

catalog.name: hbase-log4j
catalog.sample_line: 2019-03-27 09:02:05,779 ERROR [main] regionserver.HRegionServer: Failed construction RegionServer
catalog.detect_signature: hadoop-style envelope but SHORT logger names (regionserver.HRegionServer, master.HMaster, wal.FSHLog) instead of full org.apache.hadoop.* — '^ts LEVEL \[thread\] (regionserver|master|wal|zookeeper|coprocessor)\.\w+:'
catalog.fields: ts(comma millis), level, thread (RpcServer.handler=N, MemStoreFlusher, region names in thread), short logger, message; region encoded names + table names = correlation keys
catalog.notes: Sample from HDInsight troubleshooting doc. Distinguish from hadoop-daemon-log4j by the two-segment logger; GC-pause 'JvmPauseMonitor' lines shared with Hadoop.

catalog.name: hep3-capture
catalog.product: HEP3 / EEP (Homer Encapsulation Protocol) capture packets
catalog.sample_line: 48 45 50 33 01 4c  ('HEP3' magic + total length, then TLV chunks: 0000:0001 ip-family, 0000:0007 src-port, 0000:0009 ts-sec, 0000:0011 correlation-id, 0000:000f payload=raw SIP)
catalog.detect_signature: first 4 bytes == 'HEP3' (0x48455033); generic chunks vendor=0x0000 with 2-byte type + 2-byte length
catalog.fields: ip family/protocol, src/dst ip+port, tv_sec/tv_usec, capture-agent id, protocol-type (1=SIP), correlation-id, payload
catalog.notes: What Homer/heplify/sipcapture agents ship. tv_sec -> ts, correlation-id -> trace_id, payload -> sip-raw-message.

catalog.name: hivemq-event-log
catalog.sample_line: 2018-05-11 14:33:02,456 - Client ID: testClient, IP: 127.0.0.1, Clean Start: true, Session Expiry: 0 connected.
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3}\s*- Client ID: |- Outgoing publish message was dropped
catalog.fields: date, '- ', k:v event text: Client ID, IP, Clean Start, Session Expiry, verbs connected/disconnected gracefully/dropped, drop reason
catalog.notes: Pattern %-24(%d)- %msg%n%ex and event examples verified from docs.hivemq.com. No level column — category should be client-lifecycle; level=info except drop events (warn).

catalog.name: hivemq-log
catalog.sample_line: 2018-05-11 14:32:45,123 INFO - Started TCP Listener on address 0.0.0.0 and on port 1883
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3} (INFO|WARN|ERROR|DEBUG|TRACE)\s*-
catalog.fields: date HH:mm:ss,SSS + level padded into 30-char field, '- ', message, optional exception lines
catalog.notes: Pattern %-30(%d %level)- %msg%n%ex and sample line verified from docs.hivemq.com logging guide. No logger/thread column — distinguishes it from generic logback.

catalog.name: hl7v2-mllp-frame
catalog.product: HL7 MLLP (Minimal Lower Layer Protocol) wire framing — raw TCP captures / interface-engine wire logs
catalog.sample_line: \x0bMSH|^~\&|MegaReg|XYZHospC|SuperOE|XYZImgCtr|20060529090131-0500||ADT^A01^ADT_A01|01052901|P|2.5\x1c\x0d
catalog.detect_signature: Byte 0x0B (VT) immediately followed by 'MSH|', payload terminated by 0x1C 0x0D (FS CR); multiple frames may be concatenated in one capture
catalog.fields: Strip 0x0B/0x1C0x0D envelope then delegate to hl7v2-er7-message parser; frame boundaries define message boundaries -> one event per frame
catalog.notes: MLLP block format is the standard HL7 v2 transport (HL7 MLLP spec); envelope bytes are fixed constants. Inner sample is the verified Wikipedia message.

catalog.name: hpe-3par-syslog
catalog.product: HPE 3PAR StoreServ event/alert syslog (sw_cli audit + hardware events)
catalog.sample_line: May  1 12:00:00 3par01 3par01 sw_cli {admin super all} {createvv ...} {Error: ...} {}
catalog.detect_signature: tokens 'sw_cli {' user/role braces, 'hw_cage:', 'hw_cage_bat:', 'Cage N, Magazine', 'Interface Card N'; search key '3par_'
catalog.fields: component (sw_cli/hw_*), cli_username+role in braces, command, Error:, cage/magazine/interface-card ids, disk WWN magazine ids
catalog.notes: Fields and pre/post contexts extracted from VMware Log Insight content pack vmw-loginsight/vlcp content/HP-StoreFront_Analytics-v1.0.vlcp (com.hp.3par: hp_3par__cli_username preContext 'sw_cli \\{', hp_3par__cage_id preContext 'Cage ', hp_3par__hw_cage etc.). Sample reconstructed from those anchors — needs raw fixture from 'showeventlog'/syslog forward.

catalog.name: hpe-data-protector-session-log
catalog.product: HPE / Micro Focus / OpenText Data Protector session messages (omnib output, session reports, Ob2EventLog)
catalog.sample_line:
[Normal] From: BSM@cellmgr.example.com "NightlyFS"  Time: 7/21/2026 2:00:01 AM
	Backup session 2026/07/21-1 started.
catalog.detect_signature: ^\[(Normal|Warning|Minor|Major|Critical)\] From: [A-Z]+@\S+ — severity bracket + agent@host header line, message on following indented line(s); session id pattern \d{4}/\d{2}/\d{2}-\d+
catalog.fields: severity → level (Normal=info, Minor/Major=warn/error, Critical=fatal), agent (BSM/VBDA/BMA → source), host, session_id → trace_id, ts (locale), indented message body
catalog.notes: Two-line record — header + indented body. Severity ladder is DP-specific and worth a mapping table.

catalog.name: hpux-syslog

catalog.notes: Framing is plain RFC3164, so this is a source-tagging variant rather than a new grammar: detect on path + vmunix/LVM vocabulary and set source=hpux. Sources: docstore.mik.ua HP-UX manual (LVM line quoted), Spiceworks HP-UX system logs thread.

catalog.name: ibmi-audit-syslog-forward

catalog.detect_signature: Standard RFC3164/5424 or CEF envelope whose device vendor/product is IBM/IBM i and whose signature id is the 2-char QAUDJRN entry type (+ subtype like PW-P); produced by the SQL syslog services or ports of MERLIN/PowerSC agents
catalog.fields: syslog/CEF envelope + audit entry type, user, job, object, source IP
catalog.notes: How IBM i shops feed SIEMs without raw journals. Sample reconstructed — verify exact CEF extension keys emitted by the QSYS2 service.

catalog.name: ibmi-display-journal-sql
catalog.product: IBM i QSYS2.DISPLAY_JOURNAL table function output (exported rows: audit + any journal)
