catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-21T15:40:39.123Z pid=12345 tid=abc123 class=HardWorker jid=9f8e7d INFO: start
catalog.detect_signature: '<ISO8601Z> pid=<n> tid=<hex> [class=.. jid=..] <LEVEL>: <message>' — logfmt-ish metadata (pid/tid/class/jid) then 'LEVEL: msg'
catalog.fields: ts, data.pid, data.tid, data.class (job), data.jid, level, message; source=Sidekiq
catalog.notes: Newer Sidekiq (6+) can emit JSON. The pid=/tid=/jid= tags correlate a job's start/done/fail lines. Failures append a Ruby backtrace.

catalog.name: siemens-s7-diagnostic-buffer
catalog.product: Siemens SIMATIC S7 PLC diagnostic buffer (STEP7/TIA Portal text export)
catalog.sample_line:
Event 1 of 10:  Event ID 16# 4302
Mode transition from STARTUP to RUN
catalog.detect_signature: ^Event \d+ of \d+:\s+Event ID 16# [0-9A-Fa-f]{4}
catalog.fields: event index, total count, Event ID (16# hex), descriptive text line(s), timestamp per entry (date/time of CPU clock), incoming/outgoing state, priority class/OB info
catalog.notes: Export layout from STEP7/TIA 'Save diagnostic buffer as text' as widely posted in Siemens forum threads; not re-verified this session (Siemens support pages gated) - confirm exact timestamp line format from a real .txt export.

catalog.name: sipp-error-log
catalog.sample_line: 2026-01-05 10:26:12.123456 1767608772.123456: Aborting call on unexpected message for Call-Id 'abc123@10.0.0.5': while expecting '200' response, received 'SIP/2.0 486 Busy Here'
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} [\d:]{8}\.\d{6} \d+\.\d{6}: (human ts + epoch.µs + ': ' prefix), messages mention Call-Id/unexpected message/discarding
catalog.fields: wall-clock ts, epoch ts, message (often includes Call-Id and received SIP snippet)
catalog.notes: Companion *_messages.log covered separately; *_screen.log and CSV stats (semicolon-separated StartTime;LastResetTime;CurrentTime;...) can be a later variant.

catalog.name: smf-cics-110
catalog.product: IBM CICS TS SMF type 110 (CICS monitoring facility + statistics)
catalog.sample_line: SMF110 subtype 1 = CMF performance class: dictionary-mapped fields per transaction (TRAN, USERID, response time, CPU, DB2/File wait counts); subtype 2 = interval statistics
catalog.detect_signature: SMF header SMFxRTY=0x6E; SMF product section contains 'CICS' + applid; monitoring records are dictionary-driven (dictionary record precedes data records in the stream)
catalog.fields: applid, transaction id, task number, userid, terminal, start/stop STCK, response time, dispatch/CPU/suspend breakdown, abend code
catalog.notes: Per-transaction telemetry = mainframe APM. Requires reading the in-stream dictionary record to decode field offsets — adapter must be stateful.

catalog.name: smf-db2-100-102
catalog.product: IBM Db2 for z/OS SMF types 100/101/102 (statistics, accounting, performance trace)
catalog.sample_line: SMF101 (accounting, IFCID 3): QWHS standard header (subsystem id, store clock timestamps) + QWAC accounting section (class 1/2 elapsed & CPU, getpages, locks)
catalog.detect_signature: SMF header SMFxRTY=0x64/0x65/0x66; Db2 self-defining section pointing to QWHSxxxx standard header with Db2 ssid; IFCID number identifies the trace record
catalog.fields: Db2 subsystem, plan/package, auth id, correlation id, IFCID, class1/class2 times, SQL counts, buffer-pool getpages, deadlock/timeout details (IFCID 172/196)
catalog.notes: Usually post-processed by OMEGAMON/DB2PM; raw layout documented in Db2 SDSNMACS (DSNDQWHS etc.).

catalog.name: smf-rmf-70-79
catalog.product: IBM z/OS RMF/SMF types 70-79 (performance: CPU, paging, workload, device)
catalog.sample_line: SMF70: interval CPU activity — product section carries RMF interval start/length, CPU-data sections per processor (wait time, online time), LPAR partition data sections
catalog.detect_signature: SMF header SMFxRTY in 0x46-0x4F; RMF product section (interval start time, cycle) at first triplet; type 70=CPU/LPAR, 71=paging, 72=workload/service class, 74=device/XCF, 78=I/O queuing
catalog.fields: interval start/duration, per-CPU busy/wait, LPAR weights, service-class response times, device activity rates
catalog.notes: Metrics-shaped rather than event-shaped; normalize as periodic samples. Layouts in SYS1.MACLIB ERBSMFR mappings.

catalog.name: smf-tcpip-119
catalog.product: IBM z/OS Communications Server SMF type 119 (TCP/IP connections, FTP, Telnet)
catalog.sample_line: SMF119 subtype 2 = TCP connection termination: local/remote IP+port, bytes in/out, start/end times, userid, jobname; subtype 70/72 = FTP client/server transfer completion
catalog.detect_signature: SMF header SMFxRTY=0x77; TCP/IP identification section (stack name, sysplex) + per-subtype sections; IPv4/IPv6 addresses in binary
catalog.fields: stack name, connection 4-tuple, byte counts, duration, TLS info, FTP dataset/file name, login userid
catalog.notes: Mainframe equivalent of network flow logs; heavily used in security monitoring.

catalog.name: smf115-116-mq
catalog.product: IBM MQ for z/OS SMF types 115/116 (statistics/accounting)
catalog.sample_line: <SMF hdr rty=115|116 + QWHS header + statistic blocks (QSST storage, QJST log, QMST msg mgr) / type 116 per-task WTAS/WQST queue accounting>
catalog.detect_signature: SMF types 115 (qmgr statistics) and 116 (class-3 task/queue accounting) with MQ QWHS self-defining sections
catalog.fields: qmgr, interval, log/buffer/lock stats, per-queue puts/gets, CPU per task
catalog.notes: Decoded by MP1B/AMQSMF-style tools; EBCDIC binary.

catalog.name: smf119-commserver-tcpip
catalog.product: IBM z/OS Communications Server SMF type 119 (TCP/IP + zERT)
catalog.sample_line: <SMF hdr rty=0x77 + TCP/IP identification section + subtype sections: 2=TCP connection termination (src/dst IP:port, bytes, duration), 70=FTP server transfer, 11/12=zERT connection/summary (crypto protocol, cipher)>
catalog.detect_signature: SMF type 119 with subtype in extended header; self-defining triplets to identification + subtype-specific sections; IPs stored as IPv6-mapped binary
catalog.fields: subtype, stack name, local/remote ip+port, bytes in/out, start/end, userid, FTP command/file, zERT: protocol (TLS/SSH/IPsec), cipher, key length
catalog.notes: zERT (subtypes 11/12) is the modern crypto-posture feed auditors ask for; FTP/Telnet subtypes double as access logs.

catalog.name: smf120-websphere-liberty
catalog.product: IBM WebSphere/Liberty for z/OS SMF type 120 (request accounting)
catalog.sample_line: <SMF hdr rty=0x78 + subtype 9 (request activity) / 11 (Liberty request): server name, URI, userid, CPU on GP vs zIIP, response time, bytes>
catalog.detect_signature: SMF type 120 with subtype 9/11/12 and WebSphere/Liberty self-defining sections (server info, request info, network info)
catalog.fields: subtype, server, uri, userid, start/stop STCK, cpu (GP/zIIP), bytes rx/tx, completion code
catalog.notes: Complements the already-cataloged Liberty text logs with the z/OS-only binary accounting form.

catalog.name: snmp-trap-pdu
catalog.product: Raw SNMP trap/inform PDU on the wire (UDP 162)
catalog.sample_line: BER: 30 <len> 02 01 01 04 06 'public' a7 <len> ... (SEQUENCE, version int 0=v1/1=v2c/3=v3, community, PDU tag 0xA4=v1-Trap / 0xA7=SNMPv2-Trap / 0xA6=Inform)
catalog.detect_signature: UDP dst port 162, payload starts 0x30 (BER SEQUENCE), version INTEGER 0/1/3, PDU context tag a4/a6/a7
catalog.fields: v1: enterprise OID, agent-addr, generic-trap, specific-trap, timestamp, varbinds; v2c/v3: request-id + varbinds incl sysUpTime.0 and snmpTrapOID.0
catalog.notes: For pcap/socket ingestion paths; most deployments will hit the snmptrapd text adapter instead. v3 adds USM security envelope (may be encrypted).

catalog.name: snort-syslog-alert
catalog.sample_line: Mar  3 22:06:32 sensor1 snort[1234]: [1:1418:11] SNMP request tcp [Classification: Attempted Information Leak] [Priority: 2] {TCP} 192.168.1.5:40144 -> 10.0.0.9:161
catalog.detect_signature: syslog tag 'snort[pid]:' followed by [gid:sid:rev] and {PROTO} src -> dst
catalog.fields: gid,sid,rev,message,classification,priority,proto,src,dst

catalog.name: snort_syslog
catalog.sample_line: Jan 24 12:34:00 ids snort[2451]: [1:2013028:6] ET POLICY curl User-Agent [Classification: Potentially Bad Traffic] [Priority: 2]: {TCP} 203.0.113.5:51882 -> 198.51.100.9:443
catalog.detect_signature: syslog envelope program 'snort'/'barnyard2' + '[gid:sid:rev] <msg> [Classification: ...] [Priority: N]: {PROTO}'
catalog.fields: syslog ts->ts; [gid:sid:rev]->data.signature_id; Priority->level; tuple->data
catalog.notes: Same alert content as fast.log but wrapped in syslog and without the leading MM/DD- timestamp (uses the syslog one).

catalog.name: snowflake-query-history
catalog.sample_line: Record shape (columns per Snowflake docs): {"QUERY_ID":"...","QUERY_TEXT":"...","QUERY_TYPE":"SELECT","SESSION_ID":123,"USER_NAME":"...","ROLE_NAME":"...","WAREHOUSE_NAME":"...","EXECUTION_STATUS":"SUCCESS|FAIL|INCIDENT","ERROR_CODE":n,"ERROR_MESSAGE":"...","START_TIME":...,"TOTAL_ELAPSED_TIME":ms,"BYTES_SCANNED":n}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON/CSV rows containing co-occurring keys QUERY_ID + WAREHOUSE_NAME + EXECUTION_STATUS (case-insensitive); execution_status enum success/fail/incident
catalog.fields: query_id, query_text, query_type, query_tag, session_id, user_name, role_name, database/schema, warehouse name/size/type/cluster, total_elapsed/execution/compilation/queuing times (ms), bytes_scanned, execution_status, error_code, error_message
catalog.notes: Not a file on disk — arrives as table exports / Snowpipe JSON. Map END_TIME→ts, execution_status fail→level=error. Column list grounded from docs.snowflake.com account-usage/query_history. Snowflake Event Tables (logs/traces) are a separate OTLP-like JSON format worth a follow-up.

catalog.name: sns-delivery-status-json
catalog.product: Amazon SNS delivery status logs (CloudWatch Logs, sns/region/acct/topic log groups)
catalog.sample_line: {"notification":{"timestamp":"2015-01-26 23:29:35.678","messageId":"c3ad79b0-8996-550a-8bfa-24f05989898f"},"delivery":{"statusCode":8,"dwellTimeMs":1451,"attempts":1,"providerResponse":"NotificationErrorResponse(command=8, status=InvalidToken, id=1, cause=null)","destination":"arn:aws:sns:us-east-2:111122223333:endpoint/APNS_SANDBOX/APNSPushApp/986cb8a1-..."},"status":"FAILURE"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with top-level keys notification{messageId,timestamp} + delivery{providerResponse|dwellTimeMs|destination}
catalog.fields: notification.messageId/timestamp/topicArn, delivery.destination arn, delivery.statusCode/dwellTimeMs/attempts/providerResponse, status SUCCESS|FAILURE
catalog.notes: Sample verified from AWS SNS developer guide (sns-msg-status.md, siagholami/aws-documentation mirror). Same envelope used for HTTP, Lambda, SQS, and mobile-push delivery status. trace_id <- notification.messageId.

catalog.name: softether-server-log
catalog.sample_line: 2023-01-15 12:00:00.123 On the TCP Listener (Port 5555), a Client (IP address 203.0.113.5, Host name "host1", Port number 50624) has connected.
catalog.detect_signature: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm ' + SoftEther English sentence templates ('On the TCP Listener', 'Session "SID-', 'a Client (IP address', 'VPN Client', 'Virtual Hub')
catalog.fields: ts (ms), prose message with embedded IP/hostname/port/session-id 'SID-NAME-N'
catalog.notes: Sentence-template prose; language of templates follows server locale (English/Japanese) — detect on ts shape + 'SID-' token as fallback.

catalog.name: solaris-bsm-praudit
catalog.product: Solaris/illumos BSM audit trail via praudit(8)
catalog.sample_line: header,69,2,su,,example-host,2026-07-20 14:33:05.121-07:00,subject,alice,root,staff,alice,staff,2001,1234,195 22 example-host
catalog.detect_signature: Comma-delimited token stream starting with 'header,<len>,<version>,<event>'; tokens named header/subject/return/path/attribute/exec_args/zone/trailer. -x variant is XML with <record>/<subject> tags; -l puts one record per line
catalog.fields: token type, byte count, version, audit event name, machine, ISO-ish timestamp, subject (audit-uid,uid,gid,ruid,rgid,pid,sid,tid), return status
catalog.notes: Underlying /var/audit/* files are binary BSM token streams (same lineage as macOS OpenBSM — reuse that parser core if present). Source: illumos praudit(8).

catalog.name: solaris-fmdump-ereport-nvlist
catalog.sample_line: Oct 06 2007 11:53:20.975021712 ereport.io.ddi.context
catalog.detect_signature: Header line 'Mon DD YYYY HH:MM:SS.nnnnnnnnn ereport.<class>' followed by 'nvlist version: 0' and indented 'key = value' pairs incl. 'class = ereport.', 'ena = 0x', 'detector = (embedded nvlist)', '__ttl', '__tod'
catalog.fields: nanosecond timestamp, ereport class, ena, detector nvlist (scheme/device-path), payload members; fmdump -Vj emits the same as JSON
catalog.notes: Multi-line nvlist record; the JSON variant (-j) is a separate easy parse. Source: illumos fmdump(8).

catalog.name: solaris-svcs-explain
catalog.sample_line: svc:/system/intrd:default (interrupt balancer)
catalog.detect_signature: Block: line starting 'svc:/...' with '(description)', followed by indented 'State: maintenance since ...', 'Reason: ...', 'See: http://illumos.org/msg/SMF-8000-..', 'See: /var/svc/log/...', 'Impact: N dependent services are not running.'
catalog.fields: fmri, description, state+since, reason, see-links (msg-id URL, man page, logfile), impact
catalog.notes: Multi-line record; anchor on 'State:' + 'Reason:' + 'Impact:' triplet under an svc:/ header.

catalog.name: solaris-svcs-list
catalog.sample_line: online         13:25:03 svc:/milestone/multi-user:default
catalog.detect_signature: Header 'STATE          STIME    FMRI' or lines with state keyword (online|offline|disabled|maintenance|degraded|legacy_run|uninitialized) + STIME + svc:/ or lrc:/ FMRI
catalog.fields: state, nstate (optional), stime (HH:MM:SS or Mon_DD), ctid, fmri
catalog.notes: Source: illumos svcs(1) EXAMPLES (quoted verbatim).

catalog.name: solaris_messages
catalog.sample_line: Jul 20 14:03:11 sunhost ufs: [ID 845546 kern.notice] alloc: /: file system full
catalog.detect_signature: rfc3164 ts + host + tag + '[ID <msgid> <facility>.<priority>]' bracket
catalog.fields: ts=BSD; host; module/tag; msgid=numeric inside [ID N facility.pri]; facility.priority dotted; message after bracket
catalog.notes: Solaris 8+ adds the '[ID msgid facility.priority]' block. msgid catalog is stable across boots. genunix/ufs/scsi common tags.

catalog.name: sonic-nos-syslog
catalog.sample_line: Aug 17 01:20:14.903331 sonic INFO swss#orchagent: :- setPortAdminStatus: Set port Ethernet0 admin status to up
catalog.detect_signature: syslog ts with 6-digit fractional seconds, hostname, UPPERCASE severity word (INFO/NOTICE/WARNING/ERR), then 'container#program:' token; message often begins ':- functionName:'
catalog.fields: ts.us, hostname, severity word, container, program, function?, message
catalog.notes: container#program (swss#orchagent, syncd#syncd, bgp#bgpd) maps cleanly to source; the FRR lines inside the bgp container also match frr-log.

catalog.name: sonicwall-syslog
catalog.detect_signature: body starts 'id=firewall sn=' with kv pairs pri= c= m= msg=; src/dst use ip:port:interface triplets
catalog.fields: id,sn,time,fw,pri,c(category bitmask),m(message id),msg,src,dst,proto,sent,rcvd,rule,app
catalog.notes: m= numeric message id keys the event type (83=port scan, 97=website hit, 537=connection closed).

catalog.name: sophos-xg-syslog
catalog.sample_line: device="SFW" date=2019-03-06 time=23:04:00 timezone="EST" device_name="XG330" device_id=A11111AAA1F9R30 log_id=010101600001 log_type="Firewall" log_component="Firewall Rule" log_subtype="Allowed" status="Allow" priority=Information duration=0 fw_rule_id=94 policy_type=1 user_name="" src_ip=10.1.1.5 src_port=51320 dst_ip=8.8.8.8 dst_port=53 protocol="UDP" in_interface="Port1" out_interface="Port2" sent_bytes=70 recv_bytes=140
catalog.detect_signature: line begins device="SFW" (or device="SFOS"); log_id= 12-digit + log_type=/log_component=/log_subtype= trio
catalog.fields: device,date,time,timezone,device_name,device_id,log_id,log_type,log_component,log_subtype,status,priority,fw_rule_id,src_ip,src_port,dst_ip,dst_port,protocol,sent_bytes,recv_bytes,url,category
catalog.notes: log_type also {ATP,IDP,Anti-Virus,Content Filtering,Event,WAF,VPN} — same kv shell. SFOS 20+ can emit the same fields as JSON (log format 'Standard Syslog Protocol' vs 'Device standard').

catalog.name: spamassassin-spamd-syslog
catalog.sample_line: Jul 20 09:01:04 mail spamd[17463]: spamd: identified spam (7.3/5.0) for jane:1001 in 2.1 seconds, 4096 bytes.
catalog.detect_signature: syslog tag spamd[pid]: message begins 'spamd: ' with verbs connection from, checking message, identified spam, clean message, result: Y/. score - USER_TESTS scantime=,size=,mid=
catalog.fields: verb, score/threshold, user:uid, elapsed, size; 'result:' lines: Y|. flag, score, comma-list of rule names, scantime, size, user, mid, autolearn

catalog.name: spark-eventlog-json
catalog.product: Apache Spark event log / History Server files (spark.eventLog.enabled)
catalog.sample_line: {"Event":"SparkListenerApplicationStart","App Name":"Spark Pi","App ID":"app-20210413122423-0000","Timestamp":1618341862473,"User":"xxxx"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON-lines where first line is {"Event":"SparkListenerLogStart","Spark Version":...} and every line has top-level "Event":"SparkListener*"
catalog.fields: Event(type), Timestamp(epoch ms), App ID/Name, User, Stage/Job/Task info objects, Executor IDs; App ID = trace_id, Event = category
catalog.notes: One JSON object per line, file named after app id (may be .lz4/.snappy compressed, or rolling dir eventlog_v2_<appId> in Spark 3). Verified via LucaCanali Spark_EventLog notes + Spark EventLoggingListener source.

catalog.name: spectrum-protect-server-actlog
catalog.product: IBM Storage Protect / TSM server activity log (q actlog output, console log) — ANR-prefixed messages
catalog.sample_line: 07/21/2026 02:00:01  ANR0406I Session 12345 started for node HOST1 (WinNT) (Tcp/Ip host1.example.com(51234)). (SESSION: 12345)
catalog.detect_signature: ANR\d{4}[IWESD] code after timestamp: ^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}\s+\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\s+ANR\d{4}[IWESD]\b
catalog.fields: ts, msg_code (ANR####sev), message, trailing structured context '(SESSION: n)'/'(PROCESS: n)' — extract as trace/session id
catalog.notes: Server-side sibling of ANS client codes; the trailing (SESSION:/PROCESS:) tag is a natural trace_id. Format from IBM docs; timestamp format follows server locale.

catalog.name: speedscope file format (generic)
catalog.sample_line: {"$schema":"https://www.speedscope.app/file-format-schema.json","profiles":[{"type":"evented","events":[{"type":"O","at":0,"frame":0}]}],"shared":{"frames":[{"name":"main"}]}}
catalog.detect_signature: `$schema` == speedscope schema URL; `profiles[].type` in {evented,sampled}; `shared.frames`
catalog.fields: $schema, name, activeProfileIndex, shared.frames[{name,file,line,col}], profiles[{type,unit,startValue,endValue, events|samples+weights}]
catalog.notes: Import target for perf/py-spy/Instruments/pprof. evented uses O/C open/close events; sampled uses samples[frameIdx[]]+weights.

catalog.name: spinnaker-springboot
catalog.sample_line: 2016-09-06 16:33:06.126  INFO 18 --- [           main] s.d.spring.web.caching.CachingAspect     : Caching aspect applied
catalog.detect_signature: Spring Boot default pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3}\s+(TRACE|DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR)\s+\d+ --- \[[^\]]+\] [\w.$]+\s*: — the ' --- [thread]' separator is the tell
catalog.fields: ts, level, pid, thread, abbreviated logger class, message
catalog.notes: Generic Spring Boot adapter also covers many Java IaC/CD servers (Nexus, older Jenkins plugins, etc.) — worth a shared adapter with product tagging.

catalog.name: splunkd-log
catalog.sample_line: 01-01-2023 12:00:00.123 +0000 INFO  TailReader [12345 tailreader0] - Batch input finished reading file='/var/log/app.log'
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{4} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3} [+-]\d{4} (DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR|FATAL) \s?\w+ (\[\d+ [^\]]+\] )?- — note MM-DD-YYYY date order
catalog.fields: MM-DD-YYYY ts.mmm +offset, LEVEL, Component (TailReader, TcpOutputProc, Metrics, HttpListener), optional [tid threadname], ' - ' then message with key=value / key='value' pairs

catalog.name: squid-access-combined
catalog.product: Squid access.log with built-in 'combined' logformat (NCSA combined + squid trailer)
catalog.sample_line: logformat combined %>a - %[un [%tl] "%rm %ru HTTP/%rv" %>Hs %<st "%{Referer}>h" "%{User-Agent}>h" %Ss:%Sh   (official built-in definition, verbatim from squid src/cf.data.pre line 5238)
catalog.detect_signature: NCSA combined-shaped line (two trailing quoted strings for Referer/User-Agent) followed by ONE extra unquoted token ^[A-Z_]+:[A-Z_]+$ (squid result:hierarchy) after the closing quote
catalog.fields: same as NCSA combined plus squid.result_code and squid.hierarchy_code from the trailer
catalog.notes: Disambiguation from apache combined = the trailing TCP_*:*_* token. Reuse combined parser + trailer split.

catalog.name: squid-access-common
catalog.product: Squid access.log with built-in 'common' logformat (CLF + squid trailer)
catalog.sample_line: logformat common %>a - %[un [%tl] "%rm %ru HTTP/%rv" %>Hs %<st %Ss:%Sh   (official built-in definition, verbatim from squid src/cf.data.pre line 5237; emitted lines are CLF followed by e.g. TCP_MISS:HIER_DIRECT)
catalog.detect_signature: CLF-shaped line whose LAST token matches ^[A-Z_]+:[A-Z_]+$ with left side a squid result code (TCP_HIT|TCP_MISS|TCP_DENIED|TCP_TUNNEL|...) and right side a hierarchy code (HIER_DIRECT|HIER_NONE|DIRECT|NONE|...) — distinguishes it from plain Apache CLF
catalog.fields: client_ip, '-', user, [local time %tl e.g. 10/Oct/2023:02:30:10 +0000], "method url HTTP/version", status, bytes, result:hierarchy trailer
catalog.notes: Route through existing CLF parser then peel the %Ss:%Sh trailer into squid.result_code/squid.hierarchy_code. No independently captured wild sample located; format string is authoritative from squid source.

catalog.name: squid-store-log
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{9,10}\.\d{3} (CREATE|RELEASE|SWAPOUT|SWAPIN) -?\d+ [0-9A-F]{8} [0-9A-F]{32} — epoch.millis, action verb, dir number, hex file number (FFFFFFFF = memory-only), 32-hex MD5 key
catalog.fields: 13 space-separated columns per squid wiki: time(UTC epoch.millis), action(CREATE|RELEASE|SWAPOUT|SWAPIN), dir_number, file_number(hex, FFFFFFFF if never stored), md5_hash(32 hex), http_status, date_hdr(epoch), lastmod(epoch, -1 if absent), expires(epoch, -1), content_type, sizes(advertised/actual slash-separated), method, key(usually URL). printf format documented as %9ld.%03d %-7s %02d %08X %s %4d %9ld %9ld %9ld %s %ld/%ld %s %s
catalog.notes: Sample is a real captured line (github dev-bazz/proxy-server logs/store.log); field list verified from wiki.squid-cache.org/SquidFaq/SquidLogs. SWAPOUT=cached, RELEASE=uncached-or-evicted. Off by default in modern squid (cache_store_log).

catalog.name: squid_access
catalog.sample_line: 1682942400.123    215 10.0.0.5 TCP_MISS/200 3456 GET http://example.com/ - HIER_DIRECT/93.184.216.34 text/html
catalog.detect_signature: line begins with epoch.millis then elapsed ms, client ip, 'RESULT_CODE/STATUS' token (TCP_MISS/200)
catalog.fields: ts(epoch.ms), duration_ms, client_ip, Squid_result/http_status, bytes, method, url, rfc931, hierarchy/peer, content_type -> data; 4xx/5xx or TCP_DENIED->WARN
catalog.notes: Squid result codes (TCP_MISS, TCP_DENIED, TCP_HIT) precede the HTTP status via '/'. Epoch-with-ms timestamp. Common on egress proxies/security gateways.

catalog.name: squidguard-log
catalog.sample_line: 2012-10-25 14:13:14 [31277] Request(default/adult/-) http://static.videohub.com/core/core-as3-v5.0.0.swf 10.10.30.17/- - GET REDIRECT
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} \[\d+\] Request\([^)]+\) \S+ \S+/\S+ \S+ [A-Z]+ (REDIRECT|PASS|BLOCK) — ISO-ish date, [pid], Request(profile/category/rule)
catalog.fields: ts YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS; pid in brackets; Request(acl_profile/target_category/rewrite_rule); url; client (ip/domain or ip/-); ident user ('-'); method; action (REDIRECT etc.). Non-request lines are daemon status: 'squidGuard ready for requests', 'init domainlist ...'
catalog.notes: Sample verified from wallix/pylogsparser squidguard.xml normalizer (documented pattern: DATE [PID] Request(CATEGORY) URL FROM/DOMAIN IDENT METHOD ACTION). Extremely common on pfSense/school filters alongside squid.

catalog.name: srun / mpirun per-rank prefixed lines
catalog.sample_line: 3: Hello from rank 3 of 16
catalog.detect_signature: /^\d+: / integer-colon prefix on every line (srun --label prepends the task rank)
catalog.fields: task_rank(int); message
catalog.notes: srun --label prepends the step task id. Simple but common; distinguish from OpenMPI [j,r]<stream> form.

catalog.name: stepfunc-dnp3-tracing
catalog.product: Step Function I/O dnp3 (Rust/C/.NET DNP3 library) tracing output
catalog.sample_line: INFO DNP3-Master-TCP{endpoint="127.0.0.1:20000"}: connected to 127.0.0.1:20000
catalog.detect_signature: DNP3-(Master|Outstation)-(TCP|TLS|Serial)\{|^APP (TX|RX) - ctrl: \[fir:
catalog.fields: level, tracing span (component + endpoint KVs), message; protocol decode lines APP TX/RX with ctrl flags [fir/fin/con/uns], func, object headers
catalog.notes: Samples quoted from docs.stepfunc.io dnp3 0.9.1 logging guide (Rust tracing-crate format, span fields configurable).

catalog.name: storm-log4j2
catalog.sample_line: 13:02:02.098 [main] INFO  o.a.s.d.s.Supervisor - Starting Supervisor with conf
catalog.detect_signature: time-only or full ts + ' [thread] LEVEL o.a.s.... - msg' — 1.-abbreviated logger o.a.s.* plus dot-millis; worker.log variant prefixes yyyy-MM-dd
catalog.fields: ts(HH:mm:ss.SSS, worker files add date), thread (executor threads named Thread-N-<component>-executor[x x]), level, abbreviated logger (%c{1.}), message; topologyId in path + messages
catalog.notes: Real lines from Storm startup pastebin (topology countApp-1-1462550522). Worker logs live at workers-artifacts/<topologyId>/<port>/worker.log — the path itself carries trace context.

catalog.name: strace -c summary table
catalog.sample_line: % time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall\n 40.00    0.001234          61        20         2 openat
catalog.detect_signature: Header `% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall` then aligned rows, dashed separator, total row
catalog.fields: % time, seconds, usecs/call, calls, errors, syscall name
catalog.notes: Produced by -c/-C. Ends with `------` line and `100.00 ... total`.

catalog.name: strongswan_ipsec
catalog.sample_line: Jan 24 12:44:10 vpn charon: 09[IKE] <conn-a|3> IKE_SA conn-a[3] established between 198.51.100.1[vpn.example.com]...203.0.113.9[client]
catalog.detect_signature: program 'charon'/'pluto'/'ipsec' + '<threadid>[<SUBSYS>]' bracket (SUBSYS in {IKE,ENC,NET,CFG,CHD,MGR}) + optional '<conn|uniqueid>' tag
catalog.fields: [SUBSYS]->category; conn name/unique id->trace_id; 'IKE_SA established/CHILD_SA established/deleting'->data+level; peer IPs->data
catalog.notes: charon uses '<threadid>[SUBSYS] <ikesa|uniqueid> message'. Libreswan/pluto differs slightly. Success/failure keywords: 'established', 'authentication failed', 'received DELETE'.

catalog.name: structlog_keyvalue
catalog.sample_line: event='user logged in' level='info' timestamp='2023-11-08T15:28:26Z' user_id=42
catalog.detect_signature: pure key=value stream that always contains event=... and usually level=... and timestamp=...; values single-quoted when spaces present
catalog.fields: message←event, level←level, ts←timestamp, everything else→data.*
catalog.notes: Overlaps generic logfmt (already covered) but the mandatory event= key and single-quote quoting style are the structlog fingerprint. Key order is insertion order, not fixed.

catalog.name: stunnel-log
catalog.sample_line: 2023.01.15 12:00:00 LOG5[0]: Service [https] accepted connection from 203.0.113.5:50624
catalog.detect_signature: dot-separated date 'YYYY.MM.DD HH:MM:SS' + 'LOGn[tid]:' token (n=syslog severity 0-7)
catalog.fields: ts, severity digit (syslog scale), thread/connection id, service name in brackets, message
catalog.notes: 'LOG5[' token is unique; severity digit maps directly onto the unified level enum.

catalog.name: su
catalog.sample_line: Jan 24 12:18:03 web1 su[20512]: FAILED SU (to root) alice on pts/1
catalog.detect_signature: program 'su' with message '(FAILED SU|Successful su) ... (to <user>) <user> on <tty>' or PAM session lines
catalog.fields: FAILED/Successful->level; to <user>->data.target; actor+tty->data
catalog.notes: Small fixed template set; pairs with pam_unix session lines. Lower volume than sshd/sudo.

catalog.name: sudo-json
catalog.sample_line: {"sudo":{"accept":{"uuid":"616bc9efcf-b239-469d-60ee-deb5af8ce6","server_time":{"seconds":1643379862},"submituser":"czanik","command":"/bin/bash","runuser":"root","ttyname":"/dev/pts/0","submitcwd":"/home/czanik"}}}
catalog.detect_signature: top-level key "sudo" containing accept|reject|alert|exit object with submituser/runuser/command
catalog.fields: event class, uuid, server_time/submit_time, submituser, runuser, rungroup, command, runargv, ttyname, submithost, lines/columns
catalog.notes: Enabled via 'Defaults log_format=json' or sudo_logsrvd; sudo.ws/posts/2020/12/sudo-1.9.4-new-options-for-logging/

catalog.name: suricata-fast-log
catalog.sample_line: 07/16/2015-01:32:12.275324  [**] [1:2008983:6] ET USER_AGENTS Suspicious User Agent (BlackSun) [**] [Classification: A Network Trojan was detected] [Priority: 1] {TCP} 10.0.2.15:49779 -> 74.125.28.99:80
catalog.detect_signature: MM/DD/YYYY-HH:MM:SS.ffffff timestamp then ' [**] [gid:sid:rev] ' ... '[Classification: ...] [Priority: N] {PROTO} ip:port -> ip:port'
catalog.fields: timestamp,gid,sid,rev,signature,classification,priority,proto,src_ip,src_port,dst_ip,dst_port
catalog.notes: Nearly identical to snort fast alert but timestamp includes year (MM/DD/YYYY vs Snort MM/DD).

catalog.name: swift-storage-node-access
catalog.product: Swift account-server, container-server, object-server request logs (syslog)
catalog.sample_line: TEMPLATE (verified from Swift docs): remote_addr - - [datetime] "request_method request_path" status_int content_length "referer" "transaction_id" "user_agent" request_time additional_info server_pid policy_index
catalog.detect_signature: CLF-like line but with a quoted Swift transaction id ('"tx[0-9a-f]{21}-…"') in the position CLF/NCSA would not have one, followed by float request_time and trailing pid + policy_index integers
catalog.fields: remote_addr, datetime, request_method, request_path, status_int, content_length, referer, transaction_id(trace_id), user_agent, request_time, additional_info, server_pid, policy_index
catalog.notes: Format verified verbatim from docs.openstack.org/swift/latest/logs.html. Distinguish from Apache CLF by the quoted tx-id field and the extra trailing numeric fields; correlates with swift-proxy-access via transaction_id.

catalog.name: switch_nxlink
catalog.product: Nintendo Switch homebrew stdout/stderr over nxlink (devkitPro libnx)
catalog.sample_line:
main: initializing gfx
player spawned at (0.0, 1.5, 0.0)
catalog.detect_signature: Plain printf/puts text streamed over TCP to `nxlink -s`; no framing beyond newlines; context is 'received via nxlink NetLoader'
catalog.fields: data.message=raw text; no level/ts unless the app prints its own
catalog.notes: nxlinkStdio() redirects stdout/stderr over TCP after socketInitializeDefault(). Format is whatever the homebrew printf-s — essentially raw. Same story for devkitPro 3DS (3dslink) and Wii/GC. Source: devkitpro.org, egetrickrolled homebrew guide.

catalog.name: symantec-event-export-json
catalog.product: Symantec Endpoint Security (SES cloud Event Export / ICDm, JSON)
catalog.sample_line: {"type_id":8001,"time":"2022-07-11T20:33:24.000Z","device_name":"win-desktop01","user_name":"jdoe","threat":{"name":"Trojan.Gen.2","file":{"path":"C:\\Users\\jdoe\\evil.exe","sha2":"abc..."}},"disposition":"Quarantined","severity_id":5,"product_name":"Symantec Endpoint Security"}
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with numeric "type_id" + "severity_id" + "product_name" containing "Symantec"; nested threat.file object with sha2
catalog.fields: type_id (numeric event class), time (ISO8601), device_name, user_name, threat{name,file{path,sha2,md5}}, disposition, severity_id, product_name, feature_name
catalog.notes: Cloud SES event export (Chronicle 'symantec-event-export' parser). Numeric type_id/severity_id + nested threat object distinguish it from on-prem SEP CSV.

catalog.name: symantec-sep-av-export-csv
catalog.product: Symantec Endpoint Protection (SEP risk/AV log exported to text, CSV)
catalog.sample_line: 2020-01-16 08:00:31,Critical,WIN-DESKTOP01,Trojan.Gen.2,C:\Users\jdoe\evil.exe,jdoe,Quarantine,Cleaned,Auto-Protect,1,SHA256,abc...
catalog.detect_signature: CSV whose first two columns are an event time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) and a Symantec severity word (Critical/Major/Minor/Info); risk-name and Actual/Requested action columns present
catalog.fields: Event time, Severity, Computer name, Risk name, Application/file path, User, Actual action, Requested action, Detection source (Auto-Protect/Scheduled Scan), Occurrences, Hash type, Application hash, Disposition
catalog.notes: SEP exported logs always start with event-time + severity columns (verified Broadcom KB). Field set from Broadcom exported-fields KB.

catalog.name: synology-dsm-syslog
catalog.product: Synology DSM NAS logs (synoscgi_SYNO.API.* / synoscimprofile / pam over ISO8601 syslog)
catalog.sample_line: 2024-09-10T07:25:27+08:00 Synology_NAS synoscgi_SYNO.API.Auth_7_login[13748]: pam_unix(webui:auth): authentication failure; logname= uid=0 euid=0 tty= ruser= rhost=10.0.0.147  user=Allen
catalog.detect_signature: program names 'synoscgi_SYNO.API.<Service>_<ver>_<method>' or syno* daemons; ISO8601+TZ timestamp first token; DSM source-file 'path.h:line LEVEL:' style in syno daemons
catalog.fields: iso_ts, hostname, syno program (API service/version/method), pid, pam module fields (rhost/user) or file:line + LEVEL + message
catalog.notes: Verbatim from yfeng445/Synology successful_logins.log (also shows 'synoscimprofile[21731]: ../..//include/converter/../dao/BaseDao.h:21 ERROR: setresuid...'). Covers the huge prosumer/SMB NAS install base; QNAP is the analogous gap.

catalog.name: syslog-ng-internal
catalog.sample_line: syslog-ng[2134]: syslog-ng starting up; version='3.38.1'
catalog.detect_signature: syslog-ng\[\d+\]: .*; ([a-z_]+='[^']*'(, )?)+$ (semicolon then key='value' comma list)
catalog.fields: message clause ';' then key='single-quoted-value' pairs (version=, filename=, error=, processed=); includes periodic 'Log statistics;' lines

catalog.name: syslog_ng_template
catalog.sample_line: 2026-07-20T14:03:11+00:00 myhost prg: message
catalog.detect_signature: configurable; ISODATE template = RFC3339; default = rfc3164
catalog.fields: template-defined; commonly ts(ISODATE/BSD); host; program[pid]; message
catalog.notes: syslog-ng templates are user-configurable but ISODATE ($ISODATE) and default($DATE BSD) dominate. Parser can fall back to rfc5424/3164/filefmt detectors.

catalog.name: sysmon-file-create-xml
catalog.sample_line: <EventData><Data Name="UtcTime">2020-07-29 04:20:00.100</Data><Data Name="ProcessGuid">{e8a2...}</Data><Data Name="Image">C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe</Data><Data Name="TargetFilename">C:\Users\Public\dropper.ps1</Data><Data Name="CreationUtcTime">2020-07-29 04:20:00.099</Data></EventData>
catalog.detect_signature: Sysmon provider AND EventID in {11,15,23,26}; Data-Name TargetFilename (+Hash/Contents for 15, +Archived for 23)
catalog.fields: UtcTime, ProcessGuid, Image, TargetFilename, CreationUtcTime, Hash (id 15), Contents, IsExecutable, Archived (id 23)

catalog.name: sysmon-image-load-xml
catalog.sample_line: <EventData><Data Name="UtcTime">2020-07-29 03:55:01.010</Data><Data Name="ProcessGuid">{e8a2...}</Data><Data Name="Image">C:\app.exe</Data><Data Name="ImageLoaded">C:\Windows\System32\amsi.dll</Data><Data Name="Signed">true</Data><Data Name="Signature">Microsoft Windows</Data><Data Name="SignatureStatus">Valid</Data><Data Name="Hashes">SHA256=...</Data></EventData>
catalog.detect_signature: Sysmon provider AND EventID==7; Data-Names ImageLoaded+Signed+SignatureStatus
catalog.fields: UtcTime, ProcessGuid, Image, ImageLoaded, FileVersion, Description, Product, Company, OriginalFileName, Hashes, Signed, Signature, SignatureStatus

catalog.name: sysmon-linux-syslog
catalog.sample_line: <Event><System><Provider Name="Linux-Sysmon" Guid="{ff032593-a8d3-4f13-b0d6-01fc615a0f97}"/><EventID>1</EventID></System><EventData><Data Name="UtcTime">2024-04-28 22:08:22.025</Data><Data Name="Image">/usr/bin/curl</Data><Data Name="CommandLine">curl http://evil/x</Data><Data Name="CurrentDirectory">/home/jdoe</Data></EventData></Event>
catalog.detect_signature: Provider Name="Linux-Sysmon" (Guid {ff032593-...}); same EventData Name-keyed layout as Windows Sysmon but with POSIX paths
catalog.fields: Provider(Linux-Sysmon), EventID (subset: 1,3,5,9,10,11,23), EventData: UtcTime, Image (POSIX path), CommandLine, CurrentDirectory, User, ProcessGuid
catalog.notes: Sysmon for Linux emits the same Windows-style XML schema (via syslog/journald) but Linux provider GUID and unix paths. Distinct provider name is the discriminator.

catalog.name: sysmon-pipe-wmi-xml
catalog.sample_line: <EventData><Data Name="EventType">CreatePipe</Data><Data Name="UtcTime">2020-07-29 04:40:00.000</Data><Data Name="ProcessGuid">{e8a2...}</Data><Data Name="PipeName">\PSEXESVC</Data><Data Name="Image">C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe</Data></EventData>
catalog.detect_signature: Sysmon provider AND EventID in {17,18} (Data-Name PipeName) OR {19,20,21} (Data-Names Operation+Consumer/Filter/Query)
catalog.fields: PipeEvent: EventType, PipeName, Image. WmiEvent: Operation, User, EventNamespace, Name, Query (19), Type/Destination (20), Consumer+Filter (21)

catalog.name: sysmon-registry-value-set-xml
catalog.sample_line: <EventData><Data Name="EventType">SetValue</Data><Data Name="UtcTime">2020-07-29 03:59:12.500</Data><Data Name="ProcessGuid">{e8a2...}</Data><Data Name="Image">C:\Windows\regedit.exe</Data><Data Name="TargetObject">HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\evil</Data><Data Name="Details">C:\Users\Public\evil.exe</Data></EventData>
catalog.detect_signature: Sysmon provider AND EventID in {12,13,14}; Data-Names EventType+TargetObject (+Details for 13, NewName for 14)
catalog.fields: EventType (CreateKey/DeleteKey/SetValue/RenameKey/RenameValue), UtcTime, ProcessGuid, Image, TargetObject, Details, NewName

catalog.name: systemd-networkd-dhcp
catalog.product: systemd-networkd DHCPv4/v6 client messages in journald
catalog.sample_line: systemd-networkd[321]: eth0: DHCPv4 address 192.168.1.100/24 via 192.168.1.1
catalog.detect_signature: unit 'systemd-networkd' + '<iface>: DHCPv4 address <ip>/<prefix> via <gw>' (also 'DHCPv6 address', 'DHCP lease lost', 'DHCPv4 connection considered critical')
catalog.fields: iface, ip/prefix, gateway/server, lease events
catalog.notes: Arrives through journald (already covered) but the payload grammar is DHCP-specific and worth structured extraction; companion state files /run/systemd/netif/leases/* are KEY=VALUE.

catalog.name: sysv-sulog
catalog.product: System V su log (/var/adm/sulog — Solaris, HP-UX, AIX)
catalog.sample_line: SU 07/20 14:33 + pts/1 alice-root
catalog.detect_signature: Line regex ^SU \d{2}/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2} [+-] \S+ \S+-\S+$ ; '+'=success '-'=failure, last field is fromuser-touser
catalog.fields: literal SU, MM/DD, HH:MM, success flag, tty, from-user'-'to-user
catalog.notes: Classic SysV format still produced on Solaris/HP-UX/AIX; no year in timestamp (needs file-mtime year inference).

catalog.name: tailscale-network-flow-json
catalog.product: Tailscale network flow logs (control-plane API / log streaming)
catalog.detect_signature: JSON with 'nodeId' + 'logged' + one of virtualTraffic/subnetTraffic/exitTraffic/physicalTraffic arrays
catalog.fields: nodeId, logged, start/end window, per-flow {proto (IANA), src, dst, txPackets, txBytes, rxPackets, rxBytes}, srcNode/dstNodes metadata (name, addresses, os, user/tags)
catalog.notes: Schema grounded from tailscale.com/kb/1219. Aggregated 5s windows, not per-packet; category split (virtual/subnet/exit/physical) belongs in data.

catalog.name: teamcity-service-messages
catalog.product: TeamCity service messages (build script → server protocol)
catalog.sample_line: ##teamcity[testStarted name='MyTest.test1' captureStandardOutput='true']
catalog.detect_signature: ^##teamcity\[\w+( \w+='(escaped)')*\]$ — message name (testStarted/testFailed/blockOpened/buildProblem/progressMessage/setParameter...) + single-quoted attrs with |-escaping (|n |r |' ||)
catalog.fields: messageName, attributes (name, duration, message, details, flowId, timestamp), TeamCity |-escape decoding

catalog.name: terragrunt-log
catalog.sample_line: time=2024-01-11T21:31:46Z level=info prefix=[/app/deployments/saws2-dev/us-west-2/squid] msg=Initializing the backend...
catalog.detect_signature: logfmt-ish line with time=,level=,msg= plus terragrunt-specific keys prefix=[<module path>] / tf-path=; JSON mode has {"level","msg","time","prefix"}; pretty format = 'HH:MM:SS.mmm LEVEL [module] msg'
catalog.fields: time, level, prefix (unit/module dir), tf-path, msg; wraps embedded terraform output

catalog.name: tibco-ems-server-log
catalog.detect_signature: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3} \S.*$ with no level token; startup lines 'Process started from', 'Server name:', 'Accepting connections on tcp://', 'Recovering state'
catalog.fields: timestamp (ms precision), free-text message; warnings/errors appear as 'WARNING:' or '[anonymous]@host' connection messages inline — no fixed level column
catalog.notes: Real lines verified from craignicholson/tibcoems-tutorials (tibemsd 8.x startup log). Level must be inferred from keywords (WARNING, Error, 'Server is active'). Also covers EMS $sys.monitor topic logs when dumped to file.

catalog.name: tomcat-access-valve
catalog.detect_signature: Base is NCSA common/combined (already-covered CLF grammar) — detect Tomcat variant by filename localhost_access_log* and by optional trailing extension tokens from patterns like %D (millis int), %S (session id hex), %I (thread name) appended after the CLF core
catalog.fields: client ip, ident, authuser, [ts], "request", status, bytes, then optional %D time-ms / %F commit-time / %S sessionid / %I thread per configured pattern
catalog.notes: Only worth a dedicated adapter for the Tomcat extensions + filename detect; pure common/combined lines should fall through to the existing CLF adapter.

catalog.name: topsecret-tss-audit
catalog.product: Broadcom (CA) Top Secret — TSS console messages + Audit/Tracking File (SMF)
catalog.sample_line: TSS7251E 226 J=PAYROLL  A=JSMITH   T=BATCH    F=NONE     - Password Is Incorrect
catalog.detect_signature: Console/syslog lines with message id ^TSS[0-9]{4}[EIW] followed by keyword=value pairs J=(jobname) A=(acid) T=(facility) F=(function); raw audit in site-assigned SMF type + Audit/Tracking File records reported via TSSUTIL
catalog.fields: message id, violation code, jobname, ACID (user), facility, function, resource, reason text
catalog.notes: Third mainframe ESM. The J=/A=/T=/F= keyword style is distinctive and easy to detect. Sample reconstructed from documented TSS message format — verify code/text pairing.

catalog.name: tornado_access
catalog.detect_signature: '[<L> <yymmdd> <HH:MM:SS> <module>:<line>] <status> <VERB> <path> (<ip>) <ms>ms' — single-char level 'I/W/E/D' and 6-digit date in bracket
catalog.fields: level (letter), ts (yymmdd + time), source (module:line), data.status/method/path/ip/duration_ms
catalog.notes: Tornado's LogFormatter default. Compact date. App logs share the '[L yymmdd HH:MM:SS module:line] msg' prefix without the request tail.

catalog.name: trace-cmd report
catalog.sample_line: ls-4262  [001] 212767.154882: sched_wakeup:         comm=ls pid=4262 prio=120 target_cpu=001
catalog.detect_signature: Same TASK-PID [CPU] TIMESTAMP: event: layout as ftrace but demuxed from trace.dat; no `#` tracer banner
catalog.fields: task-pid, cpu, timestamp, event name, decoded tracepoint fields
catalog.notes: Reads binary trace.dat. `-R` keeps raw event order; `-l` adds latency columns.

catalog.name: trellix-mcafee-epo-threat-cef
catalog.product: Trellix / McAfee ePolicy Orchestrator (ePO) + ENS (threat event, syslog CEF)
catalog.sample_line: CEF:0|McAfee|ePolicy Orchestrator|5.10.0|1027|Threat detected|7|rt=Jul 11 2022 20:33:24 dvchost=win-desktop01 suser=jdoe cs1=Endpoint Security cs1Label=Product cs2=Trojan-FGYK!ABCD cs2Label=ThreatName filePath=C:\Users\jdoe\evil.exe act=cleaned
catalog.detect_signature: CEF header vendor "McAfee" (newer: "Trellix") product "ePolicy Orchestrator"; numeric threat-event signatureId; cs*Label=Product/ThreatName
catalog.fields: CEF header (vendor=McAfee/Trellix, product=ePolicy Orchestrator), rt, dvchost, suser, cs1=Product(ENS/VSE), cs2=ThreatName, filePath, act (action), plus ThreatType/ThreatCategory/AnalyzerDetectionMethod
catalog.notes: ePO forwards ENS/VSE threat events as CEF. Vendor migrated McAfee->Trellix; detect() should accept both. Sample reflects documented ePO CEF layout — confirm numeric signatureIds against ePO event catalog.

catalog.name: trendmicro-visionone-cef
catalog.product: Trend Micro Vision One (XDR workbench/detection syslog, CEF)
catalog.sample_line: CEF:0|Trend Micro|Apex Central|2019|WB:12345|Workbench Alert|6|rt=Jul 11 2022 20:33:24 dvchost=win-desktop01 cs1=Possible Credential Dumping cs1Label=Workbench Model cs2=T1003 cs2Label=MITRE ATT&CK act=Detected
catalog.detect_signature: CEF header vendor "Trend Micro" with Vision One workbench event class prefix "WB:" and cs*Label mentioning "Workbench Model" / MITRE ATT&CK
catalog.fields: CEF header, rt, dvchost, cs1=Workbench Model name, cs2=MITRE technique, act, plus observed-attack-technique fields
catalog.notes: Vision One XDR correlated detections (workbench alerts). Carries MITRE technique mapping.

catalog.name: typesense-glog
catalog.product: Typesense (search/vector engine) server log — butil/brpc glog with 4-digit year
catalog.sample_line: I20220718 21:56:46.413625 8 typesense_server_utils.cpp:352] Starting Typesense 0.23.1
catalog.detect_signature: ^[IWEF]\d{8} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{6} \d+ [\w_]+\.(cpp|h):\d+\] ; discriminate from nebula via typesense source files (typesense_server_utils.cpp, raft_server.cpp, store.h, batched_indexer)
catalog.fields: level+date, time µs, thread id, file:line, message
catalog.notes: Verbatim from typesense/typesense issues (also captured docker-wrapped form with an outer RFC3339 ts prefix).

catalog.name: udhcpc-log
catalog.sample_line: udhcpc: lease of 172.16.0.2 obtained, lease time 86400
catalog.detect_signature: program 'udhcpc' with 'sending discover' / 'sending select for <ip>' / 'lease of <ip> obtained[ from <ip>], lease time <n>'
catalog.fields: phase, ip, optional server ip, lease seconds
catalog.notes: Ubiquitous on embedded firmware; often kern.info via -S syslog flag. Sibling udhcpd server logs 'sending OFFER of <ip>' / 'sending ACK to <ip>'.

catalog.name: unicorn_stdout
catalog.detect_signature: Ruby stdlib Logger default: '<S>, [<ISO8601 #pid>] <LEVEL> -- <progname>: <message>' where S is first letter of severity (I/E/W/D/F)
catalog.fields: level (letter + word), ts (bracket), data.pid, data.progname, message; source=Unicorn
catalog.notes: This is Ruby's built-in Logger format (also used by many raw Ruby scripts) — worth a general 'ruby_stdlib_logger' adapter. Distinct from Rails' formatter.

catalog.name: uv output / log
catalog.sample_line:
Resolved 34 packages in 12ms
Downloaded 5 packages in 340ms
Installed 34 packages in 89ms
 + requests==2.31.0
catalog.detect_signature: 'Resolved N packages in <t>', 'Installed N packages in <t>', ' + pkg==ver' / ' - pkg==ver' diff lines. Structured tracing via RUST_LOG/UV_LOG (tracing crate: 'TRACE uv_resolver: ...').
catalog.fields: action, count, duration, package, version
catalog.notes: Underlying Rust tracing gives 'LEVEL target: message' when RUST_LOG set.

catalog.name: uvicorn_default
catalog.sample_line:
INFO:     Started server process [12345]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
catalog.detect_signature: '<LEVEL padded to col>  <message>' with the same left-padded level prefix as the access log but free-text messages (Started server process, Application startup complete, etc.)
catalog.fields: level, message; no ts by default
catalog.notes: Companion to uvicorn_access. No timestamp unless log config adds asctime. Gunicorn+UvicornWorker mixes this with gunicorn error-log lines.

catalog.name: varnish-backend-health-vsl
catalog.product: Varnish backend health probe log (VSL Backend_health tag, via varnishlog -g raw -i Backend_health)
catalog.sample_line: Boot.default Still healthy 4---X-RH 4 3 5 0.001419 0.001784 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
catalog.detect_signature: (vcl_name)\.(backend_name) (Still healthy|Back healthy|Still sick|Went sick) [4-6UxXrRHE-]{8} \d+ \d+ \d+ [0-9.]+ [0-9.]+ — status phrase + 8-char probe-bits field + good/threshold/window counters
catalog.fields: backend=VCLname.backendname; transition (Still/Back/Went x healthy/sick); probe result bits (8 chars: 4=IPv4 6=IPv6 x=req-err X=req-sent r=resp-err R=resp-recvd H=happy E=exists); good_count threshold window; avg_response_time last_response_time; probe HTTP response ('HTTP/1.1 200 OK') or error ('Open error 111')
catalog.notes: Real lines verified from varnish-software troubleshooting tutorial: 'Boot.default Still sick -------- 2 3 5 0.000000 0.000000 Open error 111' and 'Boot.default Back healthy 4---X-RH 3 3 5 0.001177 0.001906 HTTP/1.1 200 OK'. catalog.name: windows-eventforwarding-collected
catalog.product: Windows Event Forwarding / WEC ForwardedEvents channel (WS-Man/SubscriptionManager, RenderingInfo blocks)

catalog.name: windows-rasclient-event

catalog.fields: username, connection name, ras error code (600-900 range: 809 NAT-T blocked, 812 policy, 691 auth)
catalog.notes: The de-facto diagnostic for every native Windows VPN failure; error-code table is a high-value enrichment.

catalog.name: windows-security-mitigations-exploitguard

catalog.name: windows_etw_tracefmt
catalog.product: Windows ETW trace (tracerpt/tracefmt/logman CSV or text)
catalog.sample_line: [0]0F70.1A34::2026-07-20 14:03:11.123456 [Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Process]Process 1234 started

catalog.notes: ETW is binary .etl; text forms come from tracefmt (WPP) or tracerpt (CSV/XML). WPP lines start with '[cpu]PID.TID::timestamp'. TraceLogging/EventSource decode similarly.

catalog.name: windows_firewall_log
catalog.detect_signature: a '#Fields:' header line ('#Fields: date time action protocol src-ip dst-ip ...') then space-separated rows with action DROP/ALLOW/OPEN/CLOSE

catalog.notes: W3C-extended-log-file style with '#Version'/'#Fields' preamble and '-' for empty. Similar structure to IIS but different field set. Space-separated.

catalog.name: windows_firewall_pfirewall
catalog.detect_signature: file has '#Fields:' header (date time action protocol src-ip dst-ip ...) then space-separated rows; action DROP/ALLOW

catalog.notes: W3C-style with '#Version/#Fields' header (share logic with IIS/W3C parsers). '-' = empty. Local-time timestamps.

catalog.name: wireguard-go-log
catalog.product: wireguard-go userspace daemon (also used by tailscaled internals)
catalog.sample_line: DEBUG: (wg0) 2023/01/15 12:00:00 peer(IQzM…FEqw) - Received handshake initiation
catalog.detect_signature: 'DEBUG: (ifname) ' or 'ERROR: (ifname) ' prefix + Go date + 'peer(AAAA…BBBB)' abbreviated-pubkey token with U+2026 ellipsis
catalog.fields: level (DEBUG/ERROR only), ifname, ts (Go 2006/01/02 15:04:05), peer key abbrev (first4…last4 of base64), message

catalog.name: x12-hipaa-edi
catalog.product: ASC X12 HIPAA EDI transactions — 837 claims, 835 remittance, 270/271 eligibility, 278 auth (clearinghouse/billing interface logs and drop files)
catalog.detect_signature: Interchange starts 'ISA*' with fixed-width 106-char ISA segment (element sep usually *, segment terminator ~); or transaction-level 'ST*837*'/'ST*835*'/'ST*270*' + implementation guide version like 005010X222; GS*HC (claims) / GS*HP (payment) functional groups
catalog.fields: ISA09+ISA10 or GS04+GS05 date+time -> ts; ISA13 interchange control number / ST02 -> trace_id; ST01 transaction code (837/835/270...) -> category; ISA06/ISA08 sender/receiver IDs -> source; BHT03 originator ID, BHT04/05 date/time; segment count SE01 consistency; full interchange -> raw
catalog.notes: Sample segments verified verbatim from x12.org/examples 005010X222 Example 01 (Commercial Health Insurance): ST*837*0021*005010X222~ BHT*0019*00*244579*20061015*1023*CH~ NM1*41... ISA/GS envelope layout is fixed by X12.5/X12.6 standards (published example omits envelope). Delimiters are declared positionally by the ISA segment itself — parser must read them, not assume '*'/'~'. PHI/claims data — masking support needed.

catalog.name: xbox_etw_etl
catalog.product: Xbox One / Xbox Series (and Windows) Event Tracing for Windows (.etl)
catalog.sample_line: (binary .etl; decoded via tracerpt/WPA to: EventName, PID, TID, TimeStamp, ProviderGuid, Level, Keyword, payload fields)
catalog.detect_signature: File magic: ETL WMI event-trace log header (starts with EVENT_TRACE_HEADER / logfile header 'RSDS'-adjacent); on Xbox produced by xbdiagcap.exe / xperf.exe
catalog.fields: after decode: ts=TimeStamp(FILETIME 100ns), level=Level(1-5 -> crit/err/warn/info/verbose), source=ProviderName/GUID, trace_id=ActivityId, data.message=formatted message, PID/TID
catalog.notes: Binary — needs tracerpt/logman/WPA or libtraceevent to decode to CSV/XML first, then map. Xbox tools: xbdiagcap.exe (preset providers), xperf.exe (general). Levels: 1=Critical 2=Error 3=Warning 4=Information 5=Verbose. Source: xboxoneresearch.github.io ETW wiki, MS Learn ETW.

catalog.name: xcodebuild-output

catalog.detect_signature: Lines of ' | '-separated columns: microsecond timestamp 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff | ' prefix, optional hostname column, Ansible-ish bodies ('TASK [', 'ok:', 'changed:', 'PLAY RECAP')
catalog.fields: timestamp, hostname(node), status(ok/changed/failed for result lines), message; TASK/PLAY markers give category=ci; multiline command output repeats the host column per line
catalog.notes: Separator and line-construction formats ('{now} | {msg}', '{host} | {status}: {msg}', continuation '{host} | {msg_line}') verified from zuul/ansible/base/callback/zuul_stream.py on opendev.org. Every OpenStack upstream CI log is in this format — huge public corpus.

catalog.name: zvm-cp-console
catalog.product: IBM z/VM CP/CMS console log (HCP/DMS messages)
catalog.sample_line: HCPGIR450W CP entered; disabled wait PSW 00020000 80000000 00000000 00961210
catalog.detect_signature: Message ids ^HCP[A-Z]{3}[0-9]{3,4}[IWEAS] (CP) or ^DMS...[0-9]+[IWE] (CMS); console spool files prefixed with time hh:mm:ss and userid columns when logged via RECORDING/console spool
catalog.fields: time, vm userid, message id (module+number+severity), text (PSW, device, guest names)
catalog.notes: z/VM hosts Linux-on-Z fleets; guest Linux logs are already covered, this is the hypervisor side. HCPGIR450W is the classic 'guest died' line.
